title.zh: '''卷二百二十四上''' 列傳第一百四十九上 叛臣上

meta.sourceNote: Body created from Wikisource raw text because the ChineseNotes scrape produced a zero-byte file.

sentences.zh: ◎叛臣上仆固懷恩，鐵勒部人。

translations.literal: Rebellious Ministers, Part One: Pugu Huai’en was a man of the Tiele tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious Ministers, Part One: Pugu Huai’en came from the Tiele confederation.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，鐵勒九姓大首領率眾降，分置瀚海、燕然、金微、幽陵等九都督府，別為蕃州，以仆骨歌濫拔延為右武衛大將軍、金微都督，訛為仆固氏。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, the great chieftains of the nine Tiele clans led their people in submission. Nine protectorates were established at Hanhai, Yanshan, Jinwei, Youling, and elsewhere, with a separate Fan prefecture. Pugu Gelanbayan was made General of the Right Martial Guard and Jinwei Protector; the name was corrupted to the Pugu clan.
translations.idiomatic: In 646, the great chieftains of the nine Tiele tribes submitted with their followers. The court set up nine protectorates—among them Hanhai, Yanshan, Jinwei, and Youling—and a separate Fan prefecture. Pugu Gelanbayan was appointed General of the Right Martial Guard and Jinwei Protector; the clan name later came to be written as Pugu.

sentences.zh: 生乙李啜；

translations.literal: He fathered Yili Chuo;
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yili Chuo;

sentences.zh: 乙李啜生懷恩，世襲都督。

translations.literal: Yili Chuo fathered Huai'en, who inherited the protectorate in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yili Chuo fathered Huai'en, who inherited the protectorate as his family's hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 懷恩善戰鬥，曉識戎情，部分謹嚴。

translations.literal: Huai'en was skilled in battle, understood barbarian conditions, and was strict in dividing his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en excelled in combat, understood frontier warfare, and kept his units under tight discipline.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，從朔方節度使郭子儀討賊雲中，破之；

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he followed Shuofang Military Commissioner Guo Ziyi to attack the rebels at Yunzhong and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, he followed Shuofang commissioner Guo Ziyi against the rebels at Yunzhong and routed them;

sentences.zh: 敗薛忠義於背度山，殺七千騎，禽忠義子，下馬邑。

translations.literal: he defeated Xue Zhongyi at Beidu Mountain, killed seven thousand horsemen, captured Zhongyi's son, and took Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: he defeated Xue Zhongyi at Beidu Mountain, slew seven thousand cavalry, captured Zhongyi's son, and seized Mayi.

sentences.zh: 進會李光弼，戰常山、趙郡、沙河、嘉山，走史思明。

translations.literal: Advancing, he joined Li Guangbi and fought at Changshan, Zhao Commandery, Shahe, and Jiashan, driving off Shi Siming.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to join Li Guangbi and fought at Changshan, Zhao, Shahe, and Jiashan, putting Shi Siming to flight.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，與子儀赴靈武。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, he went with Ziyi to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, he accompanied Guo Ziyi to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 時同羅部落叛，祿山北掠朔方，子儀率懷恩迎擊。

translations.literal: At that time the Tongluo tribes rebelled, and Lushan raided north into Shuofang; Ziyi led Huai'en to meet the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongluo tribes had rebelled, and Lushan was raiding north into Shuofang; Guo Ziyi led Huai'en out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 懷恩子玢戰敗降虜，已而自拔歸，懷恩怒，叱斬之。

translations.literal: Huai'en's son Bin was defeated in battle and surrendered to the enemy; later he escaped and returned. Huai'en was enraged and ordered him beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's son Bin was defeated and captured, but later broke free and came back. Huai'en flew into a rage and had him executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 將士股栗，皆殊死戰，遂破其眾，收馬、橐它、器械甚眾。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers trembled in their legs; all fought to the death, and they finally broke the enemy host, capturing many horses, camels, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and men were terrified into fighting with abandon; they broke the enemy force and took vast numbers of horses, camels, and arms.

sentences.zh: 帝又詔與敦煌王承寀使回紇請師，回紇聽命。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered him, together with Prince of Dunhuang Cheng Cai, to go as envoy to the Uyghurs to request troops; the Uyghurs obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent him with Prince of Dunhuang Cheng Cai as envoy to the Uyghurs to request military aid, and the Uyghurs agreed.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，從子儀下馮翊、河東，走賊將崔乾祐，襲潼關，破之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, following Ziyi he descended on Fengyi and Hedong, drove off the rebel general Cui Qianyou, raided Tong Pass, and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In 757 he followed Guo Ziyi into Fengyi and Hedong, put the rebel general Cui Qianyou to flight, stormed Tong Pass, and carried the day.

sentences.zh: 賊將安守忠、李歸仁苦戰二日，王師敗績。

translations.literal: The rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren fought bitterly for two days, and the imperial army suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren fought fiercely for two days, and the imperial forces were defeated.

sentences.zh: 懷恩至渭水，無舟，抱馬鬛以逸，收散卒還河東。

translations.literal: Huai'en reached the Wei River with no boats; clutching his horse's mane he swam across, gathered scattered troops, and returned to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en reached the Wei with no boats available; he clutched his horse's mane and swam across, rallied scattered troops, and withdrew to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 子儀赴鳳翔，歸仁以勁兵邀戰三原，子儀使懷恩與王升、陳回光、渾釋之、李國貞五將軍伏白渠下，賊至遇伏，敗而走。

translations.literal: Ziyi went to Fengxiang; Guiren blocked him with crack troops at Sanyuan. Ziyi had Huai'en, together with the five generals Wang Sheng, Chen Huiguang, Hun Jiezhi, and Li Guozhen, lie in ambush below the White Canal. When the rebels arrived they met the ambush, were defeated, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi marched to Fengxiang; Li Guiren barred his way at Sanyuan with elite troops. Guo Ziyi sent Huai'en and four other generals—Wang Sheng, Chen Huiguang, Hun Jiezhi, and Li Guozhen—to lie in ambush along the White Canal. The rebels walked into the trap, were routed, and fled.

sentences.zh: 又戰清渠，不利，引還。

translations.literal: They fought again at Qing Canal without success and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again at Qing Canal without success and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 時回紇使葉護、帝得以四千騎濟師，南蠻、大食等兵亦踵至。

translations.literal: At that time the Uyghur envoy Yehu and the emperor were able to cross with four thousand cavalry as reinforcements; troops from the southern barbarians, Dashi, and elsewhere also arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur envoy Yehu and the emperor were then able to cross with four thousand cavalry as reinforcements, and troops from the southern tribes, the Arabs, and elsewhere followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔廣平王為元帥，使懷恩統回紇兵，從王戰香積寺北。

translations.literal: The emperor then appointed the Prince of Guangping as supreme commander and had Huai'en command the Uyghur troops, following the prince to fight north of Xiangji Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed the Prince of Guangping supreme commander and placed the Uyghur forces under Huai'en; they followed the prince into battle north of Xiangji Temple.

sentences.zh: 賊以一軍伏營左，懷恩馳掩之，馘斬無遺者，賊氣沮。

translations.literal: The rebels had one army lying in ambush to the left of the camp; Huai'en galloped to strike them, beheading every man without exception, and the rebels' morale collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had hidden a force to the left of the camp; Huai'en charged and wiped them out to the last man, shattering the enemy's morale.

sentences.zh: 既合戰，以回紇夾攻賊，戰酣，脫甲援矛直搗陣，殺十餘人，眾驚靡，亦會李嗣業鏖鬥尤力，賊大崩敗。

translations.literal: When battle was joined, the Uyghurs attacked the rebels from both flanks. In the heat of fighting Huai'en stripped off his armor, took up a spear, and drove straight into the enemy line, killing more than ten men; the host was stunned and scattered. Li Siye also fought with exceptional ferocity, and the rebels collapsed in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Once battle was joined, the Uyghurs hit the rebels from both flanks. In the thick of the fight Huai'en stripped off his armor, seized a spear, and charged straight into the enemy ranks, killing more than ten men and throwing their line into panic. Li Siye fought with equal fury, and the rebels broke completely.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，懷恩見王曰：「賊必棄城走，願假壯騎二百，縛安守忠、李歸仁等致麾下。」

translations.literal: As dusk fell, Huai'en saw the prince and said, "The rebels are sure to abandon the city and flee. I beg two hundred stalwart horsemen to bind An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, and the rest and deliver them to your command."
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Huai'en told the prince, "The rebels are sure to abandon the city and flee. Give me two hundred picked horsemen, and I will bind An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, and the rest and bring them before you."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「將軍戰疲，且休矣；

translations.literal: The prince said, "General, you are weary from battle; rest for now;
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied, "General, you are exhausted from battle; rest for now;

sentences.zh: 迨明，與將軍圖之。」

translations.literal: when dawn comes we shall plan with the general.
translations.idiomatic: at daybreak we will decide what to do together."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「守忠等皆天下驍賊，驟勝而敗，此天與我也，奈何縱之？

translations.literal: He replied, "Shouzhong and the rest are the fiercest rebels under heaven. To win suddenly and then lose—this is heaven's gift to us; how can we let them go?
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en answered, "Shouzhong and the others are the fiercest rebels in the realm. To win so suddenly and then let them slip away—this is heaven's gift; how can we release them?

sentences.zh: 使復得眾，必為我患，雖悔無逮。」

translations.literal: If they gather their forces again they will surely become a calamity for us; even regret will not reach them in time.
translations.idiomatic: If they rally their troops again they will surely become our ruin, and regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 王不從，固請，通夕四五反。

translations.literal: The prince would not agree; Huai'en pressed his request four or five times through the night.
translations.idiomatic: The prince refused; Huai'en pressed his case four or five times through the night.

sentences.zh: 遲明，諜者至，守忠等果遁去。

translations.literal: Near dawn scouts arrived: Shouzhong and the others had indeed fled.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn scouts reported that Shouzhong and the others had indeed escaped.

sentences.zh: 又從王破賊於新店。

translations.literal: He again followed the prince to defeat the rebels at Xindian.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the prince to defeat the rebels at Xindian.

sentences.zh: 以復兩京有殊功，詔加開府儀同三司、鴻臚卿，封豐國公，賜封二百戶。

translations.literal: For his outstanding merit in recovering the two capitals, he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies and made Minister of Ceremonial Reception; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Feng and granted two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his signal service in recovering the two capitals, he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and appointed Minister of Ceremonial Reception; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Feng with an income of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從郭子儀破安太清，下懷、衛二州，攻相州，戰愁思岡，常為先鋒，勇冠軍中。

translations.literal: Following Guo Ziyi he defeated An Taiqing, took Huai and Wei prefectures, attacked Xiangzhou, and fought at Chousi Ridge; he was often in the vanguard, and his courage was foremost in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Ziyi to defeat An Taiqing, captured Huai and Wei, attacked Xiangzhou, and fought at Chousi Ridge; he often led the van, and none in the army matched his courage.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，拜朔方行營節度使，進封大寧郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Field Army and advanced in rank to Prince of Daning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 759 he was appointed military commissioner of the Shuofang field army and advanced to Prince of Daning.

sentences.zh: 懷恩為人雄重寡言，應對舒緩，然剛決犯上，始居偏裨，意有不合，雖主將必折詬。

translations.literal: Huai'en as a man was imposing and sparing of speech, unhurried in reply, yet firm and defiant toward superiors. When he first held a subordinate command, if his views did not accord he would rebuke even the commanding general.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was a man of imposing presence who spoke little and answered slowly, yet he was stubborn and defiant toward his superiors. Even as a junior officer, if he disagreed he would rebuke his commander without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 其麾下皆蕃、漢勁卒，恃功多不法。

translations.literal: Those under his command were all crack barbarian and Han troops who, relying on their achievements, often acted outside the law.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were elite barbarian and Han fighters who, trusting in their battle honors, frequently broke the law.

sentences.zh: 子儀政寬，能優容之。

translations.literal: Ziyi's government was lenient, and he could indulge them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi's rule was lenient, and he indulged them.

sentences.zh: 及李光弼代子儀，懷恩仍為副。

translations.literal: When Li Guangbi replaced Ziyi, Huai'en remained as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangbi replaced Guo Ziyi, Huai'en continued as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 光弼守河陽，攻懷州，降安太清。

translations.literal: Guangbi held Heyang, attacked Huaizhou, and received the surrender of An Taiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi held Heyang, attacked Huaizhou, and accepted An Taiqing's surrender.

sentences.zh: 又子玚，亦善鬥，以儀同三司將兵，每深入多殺，賊憚其勇，號猛將。

translations.literal: His son Chang was also skilled in fighting; with the ceremonial rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness he led troops, often penetrating deep and killing many. The rebels feared his courage and called him a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang was likewise a formidable fighter; holding ceremonial rank as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, he led troops deep into enemy territory and killed heavily. The rebels feared his valor and called him a fierce general.

sentences.zh: 太清妻有色，玚劫致於幕，光弼命歸之，不聽，以卒環守。

translations.literal: Taiqing's wife was beautiful; Chang seized her and brought her to his tent. Guangbi ordered her returned; Chang would not obey and had soldiers surround and guard her.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing's wife was beautiful; Chang abducted her to his tent. Guangbi ordered her returned, but Chang refused and posted guards around her.

sentences.zh: 復馳騎趨之，射殺七人，奪妻還太清。

translations.literal: Guangbi again galloped toward them, shot and killed seven men, seized the wife, and returned her to Taiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi rode in again, shot seven men dead, took the woman back, and restored her to Taiqing.

sentences.zh: 懷恩怒曰：「公乃為賊殺官卒邪？」

translations.literal: Huai'en said angrily, "Sir, you would kill government soldiers for the sake of a rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en raged, "You would kill imperial soldiers for a rebel's sake?"

sentences.zh: 光弼持法嚴，少假貸。

translations.literal: Guangbi upheld the law strictly and granted little indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi enforced the law strictly and showed little forbearance.

sentences.zh: 初，會軍汜水，朔方將張用濟後至，斬纛下。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the army assembled at Sishui, the Shuofang general Zhang Yongji arrived late and was beheaded beneath the command banner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the army gathered at Sishui, the Shuofang general Zhang Yongji arrived late and was executed beneath the command banner.

sentences.zh: 懷恩心憚光弼，自用濟誅，常邑邑不樂。

translations.literal: Huai'en inwardly feared Guangbi; from Yongji's execution onward he was often depressed and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en inwardly feared Guangbi; after Yongji's execution he was often sullen and discontented.

sentences.zh: 及光弼與史思明戰邙山，不用令，以覆王師。

translations.literal: When Guangbi fought Shi Siming at Mount Mang, Huai'en did not follow orders and thereby brought disaster on the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi fought Shi Siming at Mount Mang, Huai'en disobeyed orders and helped bring defeat on the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 帝思其功，召入為工部尚書，寵以殊禮。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of his achievements, summoned him to court as Minister of Works and favored him with exceptional honors.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his past service, the emperor summoned him to court as Minister of Works and honored him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，拜隴右節度使，未行，改朔方行營節度，以副子儀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, Huai'en was appointed Military Commissioner of Longyou; before he departed the appointment was changed to Shuofang Field Army Commissioner, serving as Guo Ziyi's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Huai'en was appointed commissioner of Longyou; before he could take up the post he was reassigned as Shuofang field commissioner, serving under Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗以寧國公主下嫁毗伽闕可汗，又為少子請婚，故以懷恩女妻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Suzong had given Princess Ningguo in marriage to the Qaghan Bögü Qaghan, and the qaghan's younger son had also requested a marriage; therefore Huai'en's daughter was given to him as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Suzong had married Princess Ningguo to the Qaghan Bögü, and when the qaghan's younger son also sought a bride, Huai'en's daughter was given to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 少子立，號登裏可汗，而懷恩女為可敦。

translations.literal: The younger son succeeded and took the title Qaghan Dengli; Huai'en's daughter became the qatun.
translations.idiomatic: When the younger son succeeded as Qaghan Dengli, Huai'en's daughter became the qatun.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，帝召兵於回紇，而登裏可汗已為史朝義所誘，引眾十萬盜塞，關中大震。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying the emperor summoned troops from the Uyghurs, but Qaghan Dengli had already been enticed by Shi Chaoyi and led a hundred thousand men to raid the frontier; Guanzhong was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In 762 the emperor called for Uyghur troops, but Qaghan Dengli had already been won over by Shi Chaoyi and led a hundred thousand men to raid the passes; all of Guanzhong was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 帝遣殿中監藥子昂勞之，可汗因請見懷恩及其母，有詔報可。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Director Yao Zi'ang to comfort them; the qaghan thereupon asked to see Huai'en and his mother, and an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Director Yao Zi'ang to greet them; the qaghan then asked to see Huai'en and his mother, and the court assented.

sentences.zh: 懷恩避嫌不往，帝賜鐵券，手詔固遣，乃行。

translations.literal: Huai'en, wishing to avoid suspicion, did not go; the emperor granted him an iron certificate of mercy and personally wrote an edict firmly sending him, and only then did he go.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en stayed away to avoid suspicion; the emperor granted him an iron certificate of mercy and wrote a personal edict insisting he go, and only then did he set out.

sentences.zh: 與可汗會太原，可汗大悅，遂請和，助討朝義，即引兵屯陜州，待師期。

translations.literal: He met the qaghan at Taiyuan; the qaghan was greatly pleased, then requested peace, offered to help attack Chaoyi, and immediately led his troops to camp at Shazhou, awaiting the date for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He met the qaghan at Taiyuan; the qaghan was delighted, agreed to peace, offered to help fight Chaoyi, and encamped his army at Shazhou to await the campaign.

sentences.zh: 於是雍王以元帥為中軍，拜懷恩同中書門下平章事為之副，乃與左殺為先鋒。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Yong, as supreme commander, took the center army; Huai'en was appointed Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs as his deputy, and together with Zuo Sha he served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong served as supreme commander with the center army; Huai'en was made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs as his deputy and, with Zuo Sha, led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 時諸節度皆以兵會，次黃水，賊堅壁自固。

translations.literal: At that time the various military commissioners all gathered their troops; they halted at Huangshui while the rebels held their walls and entrenched themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The various commissioners converged with their armies and halted at Huangshui while the rebels held their fortifications.

sentences.zh: 懷恩陣西原，多張旗旝，使突騎與回紇稍南出繚賊左，舉旗為應，破賊壁，死者數萬。

translations.literal: Huai'en drew up his line on the western plain, displayed many banners and pennants, and sent shock cavalry with the Uyghurs to skirt slightly south and circle the rebels' left; raising their flags in signal they broke the rebel walls, and tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en formed his line on the western plain, raised many banners, and sent shock cavalry with the Uyghurs to swing south and envelop the rebels' left flank; at the signal of raised flags they broke the enemy fortifications, and tens of thousands were killed.

sentences.zh: 朝義擁精騎十萬來援，埋根決戰，短兵接，殺獲相當。

translations.literal: Chaoyi led a hundred thousand elite horsemen to the rescue; both sides fought to the root in decisive battle, closed in hand to hand, and kills and captures were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi brought a hundred thousand elite cavalry to relieve the siege; both sides fought a pitched battle at close quarters, and casualties were heavy on both sides.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩令射生五百攢矢註射，賊多死，而陣堅不可犯。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en ordered five hundred archers to concentrate their arrows in volleys; many rebels died, yet the formation held firm and could not be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en ordered five hundred archers to pour concentrated volleys into the enemy; many rebels fell, but their formation held and could not be broken.

sentences.zh: 馬璘怒，單騎援旗直進，奪兩盾，賊辟易，大軍乘以入，眾囂不止，朝義敗。

translations.literal: Ma Lin was enraged; alone on horseback he seized the standard and charged straight in, snatching two shields. The rebels gave way; the great army pressed in on the opening, the host roared without cease, and Chaoyi was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin, enraged, charged alone with the standard, seized two enemy shields, and threw their line into confusion; the main force poured through the gap with a roar, and Chaoyi was defeated.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬六千級，禽四千餘人，降者三萬。

translations.literal: Sixteen thousand heads were taken, more than four thousand captured alive, and thirty thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen thousand heads were taken, more than four thousand men captured, and thirty thousand surrendered.

sentences.zh: 轉戰石榴園、老子祠，賊再敗，自相奔蹂死，填尚書谷幾滿，朝義輕騎走。

translations.literal: Fighting shifted to Shiliu Garden and Laozi Shrine; the rebels were defeated again, trampled one another to death in flight until Shangshu Valley was nearly filled, and Chaoyi fled on light horse.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting moved to Shiliu Garden and Laozi Shrine; the rebels were beaten again and trampled one another to death in flight until Shangshu Valley was nearly choked with bodies; Chaoyi fled on a swift horse.

sentences.zh: 懷恩進收東都、河陽，封府庫，無所私。

translations.literal: Huai'en advanced to recover the Eastern Capital and Heyang, sealed the treasuries, and took nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en advanced to recover Luoyang and Heyang, sealed the treasuries, and took nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 釋賊所署許叔冀、王伷等，眾皆按堵。

translations.literal: He released Xu Shuji, Wang You, and others whom the rebels had appointed; the people all lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: He released Xu Shuji, Wang You, and others whom the rebels had appointed, and the populace settled peacefully.

sentences.zh: 留回紇屯河陽，使玚及北庭兵馬將高輔成以萬騎逐北，懷恩常壓賊而次。

translations.literal: He left the Uyghurs encamped at Heyang and sent Chang, together with Beiting Cavalry General Gao Fucheng, with ten thousand horsemen in pursuit north; Huai'en himself always pressed the rebels and followed in their wake.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Uyghurs encamped at Heyang and sent Chang with Beiting cavalry general Gao Fucheng and ten thousand horsemen in pursuit; Huai'en himself kept pressing the enemy from behind.

sentences.zh: 至鄭州，再戰再捷，賊帥張獻誠以汴州降，下滑州。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhengzhou, they fought twice and won twice; the rebel commander Zhang Xiancheng surrendered Bianzhou, and they descended on Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengzhou they won two battles in succession; rebel commander Zhang Xiancheng surrendered Bianzhou, and they took Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 朝義至衛州，與其黨田承嗣、李進超、李達廬合，有眾四萬，據河以戰。

translations.literal: Chaoyi reached Weizhou and joined his partisans Tian Chengsi, Li Jinchao, and Li Dalu; they had forty thousand men and held the river to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi reached Weizhou and joined Tian Chengsi, Li Jinchao, and Li Dalu; with forty thousand men they held the river line.

sentences.zh: 玚濟師登岸薄之，賊黨奔潰。

translations.literal: Chang crossed the army over the river, landed, and pressed them closely; the rebel partisans broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ferried the army across, landed, and closed on them; the rebel forces broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 進次昌樂，朝義逸，偽帥達廬降，薛高、李寶臣舉相、衛、深、定等九州獻款。

translations.literal: Advancing they halted at Changle; Chaoyi escaped, the false commander Dalu surrendered, and Xue Gao and Li Baochen offered the submission of nine prefectures including Xiang, Wei, Shen, and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to Changle; Chaoyi escaped, the rebel commander Dalu surrendered, and Xue Gao and Li Baochen offered the submission of nine prefectures, including Xiang, Wei, Shen, and Ding.

sentences.zh: 朝義至貝州，得其黨薛忠義，引眾三萬拒玚於臨清。

translations.literal: Chaoyi reached Beizhou, joined his partisan Xue Zhongyi, and led thirty thousand men to block Chang at Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi reached Beizhou, rallied his partisan Xue Zhongyi, and with thirty thousand men barred Chang's way at Linqing.

sentences.zh: 賊氣盛，玚勒兵挫其鋒，令高彥崇、渾日進、李光逸設三伏以待，賊半度，伏發，擊之，朝義走。

translations.literal: The rebels' morale was high; Chang arrayed his troops to blunt their edge and ordered Gao Yanchong, Hun Rijin, and Li Guangyi to set three ambushes in wait. When the rebels were half across, the ambushes sprang; they struck, and Chaoyi fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were in high spirits; Chang drew up his line to blunt their charge and had Gao Yanchong, Hun Rijin, and Li Guangyi lay three ambushes. When the enemy was half across, the ambushes struck; Chaoyi fled.

sentences.zh: 會回紇以輕騎至，玚卷甲馳之，大戰下博，賊背水陣，師奔擊，賊大崩，積屍蔽流而下。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs arrived with light cavalry; Chang wrapped his armor and galloped after them. At Xiabo a great battle was fought; the rebels formed with their backs to the water. The army charged; the rebels collapsed in great defeat, and piled corpses blocked the current downstream.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs arrived with light cavalry; Chang pressed the pursuit in full armor. At Xiabo a great battle was fought with the rebels trapped against the water; the imperial forces charged, the enemy collapsed, and corpses choked the river downstream.

sentences.zh: 朝義退守莫州。

translations.literal: Chaoyi withdrew to hold Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi withdrew to defend Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 於是都知兵馬使薛兼訓、郝廷玉、兗鄆節度使辛雲京會師城下，朝義與田承嗣數挑戰，不勝，臨陣斬偽黨敬榮。

translations.literal: Thereupon Army Inspector Xue Jianxun, Hao Tingyu, and Yan-Yun Military Commissioner Xin Yunjing united their armies below the city walls. Chaoyi and Tian Chengsi challenged battle several times without success; in the field he beheaded the false partisan Jing Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Army inspector Xue Jianxun, Hao Tingyu, and Yan-Yun commissioner Xin Yunjing then united their forces before the city. Chaoyi and Tian Chengsi offered battle repeatedly without success; Chaoyi executed the rebel partisan Jing Rong before the ranks.

sentences.zh: 朝義懼，率殘眾奔幽州。

translations.literal: Chaoyi was afraid and led his remnant host in flight to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chaoyi fled to Youzhou with his remaining troops.

sentences.zh: 王追躡，朝義走平州，自經死，河北平。

translations.literal: The prince pursued; Chaoyi fled to Pingzhou and hanged himself; Hebei was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The prince pursued; Chaoyi fled to Pingzhou and hanged himself, and Hebei was pacified.

sentences.zh: 懷恩與諸將皆罷兵，以功遷尚書左僕射兼中書令、河北副元帥、朔方節度使，加封戶四百。

translations.literal: Huai'en and the various generals all stood down their armies. For his achievements he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Director, Hebei Deputy Supreme Commander, and Shuofang Military Commissioner, with four hundred additional enfeoffed households.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en and the other generals stood down their armies. For his service he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Director, deputy supreme commander of Hebei, and Shuofang commissioner, with four hundred additional enfeoffed households.

sentences.zh: 初，帝有詔但取朝義，其它一切赦之。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had issued an edict to take only Chaoyi and pardon all others completely.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had earlier decreed that only Chaoyi was to be taken and all others were to be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 故薛嵩、張忠誌、李懷仙、田承嗣見懷恩皆叩頭，願效力行伍。

translations.literal: Therefore Xue Song, Zhang Zhongzhi, Li Huaixian, and Tian Chengsi, on seeing Huai'en, all knocked their heads and wished to serve in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: So when Xue Song, Zhang Zhongzhi, Li Huaixian, and Tian Chengsi met Huai'en, they all kowtowed and offered to serve under his command.

sentences.zh: 懷恩自見功高，且賊平則勢輕，不能固寵，乃悉請裂河北分大鎮以授之，潛結其心以為助，嵩等卒據以為患雲。

translations.literal: Huai'en himself saw that his achievements were high yet that once the rebels were pacified his position would grow light and he could not secure lasting favor; he therefore requested in full that Hebei be carved up and great commands given to them, secretly binding their hearts as helpers. Song and the others ultimately held those territories and became a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en saw that his merits were great but that once the rebels were crushed his influence would wane and he could not hold the court's favor; he therefore asked that Hebei be divided into great military commands and given to them, secretly winning their loyalty as allies. Song and the others ultimately held those territories and became a lasting scourge.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加太子少師，增戶五百，第一區，與一子五品官。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with five hundred additional households, a first-rank residence, and a fifth-rank office for one son.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granted five hundred additional households, a first-rank residence, and a fifth-rank office for one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 詔護回紇歸國，道太原，辛雲京內忌懷恩，又以其與回紇親，疑可汗見襲，閉關不敢犒軍。

translations.literal: He was ordered to escort the Uyghurs home; passing Taiyuan, Xin Yunjing inwardly resented Huai'en, and because of his kinship with the Uyghurs feared the qaghan might be attacked; he closed the passes and dared not provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to escort the Uyghurs home. Passing Taiyuan, Xin Yunjing bore him a private grudge and, because of Huai'en's ties to the Uyghurs, feared an attack on the qaghan; he closed the passes and refused to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 懷恩既父子新立功，舉河朔若拾遺，名出諸將遠甚，而為雲京所拒，大怒，表上其狀。

translations.literal: Huai'en, father and sons having newly achieved merit, held all of Heshuo as if picking up lost objects; his fame far exceeded the other generals, yet he was rejected by Yunjing. Enraged, he memorialized the throne reporting the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en and his sons had just won fresh honors and held sway over Heshuo as if it were theirs for the taking; his renown far outstripped the other generals, yet Yunjing had snubbed him. Furious, he memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 頓軍汾州，使裨將李光逸以兵守祁，李懷光據晉州，張如嶽據沁州，高暉等十餘人自從。

translations.literal: He halted his army at Fenzhou, had subordinate general Li Guangyi hold Qi with troops, Li Huaiguang occupy Jinzhou, Zhang Ruyue occupy Qinzhou, and more than ten others including Gao Hui follow of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: He halted his army at Fenzhou, posted subordinate Li Guangyi to hold Qi, Li Huaiguang to occupy Jinzhou, Zhang Ruyue to hold Qinzhou, and more than ten others including Gao Hui followed him of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 會監軍駱奉先自雲京所歸，雲京已厚結其歡，因言懷恩與可汗約反狀明白。

translations.literal: It happened that Army Supervisor Luo Fengxian returned from Yunjing's camp; Yunjing had already won his favor deeply, and through him stated clearly that Huai'en and the qaghan had agreed to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Luo Fengxian returned from Yunjing's camp; Yunjing had already won him over and reported that Huai'en and the qaghan had clearly agreed to rebel.

sentences.zh: 奉先過懷恩，升堂拜母，母讓曰：「若與我兒約兄弟，今何自親雲京？

translations.literal: Fengxian passed through Huai'en's camp, entered the hall, and bowed to his mother. The mother reproved him, saying, "If you pledged brotherhood with my son, why do you now attach yourself to Yunjing?
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian called on Huai'en and bowed to his mother in the hall. She rebuked him: "If you pledged brotherhood with my son, why are you now cozy with Yunjing?

sentences.zh: 然前事勿論，自今宜如初。」

translations.literal: Yet let past matters go unmentioned; from now on you should be as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Let the past be past; from now on behave as you did at first."

sentences.zh: 酒酣，懷恩舞，奉先厚納以幣。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep, Huai'en danced; Fengxian generously accepted gifts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed, Huai'en danced; Fengxian accepted lavish gifts of silk.

sentences.zh: 懷恩未及酬，奉先亟辭去，懷恩即遣左右匿其馬。

translations.literal: Before Huai'en could repay him, Fengxian hurried to take his leave; Huai'en immediately sent attendants to hide his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Before Huai'en could return the favor, Fengxian hurried to leave; Huai'en at once had his attendants hide Fengxian's horse.

sentences.zh: 奉先疑圖己，乘夜遁歸。

translations.literal: Fengxian suspected a plot against himself and fled home by night.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian suspected a trap and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 懷恩驚，追與其馬。

translations.literal: Huai'en was alarmed and pursued him to return his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Huai'en pursued him to return his horse.

sentences.zh: 奉先還，具奏懷恩反狀，懷恩亦請誅雲京、奉先，詔兩解之。

translations.literal: Fengxian returned and fully reported Huai'en's rebellious conduct; Huai'en also requested the execution of Yunjing and Fengxian. An edict reconciled both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian returned and reported Huai'en's treason in full; Huai'en in turn asked that Yunjing and Fengxian be executed. An edict ordered both sides to stand down.

sentences.zh: 懷恩之過潞，李抱玉贈以幣馬，懷恩答之。

translations.literal: When Huai'en passed through Lu, Li Baoyu presented him with silk and horses; Huai'en reciprocated.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Lu, Huai'en received gifts of silk and horses from Li Baoyu and returned the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 俄抱玉表懷恩私有所結。

translations.literal: Before long Baoyu memorialized that Huai'en had private dealings with others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Baoyu memorialized that Huai'en was secretly building alliances.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，進拜太保，與一子三品、一子四品官，增封戶五百。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde he was advanced to Grand Preceptor, with a third-rank office for one son and a fourth-rank office for another, and five hundred additional enfeoffed households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangde era he was promoted to Grand Preceptor, granted a third-rank office for one son and a fourth-rank office for another, and given five hundred additional enfeoffed households.

sentences.zh: 玚與一子五品官，封戶百。

translations.literal: Chang received a fifth-rank office for one son and a hundred enfeoffed households.
translations.idiomatic: Chang received a fifth-rank office for one of his sons and a hundred enfeoffed households.

sentences.zh: 仍賜鐵券，以名藏太廟，畫象淩煙閣。

translations.literal: He was also granted an iron certificate of mercy; his name was placed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and his portrait was painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted an iron certificate of mercy; his name was entered in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and his portrait was hung in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 又以玚檢校兵部尚書、朔方行營節度使。

translations.literal: Chang was also made Acting Minister of War and Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Field Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was also made acting Minister of War and commissioner of the Shuofang field army.

sentences.zh: 然懷恩怏怏，又性強固，不肯為讒毀屈，無以自解，乃上書陳情曰：「臣世本夷人，少蒙上皇驅策。

translations.literal: Yet Huai'en was resentful; moreover his nature was stubborn and firm, and he would not bow to slander. Unable to clear himself, he submitted a memorial stating his case: "Your servant's family has been barbarian for generations; in youth I received the Former Emperor's driving and deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huai'en was bitter at heart; stubborn by nature, he refused to yield to slander and could find no way to clear his name. He submitted a memorial pleading his case: "Your servant comes from a barbarian line; in youth I served under the Former Emperor.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，臣以偏裨決死靜難，杖天威神，克滅強胡。

translations.literal: In Lushan's rebellion your servant, as a subordinate officer, resolved on death to quell the calamity, relying on heaven's awesome spirit, and destroyed the mighty barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Lushan's rebellion I, a junior officer, pledged my life to quell the uprising and, by heaven's majesty, crushed the rebel hosts.

sentences.zh: 思明繼逆，先帝委臣以兵，誓雪國讎，攻城野戰，身先士卒，兄弟死於陣，子姓沒於軍，九族之內，十不一在，而存者創痍滿身。

translations.literal: Siming succeeded to the rebellion; the Former Emperor entrusted your servant with troops, swearing to wash away the state's enmity. In storming cities and fighting in the field I led from the front; brothers died in battle, sons and clansmen perished in the army. Of nine generations, scarcely one in ten remained, and those who lived were covered with wounds.
translations.idiomatic: When Siming carried on the rebellion, the Former Emperor gave me command of troops and charged me to avenge the realm. I stormed cities and fought in the open field, always at the head of the ranks. Brothers fell in battle; sons and kinsmen died in the army. Of my nine generations, fewer than one in ten survived, and the living were scarred from head to foot.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍潛時，親總師旅，臣事麾下，悉臣之愚。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was still in concealment, you personally commanded the armies; your servant served under your banner and gave all my feeble powers.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was still heir in waiting, you personally led the armies. I served under your command and gave you everything I had, however slight.

sentences.zh: 是時數以微功，已為李輔國讒間，幾至毀家。

translations.literal: At that time, though I won only minor merit, I was already slandered and set apart by Li Fuguo, and came near to the ruin of my house.
translations.idiomatic: Even then, for trifling victories, Li Fuguo slandered me and nearly destroyed my family.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，知臣負謗，遂開獨見之明，杜眾多之口，拔臣於汧、隴，任臣以朔方，遊魂反幹，朽骨再肉。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty took the throne, knowing that your servant bore calumny, you opened your solitary insight, shut the mouths of the multitude, drew me from Qian and Long, and entrusted me with Shuofang—a wandering soul returned to the trunk, rotten bones clothed again in flesh.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, knowing I had been wronged, you saw clearly for yourself, silenced my accusers, pulled me out of Qian and Long, and gave me Shuofang—as though a lost soul had returned to its body and dead bone had been made flesh again.

sentences.zh: 前日回紇入塞，士人未曉，京輔震驚，陛下詔臣至太原勞問，許臣一切處置，因得與可汗計議，分道用兵，收復東都，掃蕩燕、薊。

translations.literal: Recently, when the Uyghurs entered the passes, the gentry did not understand and the capital region was shaken. Your Majesty ordered your servant to Taiyuan to comfort and inquire, granting me full discretion. Thus I could consult with the khan, divide our forces, recover the Eastern Capital, and sweep Yan and Ji clean.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs crossed the border lately, the court did not understand their intent and the capital was thrown into alarm. Your Majesty sent me to Taiyuan to receive them, with full authority to act as I saw fit. I was able to consult with the khan, divide our forces, retake the Eastern Capital, and drive the rebels from Yan and Ji.

sentences.zh: 時可汗在洛，為魚朝恩猜阻，已失歡心。

translations.literal: At that time the khan was at Luoyang; Yu Chao'en's suspicions and obstruction had already cost us his goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: The khan was then at Luoyang, but Yu Chao'en's suspicion and interference had already turned his goodwill sour.

sentences.zh: 及臣護送回紇，雲京閉城不出，潛使攘竊，蕃夷怨怒，彌縫百端，乃得返國。

translations.literal: When your servant escorted the Uyghurs back, Yunjing shut his city and would not come out, secretly sending men to snatch and steal. The barbarians were enraged; I patched things over by every means before they could return to their country.
translations.idiomatic: When I escorted the Uyghurs home, Yunjing shut his gates and refused to receive them, while secretly sending men to plunder their baggage. The tribes were furious; only after I smoothed matters every way I could were they persuaded to return home.

sentences.zh: 臣還汾州，休息士馬雲京亦不使一介相聞，畏臣劾奏，故構為飛謗，以起異端。

translations.literal: When your servant returned to Fenzhou to rest troops and horses, Yunjing would not send even a single messenger; fearing my impeachment, he fabricated flying slander to raise discord.
translations.idiomatic: When I returned to Fenzhou to rest my men and horses, Yunjing would not so much as send a messenger. Fearful that I would impeach him, he spread wild rumors to stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 陛下不垂明察，欲使忠直之臣，陷讒邪之黨，臣所為拊心泣血者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not bestow clear scrutiny, and would have a loyal and upright minister fall into the clutches of slanderous villains—this is what makes your servant beat his breast and weep blood.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty will not look into this clearly and would let a loyal minister be destroyed by slanderers—that is why I beat my breast and weep blood.

sentences.zh: 然臣之罪有六，無所逃死：往者同羅背逆，以騷河曲，兵連不解，臣不顧老母，從先帝於行在，募兵討賊，同羅奔殄，是臣不忠於國，罪一也；

translations.literal: Yet your servant has six crimes for which there is no escaping death: formerly, when the Tongluo turned traitor and troubled the bend of the Yellow River and fighting would not cease, your servant, heedless of his aged mother, followed the Former Emperor to the mobile court, raised troops to punish the rebels, and the Tongluo were driven to destruction—this is your servant's disloyalty to the state, crime one;
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have six crimes, and death cannot be escaped. When the Tongluo rebelled and ravaged the Yellow River bend and the war would not end, I left my aged mother and followed the Former Emperor to the field court, raised troops against the rebels, and destroyed the Tongluo—that was my first crime of disloyalty to the state;

sentences.zh: 斬子玢以令士眾，舍天性之愛，是臣不忠於國，罪二也；

translations.literal: I beheaded my son Bin to command the host and abandoned the love of nature—this is your servant's disloyalty to the state, crime two;
translations.idiomatic: I executed my son Bin to enforce discipline and cast aside a father's love—that was my second crime of disloyalty;

sentences.zh: 二女遠嫁，為國和親，合從殄滅，是臣不忠於國，罪三也；

translations.literal: Two daughters were married far away for the state's marriage alliances, and the confederation was extinguished—this is your servant's disloyalty to the state, crime three;
translations.idiomatic: I sent two daughters far away in marriage alliances for the state and broke up enemy coalitions—that was my third crime;

sentences.zh: 又與子玚躬履行陣，誌寧邦家，是臣不忠於國，罪四也；

translations.literal: Again, with my son Chang I personally walked the battle lines, resolved to secure the realm and house—this is your servant's disloyalty to the state, crime four;
translations.idiomatic: I marched into battle with my son Chang, determined to secure the realm—that was my fourth crime;

sentences.zh: 河北新附，諸鎮皆握強兵，臣之撫綏，反側時定，是臣不忠於國，罪五也；

translations.literal: When Hebei had newly submitted and every garrison held strong troops, your servant's pacification and comfort settled those who turned this way and that—this is your servant's disloyalty to the state, crime five;
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei had just submitted and every commandery held powerful armies, I pacified them and kept restless factions quiet—that was my fifth crime;

sentences.zh: 協和回紇，戡定中原，二陵復土，使陛下勤孝兩全，是臣不忠於國，罪六也。」

translations.literal: I harmonized with the Uyghurs, settled the central plains, restored the two imperial tombs to their soil, and enabled Your Majesty to fulfill both diligence and filial piety—this is your servant's disloyalty to the state, crime six."
translations.idiomatic: I worked with the Uyghurs, pacified the central plains, restored the imperial tombs, and let Your Majesty fulfill both duty to the state and filial devotion—that was my sixth crime of disloyalty."

sentences.zh: 又言：「來瑱之誅，不暴其罪，天下為疑。

translations.literal: He also said: "In Lai Mei's execution his crimes were not made public, and the realm is in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "When Lai Mei was executed, his crimes were never made public, and the whole realm is left in doubt.

sentences.zh: 四方奏請，陛下皆云與驃騎議之，可否不出宰相。」

translations.literal: For memorials from the four quarters Your Majesty always says you will discuss them with the Champion Cavalry General; approval or rejection does not come from the chief ministers."
translations.idiomatic: For every petition from the provinces Your Majesty says you will consult the Champion Cavalry General alone; nothing is decided through the chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 詞言慢很，帝一不為慊，且欲其悔過，故推心待之。

translations.literal: His words were arrogant and harsh; the emperor was not pleased in the least, yet wished him to repent, and therefore treated him with open heart.
translations.idiomatic: The tone was arrogant and defiant. The emperor was deeply displeased, yet still hoped Huai'en would repent, and so continued to treat him with apparent trust.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相裴遵慶臨諭詔旨，因察其去就。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the chief minister Pei Zunqing to go in person to announce the imperial will and thereby observe whether he would stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chief Minister Pei Zunqing to deliver the imperial message in person and gauge whether Huai'en would submit or rebel.

sentences.zh: 遵慶至，懷恩抱其足，泣且訴。

translations.literal: When Zunqing arrived, Huai'en embraced his feet, weeping as he pleaded his case.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunqing arrived, Huai'en seized his feet and wept as he poured out his grievances.

sentences.zh: 遵慶道帝所以不疑，即勸入朝，懷恩許諾。

translations.literal: Zunqing explained why the emperor did not doubt him and at once urged him to enter court; Huai'en promised he would.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing explained why the emperor still trusted him and urged him to come to court; Huai'en agreed.

sentences.zh: 副將範誌誠諫，以為「嫌隙成矣，奈何入不測之朝，獨不見來瑱、李光弼乎？

translations.literal: His deputy Fan Zhicheng remonstrated, saying, "The rift is already made—how can you enter a court whose outcome cannot be foreseen? Have you alone not seen Lai Mei and Li Guangbi?
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Fan Zhicheng warned him: "The breach is already complete—why enter a court you cannot trust? Have you forgotten Lai Mei and Li Guangbi?

sentences.zh: 二臣功高不賞，瑱已及誅。」

translations.literal: Those two ministers' merit was too high to be rewarded; Mei has already met execution."
translations.idiomatic: Both men were too meritorious to be rewarded; Mei has already been put to death."

sentences.zh: 懷恩乃止。

translations.literal: Huai'en then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en held back.

sentences.zh: 欲使一子入宿衛，誌誠固止。

translations.literal: He wished to send one son into palace guard service, but Zhicheng firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to send a son to serve in the palace guard, but Zhicheng firmly refused to allow it.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫王翊使回紇還，懷恩慮泄其交通狀，因留不遣。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Wang Yi, returning from an embassy to the Uyghurs, was detained and not sent on because Huai'en feared he would reveal their dealings.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Yi was returning from an embassy to the Uyghurs; fearing he would expose their secret dealings, Huai'en detained him and would not let him proceed.

sentences.zh: 即使玚攻雲京，雲京敗，進攻榆次。

translations.literal: He then sent Chang to attack Yunjing; Yunjing was defeated, and they advanced to attack Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chang to attack Yunjing. Yunjing was defeated, and the army pushed on to Yuci.

sentences.zh: 初，帝幸陜，顏真卿請奉詔召懷恩。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor went to Shaan, Yan Zhenqing asked to be entrusted with an edict summoning Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor withdrew to Shaan, Yan Zhenqing volunteered to carry an edict summoning Huai'en to court.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝使往，辭曰：「臣往請行，時也，今無及矣！」

translations.literal: At this time the emperor sent him; he declined, saying, "When your servant asked to go before, the time was right; now it is too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor sent him again. He declined: "When I asked to go before, the moment was right. Now it is too late!"

sentences.zh: 帝問故，對曰：「頃陛下避狄於陜，臣見懷恩，責以《春秋》義，不奔問官守，故懷恩來朝，以助討賊，則其辭順。

translations.literal: The emperor asked why. He replied: "When Your Majesty lately fled the barbarians at Shaan, your servant saw Huai'en and reproached him with the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals for not rushing to inquire after his official post. Therefore Huai'en came to court to help punish the rebels, and his words were compliant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. He answered: "When Your Majesty withdrew to Shaan before, I confronted Huai'en with the Spring and Autumn principle that a minister must not abandon his post. He came to court then to help suppress the rebels, and his words were proper.

sentences.zh: 今陛下即宮京邑，懷恩進不勤王，退不釋眾，其辭曲，必不來矣！」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has taken up residence in the capital region; Huai'en, advancing, does not relieve the throne, and retreating, does not release his troops—his words will be evasive, and he will certainly not come!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty is back in the capital, Huai'en neither marches to save the throne nor disbands his army. His excuses will be twisted, and he will not come."

sentences.zh: 「然則奈何？」

translations.literal: "Then what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: "Then what should be done?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「今言懷恩反者，獨辛雲京、李抱玉、駱奉先、魚朝恩四人耳，自餘盛言其枉。

translations.literal: He said: "Those who now say Huai'en has rebelled are only Xin Yunjing, Li Baoyu, Luo Fengxian, and Yu Chao'en—the rest loudly proclaim his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Only Xin Yunjing, Li Baoyu, Luo Fengxian, and Yu Chao'en accuse Huai'en of rebellion. Everyone else insists he has been wronged.

sentences.zh: 然懷恩將士，皆郭子儀舊部曲，陛下若以子儀代之，喻以逆順，必相率而歸。」

translations.literal: Yet Huai'en's officers and soldiers are all Guo Ziyi's former subordinates. If Your Majesty replaces him with Ziyi and instructs them in what is rebellious and what is loyal, they will surely follow one another back."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's troops are all old followers of Guo Ziyi. If Your Majesty sends Ziyi in his place and teaches them loyalty from rebellion, they will come over in a body."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 子儀至河中，玚攻榆次，未拔，追兵於祁，責其緩，鞭之，眾怒。

translations.literal: When Ziyi reached Hezhong, Chang was attacking Yuci but had not taken it. Pursuing troops caught up at Qi; he blamed their slowness and flogged them, and the host was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi reached Hezhong while Chang was still besieging Yuci without success. Reinforcements caught up at Qi; Chang blamed them for delay and had them flogged, and the troops erupted in fury.

sentences.zh: 是夕，偏將焦暉、白玉等斬其首，獻闕下。

translations.literal: That night the deputy generals Jiao Hui, Bai Yu, and others cut off his head and presented it at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: That night deputy commanders Jiao Hui, Bai Yu, and others beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 懷恩聞，以告母。

translations.literal: When Huai'en heard, he told his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en heard the news, he told his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「我戒汝勿反，國家酬汝不淺，今眾變，禍且及我，奈何？」

translations.literal: His mother said, "I warned you not to rebel; the state has rewarded you generously. Now the troops have turned—disaster will reach even me. What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "I warned you not to rebel. The state has rewarded you richly. Now the army has turned against you, and even I will be caught in the ruin. What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 懷恩再拜出，母提刀逐之曰：「吾為國殺此賊，取其心以謝軍中。」

translations.literal: Huai'en bowed twice and went out; his mother seized a knife and pursued him, saying, "I will kill this traitor for the state and take his heart to appease the army."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en bowed and withdrew. His mother seized a knife and chased him, crying, "I will kill this traitor for the state and cut out his heart to satisfy the troops."

sentences.zh: 懷恩走，乃與部曲三百北度河，走靈武，稍稍引亡命，軍復振。

translations.literal: Huai'en fled. He then crossed the river north with three hundred followers, made for Lingwu, and little by little gathered fugitives until the army rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en fled. With three hundred followers he crossed the river north to Lingwu, gradually gathering fugitives until his force rallied again.

sentences.zh: 帝念舊勛，不加罪，詔輦其母歸京師，厚恤之，以壽終。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of old merit, imposed no punishment and ordered his mother conveyed by imperial carriage back to the capital, richly provided for until she died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Huai'en's past service, the emperor imposed no punishment on the family. He had the mother brought to the capital in an imperial carriage, gave her generous support, and she lived out her years in comfort.

sentences.zh: 又下詔拜懷恩太保兼中書令、大寧郡王，罷餘官。

translations.literal: Another edict appointed Huai'en Grand Preceptor and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Daning Commandery, and removed his other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict made Huai'en Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Daning, and stripped him of his other posts.

sentences.zh: 懷恩固惡不能改，遂誘吐蕃十萬入塞，豐州守將戰死。

translations.literal: Huai'en's stubborn wickedness could not be changed; he then induced a hundred thousand Tibetans to enter the passes, and the defending general of Fengzhou died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's nature would not change. He lured a hundred thousand Tibetans across the border, and the Fengzhou garrison commander was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 進掠涇、邠，祭來瑱墓。

translations.literal: Advancing, they raided Jing and Bin; he sacrificed at Lai Mei's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on to raid Jing and Bin, and Huai'en offered sacrifice at Lai Mei's tomb.

sentences.zh: 度涇水，邠寧節度使白孝德禦之，覆其陣，懷恩泣曰：「曩皆為我子，反為人致死於我。」

translations.literal: Crossing the Jing River, the Binqing Military Commissioner Bai Xiaode met them, overthrew their formation, and Huai'en wept, saying, "They were all once my sons, yet now they die for others against me."
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Jing River, Binqing commissioner Bai Xiaode met them and routed their line. Huai'en wept: "They were all once my men, and now they die fighting me for someone else."

sentences.zh: 入侵奉天，子儀拒退之。

translations.literal: They invaded Fengtian; Ziyi repelled and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: They invaded Fengtian, but Guo Ziyi beat them back.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，帝集天下兵防秋。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai the emperor gathered troops from across the realm for autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai the emperor mobilized armies from across the empire for the autumn defense.

sentences.zh: 懷恩誘合諸蕃號二十萬入寇，吐蕃自北道逼醴泉，搖奉天；

translations.literal: Huai'en induced the various barbarians to unite, claiming two hundred thousand for the invasion. The Tibetans by the northern route pressed Liquan and threatened Fengtian;
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en rallied the frontier peoples in a force said to number two hundred thousand. The Tibetans took the northern route toward Liquan and menaced Fengtian;

sentences.zh: 任敷、鄭廷、郝德自東道寇奉先，以窺同州；

translations.literal: Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, and Hao De by the eastern route raided Fengxian to spy out Tongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, and Hao De struck along the eastern route against Fengxian, probing toward Tongzhou;

sentences.zh: 羌、渾、奴剌自西道略盩厔，趣鳳翔。

translations.literal: the Qiang, Hun, and Nula by the western route plundered Zhouzhi and pressed toward Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: the Qiang, Hun, and Nula swept along the western route through Zhouzhi toward Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 京師震駭。

translations.literal: The capital was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 詔子儀屯涇陽，渾日進、白元光屯奉天，李光進屯雲陽，馬璘、郝廷玉屯便橋，董秦屯東渭橋，駱奉先、李日越屯盩厔，李抱玉屯鳳翔，周智光屯同州，杜冕屯坊州，帝御六軍屯苑中，下詔親征。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ziyi to encamp at Jingyang; Hun Rijin and Bai Yuanguang at Fengtian; Li Guangjin at Yunyang; Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Bianqiao; Dong Qin at the Eastern Wei Bridge; Luo Fengxian and Li Yueyue at Zhouzhi; Li Baoyu at Fengxiang; Zhou Zhiguang at Tongzhou; Du Mian at Fangzhou; the emperor himself led the Six Armies encamped in the park and issued an edict for a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was ordered to Jingyang; Hun Rijin and Bai Yuanguang to Fengtian; Li Guangjin to Yunyang; Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu to Bianqiao; Dong Qin to the Eastern Wei Bridge; Luo Fengxian and Li Yueyue to Zhouzhi; Li Baoyu to Fengxiang; Zhou Zhiguang to Tongzhou; Du Mian to Fangzhou. The emperor led the Six Armies into camp within the imperial park and proclaimed that he would take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 懷恩至鳴沙，病甚，還死靈武，部曲焚其屍以葬。

translations.literal: Huai'en reached Mingsha, grew gravely ill, returned, and died at Lingwu; his followers burned his corpse for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en reached Mingsha, fell gravely ill, turned back, and died at Lingwu. His followers burned his body for burial.

sentences.zh: 部將張韶、徐璜玉不能定其軍，皆前死。

translations.literal: The commanders Zhang Shao and Xu Huangyu could not steady the army and both died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders Zhang Shao and Xu Huangyu could not hold the army together and had already died.

sentences.zh: 範誌誠統眾寇涇陽。

translations.literal: Fan Zhicheng led the host to raid Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhicheng took command and attacked Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 時諸屯堅壁，大雨，溪垘流潰，賊不得進。

translations.literal: At that time the various encampments held fast behind walls; heavy rain burst streams and dikes, and the rebels could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial camps held behind their walls. Heavy rain burst the streams and dikes, and the rebels could not advance.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃既持久，又與回紇爭長，更相疑，莫適先進，因焚廬舍，驅男女數萬去。

translations.literal: The Tibetans, having dragged on long, also vied with the Uyghurs for precedence; they grew mutually suspicious and none would advance first, so they burned dwellings and drove off tens of thousands of men and women.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans had been at it too long and were now quarreling with the Uyghurs over precedence. Mutual suspicion kept each side from advancing. They burned their camps and drove off tens of thousands of captives as they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 周智光邀戰澄城，破之，收馬牛軍資萬計。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhiguang intercepted battle at Chengcheng, defeated them, and seized tens of thousands in horses, cattle, and military stores.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhiguang intercepted them at Chengcheng, routed them, and seized vast numbers of horses, cattle, and military supplies.

sentences.zh: 回紇乃詣子儀降，請擊吐蕃自效。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs then came to Ziyi to surrender and asked to strike the Tibetans to prove their merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs then came to Guo Ziyi to submit and offered to attack the Tibetans in proof of their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 子儀分兵隨之，破其眾於涇州。

translations.literal: Ziyi divided troops to follow them and broke their host at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent troops with them and routed the Tibetan force at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 任敷走，羌、渾詣李抱玉降。

translations.literal: Ren Fu fled; the Qiang and Hun came to Li Baoyu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fu fled. The Qiang and Hun submitted to Li Baoyu.

sentences.zh: 始，懷恩立功，門內死王事者四十六人。

translations.literal: From the first, when Huai'en won merit, forty-six within his household died in the king's service.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of his career, forty-six members of Huai'en's household had died in the state's service.

sentences.zh: 及拒命，士不弛甲凡三年。

translations.literal: When he defied orders, the soldiers did not unstrap their armor for three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: After he defied the throne, his troops did not lay down their armor for three full years.

sentences.zh: 帝隱忍，數下詔，未嘗聲其反。

translations.literal: The emperor bore it in restraint; he issued edicts many times but never proclaimed his rebellion aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restrained himself and issued repeated edicts, but never once declared openly that Huai'en had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 及死，為之惻然曰：「懷恩不反，為左右所誤耳！」

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor was moved with pity and said, "Huai'en did not rebel—he was misled by those at his side!"
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the emperor said with genuine sorrow, "Huai'en never meant to rebel. Those around him led him astray!"

sentences.zh: 俄而從子名臣以千騎降。

translations.literal: Before long his nephew Mingchen surrendered with a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his nephew Mingchen came over with a thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年，冊懷恩幼女為崇徽公主，嫁回紇雲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dali, Huai'en's young daughter was enfeoffed as Princess Chonghui and married to the Uyghur Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dali, Huai'en's young daughter was made Princess Chonghui and given in marriage to the Uyghur leader Yun.

sentences.zh: 周智光，少賤，失其先系，以騎射從軍，起行間為裨將。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhiguang—Zhou Zhiguang was lowly in youth, lost knowledge of his ancestral line, followed the army by horsemanship and archery, and rose from the ranks to become a deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhiguang came from humble origins and had lost track of his ancestry. He entered the army as a mounted archer and rose from the ranks to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩鎮陜州，與相昵款，數稱薦之，累遷同、華二州節度使。

translations.literal: When Yu Chao'en held Shaanzhou he grew intimate and cordial with him, repeatedly praised and recommended him, and he was promoted in succession to Military Commissioner of Tong and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en, when posted to Shaanzhou, took a liking to him, praised him repeatedly at court, and had him promoted until he held the Tong and Hua commanderies.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，吐蕃、回紇、党項羌、渾、奴剌眾十餘萬寇奉天，智光邀戰澄城，破之，獲駝馬軍貲萬計，逐北至鄜州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tangut Qiang, Hun, and Nula—more than a hundred thousand in all—raided Fengtian. Zhiguang intercepted battle at Chengcheng, defeated them, seized tens of thousands in camels, horses, and military stores, and pursued north to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tangut Qiang, Hun, and Nula—well over a hundred thousand strong—attacked Fengtian. Zhiguang met them at Chengcheng, routed them, seized vast stores of camels, horses, and supplies, and pursued them north to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 素與杜冕仇嫌，時冕屯坊州，家在鄜，智光入殺刺史張麟，害冕宗屬八十人，火民三千舍而去。

translations.literal: He had long borne enmity toward Du Mian. Mian was then encamped at Fangzhou while his family was at Fu; Zhiguang entered, killed Prefect Zhang Lin, harmed eighty of Mian's clansmen, burned three thousand dwellings of the people, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He had long hated Du Mian. Mian was posted at Fangzhou while his family remained at Fu. Zhiguang marched in, killed prefect Zhang Lin, slaughtered eighty of Mian's kinsmen, burned three thousand homes, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朝廷召，懼不赴。

translations.literal: The court summoned him; he feared to come and did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him, but he was afraid to come.

sentences.zh: 更詔冕使梁州避讎，冀其來。

translations.literal: Another edict sent Mian as envoy to Liangzhou to avoid the feud, hoping Zhiguang would come.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Mian to Liangzhou to remove the feud, hoping Zhiguang would finally answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 偃然不聽命，聚不逞數萬，恣剽掠以甘其欲，結固之。

translations.literal: He remained unmoved and would not obey; he gathered tens of thousands of malcontents, indulged in plunder to satisfy his desires, and bound them firmly to him.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the orders all the same, gathered tens of thousands of outlaws, and fed his appetites with unchecked pillage until they were bound to him.

sentences.zh: 殺陜州監軍張誌斌及前虢州刺史龐充。

translations.literal: He killed the Shaanzhou army supervisor Zhang Zhibin and the former Guo Prefect Pang Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He killed the Shaanzhou army supervisor Zhang Zhibin and the former prefect of Guo, Pang Chong.

sentences.zh: 初，誌斌自陜入奏，智光慢不為禮，誌斌責之，怒曰：「仆固懷恩豈反者邪？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhibin came from Shaan to report at court, Zhiguang was disrespectful and showed no courtesy. Zhibin reproached him, and in anger he said, "Was Pugu Huai'en truly a rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhibin came from Shaan to report at court, Zhiguang treated him with open contempt. Zhibin rebuked him, and Zhiguang burst out: "Was Pugu Huai'en really a rebel?

sentences.zh: 皆鼠輩弄威福趣之禍也。

translations.literal: It was all petty men playing with power and favor who drove him to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men playing with power and favor drove him to ruin.

sentences.zh: 我本不反，今為爾反！」

translations.literal: I was not going to rebel—now I rebel because of you!"
translations.idiomatic: I had no thought of rebelling—now I rebel because of you!"

sentences.zh: 遂叱斬誌斌，饗帳下。

translations.literal: He then shouted for Zhibin to be beheaded and feasted his command tent.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhibin executed on the spot and held a feast for his officers.

sentences.zh: 時崔圓自淮南納方物百萬，盜頡其半；

translations.literal: At that time Cui Yuan brought tribute goods worth a million from Huainan; Zhiguang stole half of it;
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yuan forwarded a million in tribute goods from Huainan, Zhiguang seized half;

sentences.zh: 天下貢奉輸漕，劫留之；

translations.literal: tribute and transport from across the realm he intercepted and held;
translations.idiomatic: he intercepted tribute and grain shipments from across the empire;

sentences.zh: 士沿調當西者懼何詰，間道走同者，遣部將邀捕斬之。

translations.literal: soldiers on rotation bound west feared interrogation, and those who took bypaths toward Tong he sent deputies to intercept, seize, and behead.
translations.idiomatic: soldiers on rotation westward, fearing interrogation, tried to slip through by back roads toward Tongzhou, and he sent officers to ambush and execute them.

sentences.zh: 代宗未暴其罪，命中使余元仙持詔拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong did not yet expose his crimes and ordered the palace envoy Yuan Yuansian to bear an edict appointing him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong had not yet denounced his crimes openly and sent palace envoy Yuan Yuansian with an edict appointing him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既受詔，恚語曰：「吾有大功，上不與平章事，且同、華地狹，不足申腳，若加陜、虢、商、鄜、坊五州，差可。」

translations.literal: After receiving the edict he spoke in resentment: "I have great merit, yet the court will not make me Grand Councilor; moreover Tong and Hua are too narrow in territory—not enough to stretch my feet. If Shaan, Guo, Shang, Fu, and Fang were added, that would do."
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the edict he raged: "I have rendered great service, yet the court will not make me chief minister. Tong and Hua are too cramped even to stretch my legs. Add Shaan, Guo, Shang, Fu, and Fang, and that might suffice."

sentences.zh: 因言：「諸子皆彎弓二百斤，有萬人敵，挾天子令諸侯，非智光尚誰可？」

translations.literal: He then said: "My sons all bend bows of two hundred jin and are a match for ten thousand men. To hold the Son of Heaven and command the feudal lords—if not Zhiguang, who is fit?"
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "My sons can each draw a two-hundred-jin bow and are match for ten thousand men. If anyone is to hold the Son of Heaven and command the lords, who but Zhiguang?"

sentences.zh: 即歷詆大臣，元仙震汗。

translations.literal: He then reviled the chief ministers one by one; Yuansian broke out in cold sweat.
translations.idiomatic: He then abused the chief ministers one by one until Yuansian was shaking with fear.

sentences.zh: 徐遺百縑遣之。

translations.literal: After a time he sent off a hundred bolts of silk to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: After a while he sent him away with a gift of a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 自立生祠，俾其下襘賽。

translations.literal: He erected a living shrine to himself and had his subordinates offer robes and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He built a living shrine to himself and ordered his men to worship there with offerings.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年，帝詔郭子儀密圖之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali the emperor ordered Guo Ziyi to plot against him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dali the emperor secretly ordered Guo Ziyi to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 同、華路閉，詔書不能通，乃召子儀婿趙縱受口詔，書帛內蜜丸，遣家童走間道傳詔。

translations.literal: The Tong and Hua routes were closed and edicts could not pass; the emperor then summoned Ziyi's son-in-law Zhao Zong to receive the oral edict, wrote it on silk inside a honey pill, and sent a household boy by a hidden path to transmit the decree.
translations.idiomatic: The roads through Tong and Hua were cut and imperial orders could not get through. The emperor summoned Guo Ziyi's son-in-law Zhao Zong, gave him the command orally, wrote it on silk sealed inside a honey pellet, and sent a household servant by a secret route to deliver it.

sentences.zh: 子儀得詔，聲言討之。

translations.literal: When Ziyi received the edict he proclaimed that he would punish Zhiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi received the order and publicly announced that he would march against Zhiguang.

sentences.zh: 未行，其眾大攜，部將李漢惠自同州降子儀。

translations.literal: Before he marched, Zhiguang's host broke apart in great disorder; the commander Li Hanhui surrendered to Ziyi from Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before Guo Ziyi even marched, Zhiguang's army collapsed. His officer Li Hanhui defected from Tongzhou to Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 乃貶智光澧州刺史，聽百人隨身，貸將吏一切不問。

translations.literal: Zhiguang was then demoted to Prefect of Lingzhou, allowed a hundred followers, and all commanders and clerks were pardoned without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang was demoted to prefect of Lingzhou, allowed only a hundred attendants, and all his officers were pardoned without question.

sentences.zh: 尋為帳下斬其首，並斬子元耀、元幹來獻，詔梟首皇城南街。

translations.literal: Before long his own command tent cut off his head, and also beheaded his sons Yuanyao and Yuangan and presented them; an edict ordered their heads displayed on spikes at the south street of the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his own officers cut off his head, beheaded his sons Yuanyao and Yuangan as well, and sent them to the capital. An edict ordered the heads spiked on the south street of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 判官邵賁、別將蔣羅漢並伏誅。

translations.literal: The aide Shao Fen and the deputy general Jiang Luohan were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Shao Fen and deputy commander Jiang Luohan were also executed.

sentences.zh: 敕有司具儀告太清宮、太廟、七陵。

translations.literal: An imperial command ordered the relevant offices to prepare rites and report to the Supreme Clear Palace, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the seven tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the proper rites performed and the victory reported to the Supreme Clear Palace, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the seven imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 先是，淮西李忠臣入朝，次潼關，聞智光反，率兵討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Zhongchen of Huaixi entered court and halted at Tong Pass; hearing that Zhiguang had rebelled, he led troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Zhongchen of Huaixi was on his way to court and had stopped at Tong Pass. Hearing of Zhiguang's rebellion, he marched to attack him.

sentences.zh: 會敗，忠臣因入華大掠，自赤水至潼關畜產財物皆盡，官吏至衣紙自蔽、累日不食者。

translations.literal: When Zhiguang was defeated, Zhongchen thereupon entered Hua and plundered on a great scale; from Chishui to Tong Pass livestock and goods were exhausted, and officials came to clothing themselves in paper and going days without food.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiguang fell, Zhongchen swept into Hua and plundered it bare. From Chishui to Tong Pass every animal and scrap of wealth was taken. Officials were reduced to wrapping themselves in paper and going days without food.

sentences.zh: 梁崇義，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi—Liang Chongyi was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 以概量業於市，力能舒鉤。

translations.literal: He made his living measuring grain in the market; his strength was enough to straighten a bent hook.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his living measuring grain in the marketplace, and was strong enough to unbend an iron hook.

sentences.zh: 後為羽林射生，事來瑱。

translations.literal: Later he became an Imperial Guard archer and served Lai Tian.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the Imperial Guard as an archer and served under Lai Tian.

sentences.zh: 沈默寡言。

translations.literal: Silent and sparing of speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was quiet and spoke little.

sentences.zh: 瑱自襄陽朝京師，分諸將戍福昌、南陽。

translations.literal: When Tian went from Xiangyang to attend court, he divided his generals to garrison Fuchang and Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Tian went from Xiangyang to the capital, he posted his generals to garrison Fuchang and Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 瑱誅，戍者潰，崇義自南陽勒眾還襄州，與李昭、薛南陽相讓為長，眾曰：「非梁卿莫可。」

translations.literal: When Tian was executed the garrison troops scattered. Chongyi, from Nanyang, gathered the force and returned to Xiangzhou. He and Li Zhao and Xue Nanyang deferred to one another for leadership, and the men said, "Only Lord Liang will do."
translations.idiomatic: After Lai Tian was executed the garrison collapsed. Chongyi rallied the troops at Nanyang and marched back to Xiangzhou. He, Li Zhao, and Xue Nanyang each yielded the lead to the others, until the men cried, "No one but Lord Liang will do."

sentences.zh: 遂總其軍，殺昭及南陽，脅制眾心。

translations.literal: He then took overall command of the army, killed Zhao and Nanyang, and coerced the men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He took command, killed Zhao and Nanyang, and bent the army to his will.

sentences.zh: 代宗因即拜節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong thereupon immediately appointed him military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong promptly appointed him military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 舉七州兵二萬，與田承嗣、李正己、薛嵩、李寶臣相輔車，根牙槃結。

translations.literal: He raised twenty thousand troops from seven prefectures. With Tian Chengsi, Li Zhengji, Xue Song, and Li Baochen he was mutually supporting like interlocking wheels, their roots intertwined.
translations.idiomatic: He fielded twenty thousand men from seven prefectures and was bound to Tian Chengsi, Li Zhengji, Xue Song, and Li Baochen like wheels locked together, their interests deeply intertwined.

sentences.zh: 然獨以地褊兵少，法令最治，折節遇士以自振，襄、漢間人識教義。

translations.literal: Yet he alone, because his territory was narrow and his troops few, kept the strictest discipline, humbled himself toward scholars to revive his standing, and people between Xiang and Han knew propriety and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his domain was small and his army thin. He enforced the strictest discipline, humbled himself before scholars to rebuild his reputation, and between the Xiang and Han rivers his rule was known for decency.

sentences.zh: 親厚數諷入朝，答曰：「來公有大功，畏閹豎讒，逡巡辭召。

translations.literal: Close associates repeatedly urged him to attend court. He replied, "Lord Lai had great merit but feared slander by the eunuchs and hesitated, declining the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Friends close to him often urged him to go to court. He answered, "Lord Lai had rendered great service, yet he feared the eunuchs' slander and lingered, refusing the summons.

sentences.zh: 至代宗立，不待駕而朝，即見族。

translations.literal: When Daizong took the throne, without waiting for the imperial procession he went to court—and immediately his clan was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong succeeded, Lai went to court without waiting for the new emperor—and was destroyed root and branch.

sentences.zh: 吾釁盈矣，若何欲見上乎？」

translations.literal: My guilt is already full. Why would you want me to see the emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: My offenses are already more than enough. Why do you want me to face the throne?"

sentences.zh: 建中元年，李希烈請討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Li Xilie requested permission to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jianzhong era, Li Xilie asked to lead a campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 崇義懼，整飭軍旅。

translations.literal: Chongyi was afraid and put his army in order.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi was alarmed and drilled his troops.

sentences.zh: 男子郭昔上變事，德宗欲示以信，流昔遠方，詔金部員外郎李舟諭旨。

translations.literal: A man named Guo Xi reported a mutiny plot. Dezong wished to show good faith, exiled Xi to a distant place, and ordered Jinbu Vice Director Li Zhou to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: When a man named Guo Xi denounced a plot, Dezong wished to show his trustworthiness, banished Xi to a distant post, and sent Li Zhou of the Ministry of Revenue to explain the court's intentions.

sentences.zh: 初，劉文喜之難，舟奉詔入涇州，俄而帳下斬文喜以聞，四方傳舟能覆軍殺將，反側者皆惡之。
