translations.literal: Earlier, during Liu Wenxi's crisis, Zhou had entered Jing Prefecture by edict; soon his subordinates beheaded Wenxi and reported it. Everywhere it was said that Zhou could overturn armies and kill generals, and all restless rebels hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Liu Wenxi affair, Zhou had entered Jing Prefecture on imperial orders; before long his own men beheaded Wenxi and reported it. Word spread that Zhou could turn armies and strike down commanders, and every wavering rebel feared him.

sentences.zh: 舟至，以入朝勸崇義，崇義不悅。

translations.literal: When Zhou arrived he urged Chongyi to attend court; Chongyi was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou reached his headquarters and pressed him to come to court; Chongyi took offense.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣使尉撫諸道，舟復如崇義所，遂不肯內，請易它使。

translations.literal: The next year the court sent envoys to comfort the various circuits. Zhou again went to Chongyi's headquarters, and Chongyi then refused to admit him, requesting another envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the court dispatched envoys to reassure the circuits. Zhou was sent to Chongyi again, but Chongyi would not let him in and asked that someone else be sent.

sentences.zh: 更命給事中廬翰往，崇義益不安，跋扈甚，諫者多死。

translations.literal: The appointment was changed to Supervising Secretary Lu Han. Chongyi grew still more uneasy, became very domineering, and many who remonstrated with him died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Han, a supervising secretary, was sent in his place. Chongyi grew more anxious, turned increasingly overbearing, and many who advised against it were killed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以不疑示天下，乃加同中書門下平章事，妻及子悉封賞，賜鐵券，擢其將藺杲為鄧州刺史，遣御史張著以手詔召崇義。

translations.literal: To show the realm that it harbored no suspicion, the court promoted him to Same Rank as Grand Councilor, enfeoffed and rewarded his wife and sons, granted an iron certificate of mercy, promoted his general Lan Gao to prefect of Dengzhou, and sent Censor Zhang Zhu with a handwritten edict to summon Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: To show the empire it had no doubts, the court made him Grand Councilor of the second rank, enfeoffed and rewarded his wife and children, granted him an iron certificate, promoted his general Lan Gao to prefect of Deng, and sent Censor Zhang Zhu with an edict in the emperor's own hand to summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 崇義使卒持滿，乃受命。

translations.literal: Chongyi had soldiers hold their bows fully drawn; only then did he accept the order.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi had his men stand with bows drawn full before he accepted the summons.

sentences.zh: 杲奉詔不敢發，詣崇義自言。

translations.literal: Gao received the edict but dared not set out and went to Chongyi to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Gao received the appointment but dared not leave; he went to Chongyi and told him so.

sentences.zh: 崇義對著號哭，遂拒詔。

translations.literal: Chongyi wept loudly before Zhang and then refused the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Facing Zhang Zhu, Chongyi broke into loud weeping—and then defied the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝命李希烈率諸道兵進討。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Li Xilie to lead troops from the various circuits in an advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Xilie to march against him at the head of forces from several circuits.

sentences.zh: 崇義先攻江陵，欲通黔、嶺，敗於四望而還。

translations.literal: Chongyi first attacked Jiangling, seeking to open a route to Qian and Ling, but was defeated at Siwang and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi struck first at Jiangling, hoping to open a path into Qian and Ling, but was beaten at Siwang and driven back.

sentences.zh: 殺希烈臨漢屯兵千餘，希烈怒，引兵循漢而上。

translations.literal: He killed more than a thousand of Xilie's troops garrisoned at Linhan. Xilie was enraged and led his army up the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered more than a thousand of Xilie's men posted along the Han at Linhan. Xilie flew into a rage and marched upriver.

sentences.zh: 崇義使翟崇暉、杜少誠戰蠻水，折北至涑口，大敗。

translations.literal: Chongyi sent Zhai Chonghui and Du Shaocheng to fight at Manshui, then turned north to Sukou and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi sent Zhai Chonghui and Du Shaocheng to give battle at Manshui, then swung north to Sukou, where they were routed.

sentences.zh: 二將降，希烈寵之，使部降兵徇襄陽，約百姓按堵。

translations.literal: The two generals surrendered. Xilie favored them and had them lead the surrendered troops through Xiangyang, promising the people they would be left in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Both commanders surrendered. Xilie treated them well and sent them ahead with the defectors into Xiangyang, pledging that the populace would not be disturbed.

sentences.zh: 崇義閉壁，守者斬關出，不可止，乃與妻赴井死，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Chongyi closed the walls. The defenders cut through the gates and fled; he could not stop them. He and his wife then threw themselves into a well and died, and his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi shut the city gates, but his own garrison broke out and fled beyond his control. He and his wife leapt into a well and died; his head was forwarded to the capital.

sentences.zh: 希烈誅其親族及軍從臨漢役者三千人。

translations.literal: Xilie executed his clansmen and three thousand soldiers who had served at Linhan.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie put his kin to death and executed three thousand men who had served under him at Linhan.

sentences.zh: 崇義孫叔明，養於李納，後從劉悟為昭義將，從諫死，遣進旄節，有詔誅之。

translations.literal: Chongyi's grandson Shuming was raised by Li Na. Later he followed Liu Wu as a general of Zhaoyi. When Wu died, Shuming was sent to advance the banners and credentials of office; an edict ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi's grandson Shuming was reared by Li Na and later served Liu Wu as an officer of Zhaoyi. After Wu's death Shuming was sent to present the military commission; the court ordered him put to death.

sentences.zh: 李懷光，渤海靺鞨人，本姓茹。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang—Li Huai'guang was a Mohe man of Bohai; his original surname was Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang was a Mohe tribesman from Bohai; his family name had been Ru.

sentences.zh: 父常，徙幽州，為朔方部將，以戰多賜姓，更名嘉慶。

translations.literal: His father Chang moved to Youzhou and became a Shuofang department general. For many battles he was granted a surname and was renamed Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang migrated to Youzhou and served as a Shuofang officer. For repeated victories in battle he was granted a surname and renamed Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 懷光在軍，積勞至開府儀同三司，為都虞候。

translations.literal: Huai'guang in the army accumulated merit until he reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies and became Chief Army Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In service Huai'guang rose through accumulated merit to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and became chief army inspector.

sentences.zh: 勇鷙敢誅殺，雖親屬犯法，無所回貸。

translations.literal: Fierce and brutal, he dared to execute and kill; even when kin violated the law he granted no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce and ruthless, ready to kill; even relatives who broke the law received no mercy.

sentences.zh: 節度使郭子儀仁厚，不親事，以紀綱委懷光，軍中畏之。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Guo Ziyi was benevolent and lenient and did not manage affairs personally; he entrusted discipline to Huai'guang, and the army feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, the commissioner, was mild and did not attend to daily affairs himself; he left discipline to Huai'guang, and the troops feared him.

sentences.zh: 會母喪，起兼邠、寧、慶都將。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning to serve concurrently as commander of the Bin, Ning, and Qing forces.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death he was called back from mourning to command the Bin, Ning, and Qing armies.

sentences.zh: 德宗罷子儀副元帥，以所部兵分諸將，故懷光檢校刑部尚書，為寧、慶、晉、絳、慈、隰等州節度使。

translations.literal: Dezong removed Ziyi as vice commander-in-chief and divided his troops among the generals. Therefore Huai'guang was made acting Minister of Justice and military commissioner of Ning, Qing, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong stripped Guo Ziyi of the vice command and split his forces among other generals. Huai'guang was made acting Minister of Justice and commissioner over Ning, Qing, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 引眾城長武，據原首，臨涇水，以扼吐蕃空道，自是不敢南侵。

translations.literal: He led his host to fortify Changwu, held Yuan Shou, faced the Jing River, and blocked the Tibetans' open route; from then on they dared not invade south.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men to build up Changwu, seized Yuan Shou, and stood above the Jing River, choking the Tibetans' open corridor—after which they no longer dared push south.

sentences.zh: 建中初，楊炎欲城原州，使懷光兼帥涇原，遂其功。

translations.literal: Early in Jianzhong, Yang Yan wished to fortify Yuanzhou and had Huai'guang also command Jingyuan to accomplish it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong, Yang Yan wanted to rebuild Yuanzhou and had Huai'guang take Jingyuan as well to carry the work through.

sentences.zh: 原州宿將史抗、溫儒雅等，故子儀麾下，嘗在懷光右，及處其下，意郁郁，懷光因罪誅之，由是涇軍迎畏。

translations.literal: The veteran generals of Yuanzhou, Shi Kang and Wen Ruya, had formerly been under Ziyi and had once ranked above Huai'guang. When placed beneath him they were sullen; Huai'guang executed them on charges, and from this the Jing army both feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhou's old commanders Shi Kang and Wen Ruya had served under Guo Ziyi and once outranked Huai'guang. Subordinated to him, they brooded; Huai'guang had them executed on trumped-up charges, and the Jing troops learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 劉文喜者，因眾懼，遂叛。

translations.literal: Liu Wenxi, because the troops were afraid, then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenxi rebelled when he saw how frightened the men were.

sentences.zh: 詔與朱泚討平之，加檢校太子少師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him and Zhu Ci to pacify the rebellion, and he was added as Acting Crown Prince Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhu Ci were ordered to suppress the revolt, and Huai'guang was named acting Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙朔方節度使，實封戶四百，仍領邠寧。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Shuofang military commissioner with four hundred enfeoffed households and still commanded Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was moved to Shuofang commissioner with four hundred taxable households and retained Bin-Ning.

sentences.zh: 時馬燧、李抱真討田悅，未克，詔懷光以朔方兵萬五千並力。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Sui and Li Baozhen were attacking Tian Yue without success. An edict ordered Huai'guang to bring fifteen thousand Shuofang troops to join the effort.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and Li Baozhen were then besieging Tian Yue without result. The court ordered Huai'guang to march with fifteen thousand Shuofang troops to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 懷光至魏，未及營，與朱滔等戰連篋山，為賊所敗，悅因決水灌軍，燧等退屯魏縣。

translations.literal: Huai'guang reached Wei. Before he had set camp he fought Zhu Tao and others at Lianqieshan and was defeated by the rebels. Yue then broke the dam to flood the army, and Sui and the rest withdrew to camp at Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang reached Wei, but before his camp was pitched he fought Zhu Tao and others at Lianqieshan and was beaten. Yue broke the dikes to flood the allied army, and Ma Sui fell back on Weixian.

sentences.zh: 尋進同中書門下平章事，益戶二百。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Same Rank as Grand Councilor with two hundred additional households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Grand Councilor of the second rank and given two hundred more enfeoffed households.

sentences.zh: 與滔等相持，久不戰。

translations.literal: He and Tao and the others faced one another and for a long time did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhu Tao remained locked in stalemate, neither side giving battle for a long while.

sentences.zh: 帝狩奉天，懷光率所部奔命。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Fengtian on campaign, Huai'guang led his troops to rush to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew to Fengtian, Huai'guang marched his command to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 方雨淖，奮厲軍士倍道進，自蒲津絕河，敗泚軍於醴泉。

translations.literal: Rain had turned the roads to mud, yet he roused his soldiers to advance by double marches, forded the river from Pujin, and defeated Ci's army at Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were churned to mud by rain, but he drove his men forward at forced march, crossed the Yellow River at Pujin, and routed Zhu Ci's force at Liquan.

sentences.zh: 將抵奉天，前遣裨將張韶以蠟韜表，隨賊攻城，叩壘呼曰：「我朔方使也！」

translations.literal: As he was about to reach Fengtian he first sent Deputy General Zhang Shao with a wax-sealed memorial. Shao followed the rebels as they besieged the city, knocked on the rampart, and called out, "I am an envoy from Shuofang!"
translations.idiomatic: Near Fengtian he sent his deputy Zhang Shao ahead with a memorial sealed in wax. Shao slipped in among the rebels besieging the city, beat on the wall, and shouted, "I am from Shuofang!"

sentences.zh: 縋而上，比登，身被數十矢。

translations.literal: They lowered a rope and pulled him up; by the time he climbed the wall his body had been struck by dozens of arrows.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him up on a rope; by the time he gained the top he had taken dozens of arrows.

sentences.zh: 時帝被圍急，聞之喜，即持韶大號城上，人心乃安。

translations.literal: The emperor was in desperate straits under siege; hearing this he rejoiced and immediately held Shao aloft, shouting from the wall, and the people's hearts were settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was hard pressed in the siege; when he heard, he rejoiced, lifted Shao high above the parapet for all to see, and the city's panic eased.

sentences.zh: 又敗賊於魯店，泚解圍去。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels at Ludian, and Ci lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels again at Ludian, and Zhu Ci broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進加副元帥、中書令。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Commander-in-Chief and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander-in-chief and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 懷光為人疏而愎，誦言：「宰相謀議乖剌，度支賦斂重，京兆尹刻薄軍食，天下之亂皆由此。

translations.literal: Huai'guang as a man was coarse and obstinate. He kept saying, "The chancellors' counsel is perverse, the Revenue Commission's levies are heavy, and the Jingzhao intendant skimps the army's provisions—all the disorder under heaven stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang was blunt and stubborn. He said again and again, "The chancellors plot crookedly, the Revenue Board taxes too heavily, and the intendant of Jingzhao pinches our rations—every calamity in the realm comes from this.

sentences.zh: 吾見上，且請誅之。」

translations.literal: When I see the emperor I shall request their execution."
translations.idiomatic: When I see His Majesty I will ask that they be put to death."

sentences.zh: 或以告王翃，翃等計：「懷光有大功，上且訪以得失，使其言入，豈不殆哉！」

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Wang Hong. Hong and the others plotted: "Huai'guang has great merit; the emperor will consult him on right and wrong. If his words enter court, will we not be imperiled!"
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Wang Hong. Hong and his circle said, "Huai'guang has saved the throne; the emperor will ask his judgment on affairs. If that talk reaches the throne, we are finished!"

sentences.zh: 遂告盧杞，杞即說帝曰：「懷光兵威已振，逆賊破膽，若席勝，可一舉滅賊。

translations.literal: They then told Lu Qi. Qi immediately persuaded the emperor: "Huai'guang's military prestige is already stirred and the rebels' courage is broken. If he rides the victory he can destroy the rebels in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: They went to Lu Qi. Qi at once told the emperor, "Huai'guang's army is at full heat and the rebels are terrified. Let him press the advantage and the rebellion can be ended in one blow.

sentences.zh: 今入朝，則必宴勞留連，賊得從容完備，卒難圖也！」

translations.literal: If he enters court now he will surely be feasted and detained. The rebels will gain leisure to prepare fully, and in the end they will be hard to overcome!"
translations.idiomatic: But if he is summoned to court he will be wined and detained while the rebels recover their strength—then they will be far harder to crush!"

sentences.zh: 帝不得其情，因然之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not grasp the real situation and therefore agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, not seeing their motive, agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃敕懷光屯便橋，督諸將進討。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Huai'guang to camp at Bianqiao and supervise the generals in advancing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang was ordered to hold Bianqiao and drive the other generals forward.

sentences.zh: 懷光自以徑千里赴難，為奸臣拫隔不得朝，頗恚悵，去屯咸陽。

translations.literal: Huai'guang thought that he had rushed a thousand li to rescue the crisis yet was blocked by treacherous ministers from audience and was quite resentful; he left to camp at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang believed he had raced a thousand li to save the emperor, only to be shut out by scheming ministers. Bitter and resentful, he withdrew his camp to Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 明日，李晟會陳濤斜，壁壘未具，賊大至。

translations.literal: The next day Li Sheng met the enemy at Chen Taoxie. The ramparts were not yet complete when the rebels came in force.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Li Sheng engaged at Chen Taoxie. His defenses were not finished when the rebels arrived in strength.

sentences.zh: 晟說懷光曰：「賊保宮苑，攻之良難。

translations.literal: Sheng persuaded Huai'guang: "The rebels hold the palace gardens; attacking them is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng urged Huai'guang: "The rebels are dug into the imperial parks—hard ground to storm.

sentences.zh: 今敢離窟穴，與公薄戰，此天以賊賜公也。」

translations.literal: Now they dare leave their lair and fight you at close quarters—this is heaven granting you the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: But now they have come out of their hole to meet you hand to hand. Heaven is handing them to you."

sentences.zh: 懷光曰：「吾馬未秣，士未飯，可遽戰哉？

translations.literal: Huai'guang said, "My horses are not fed and my soldiers have not eaten—can we fight in haste?
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang replied, "My horses are unfed and my men unfed. How can we fight now?

sentences.zh: 姑養吾勇以待之。」

translations.literal: For now let me nurture my warriors' courage and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Let me rest my men and hoard their fury for the moment."

sentences.zh: 晟不得已，閉壁不出。

translations.literal: Sheng had no choice and closed the walls without emerging.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng had no choice but to shut the gates and hold still.

sentences.zh: 懷光數暴杞等罪，帝為貶杞與趙贊、白誌貞，又劾奏中人翟文秀，亦殺之以尉懷光。

translations.literal: Huai'guang repeatedly exposed the crimes of Qi and the others. For his sake the emperor demoted Qi, Zhao Zan, and Bai Zhizhen, and also impeached and executed the eunuch Zhai Wenxiu, killing him as well to appease Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang kept denouncing Lu Qi and his allies. The emperor demoted Qi, Zhao Zan, and Bai Zhizhen for him, and even executed the eunuch Zhai Wenxiu to placate him.

sentences.zh: 然益自疑，堅壁八旬不出戰，屢詔使進軍，以伺釁為解，陰連朱泚。

translations.literal: Yet he grew still more suspicious, held his walls for eighty days without fighting, and though repeatedly issued an edict to advance excused himself as waiting for an opening, while secretly linking with Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he grew more suspicious still, sat behind his walls eighty days without battle, pleaded he was waiting for an opening whenever ordered forward, and secretly treated with Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 初，崔漢衡使吐蕃求助兵，尚結贊曰：「吾法，進軍以本兵大臣為信。

translations.literal: Initially, when Cui Hanheng was sent to Tibet to request aid troops, Shang Jiezan said, "By our law, an army on the march requires the native troops' grand minister as pledge.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hanheng first asked Tibet for troops, Shang Jiezan said, "By our law we advance only when the chief minister of the native force is our pledge.

sentences.zh: 今制書不署懷光，未敢前。」

translations.literal: The present imperial decree does not bear Huai'guang's signature; I dare not advance."
translations.idiomatic: Your edict is not countersigned by Huai'guang. I dare not march."

sentences.zh: 帝乃命翰林學士陸贄詣懷光議事，懷光陳三不可，且言：「吐蕃舍人馬重英陷長安，贊普責其不焚爇，今其來，必肆宿誌，一不可。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi to go to Huai'guang to discuss affairs. Huai'guang stated three impossibilities and also said, "The Tibetan attendant Ma Chongying took Chang'an; the qaghan blamed him for not burning it. Now they come—they will surely indulge their old intent. First impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi to negotiate. Huai'guang listed three reasons to refuse and said, "Ma Chongying of Tibet held Chang'an, yet the qaghan faulted him for not burning it. If they come now they will surely act on old grudges—that is the first objection.

sentences.zh: 彼雲引兵五萬，既用其人，則同漢士，儻邀我厚賞，何以致之？

translations.literal: They claim fifty thousand troops; since we use their men they are the same as Han soldiers. If they demand rich rewards from us, how can we satisfy them?
translations.idiomatic: They say they bring fifty thousand men; once we rely on them they are no different from our own troops. If they demand lavish payment, how will we afford it?

sentences.zh: 二不可。

translations.literal: Second impossible.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second.

sentences.zh: 虜人雖來，義不先用，勒兵自固，以觀成敗，王師勝則分功，敗則圖變，狡詐多端，不可信，三不可。」

translations.literal: Though the barbarians come, by principle they do not fight first. They restrain their troops to secure themselves and watch success or failure. If the imperial army wins they divide the merit; if it loses they plot change. Crafty and treacherous in many ways—they cannot be trusted. Third impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Even when they arrive they will not fight first by custom; they will hold their men back and watch how the war goes. If we win they claim a share; if we lose they turn against us. They are treacherous in a hundred ways and cannot be trusted—that is the third."

sentences.zh: 卒不肯署。

translations.literal: In the end he refused to sign.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he would not sign.

sentences.zh: 又謾罵贄曰：「爾何能？」

translations.literal: He also reviled and cursed Zhi: "What ability have you?"
translations.idiomatic: He also abused Lu Zhi to his face: "What are you good for?"

sentences.zh: 興元元年，詔加太尉，賜鐵券。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan an edict added him as Grand Marshal and granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan he was named Grand Marshal and given an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 懷光赫然怒曰：「凡疑人臣反，則賜券。

translations.literal: Huai'guang suddenly flared in anger and said, "Whenever a minister is suspected of rebellion, an iron certificate is granted.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang erupted in fury. "Whenever the court suspects a minister of rebellion," he said, "it grants an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 今授懷光，是使反也！」

translations.literal: Now granting it to Huai'guang is making me rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you give one to me—that is telling me to rebel!"

sentences.zh: 抵於地。

translations.literal: He threw it to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He dashed it to the floor.

sentences.zh: 時部將韓遊瑰將兵衛奉天，懷光約令為變，遊瑰以聞。

translations.literal: At that time the deputy Han Yougui was commanding troops guarding Fengtian. Huai'guang arranged for him to mutiny; Yougui reported it.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Han Yougui was then guarding Fengtian. Huai'guang tried to win him to mutiny; Yougui reported the plot.

sentences.zh: 數日，又密書趣之，門者捕送。

translations.literal: Several days later he again sent a secret letter urging him on; the gate guards seized it and delivered it.
translations.idiomatic: Days later another secret letter pressed him; the gate watch seized it and sent it in.

sentences.zh: 又遣將趙升鸞諜於奉天，升鸞告渾瑊曰：「懷光遣達奚承俊火乾陵，使我為內應，以脅乘輿。」

translations.literal: He also sent the general Zhao Shengquan to spy at Fengtian. Shengquan told Hun Zhen, "Huai'guang sent Daxi Chengjun to burn Ganling and made me the inside collaborator to coerce the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Zhao Shengquan to spy at Fengtian. Shengquan informed Hun Zhen, "Huai'guang sent Daxi Chengjun to fire Ganling and made me his man inside to threaten the emperor."

sentences.zh: 瑊白髮其奸，請帝決幸梁州。

translations.literal: Zhen reported, exposing the plot, and requested that the emperor decide to go to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen laid the plot bare and urged the emperor to withdraw to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝令瑊戒嚴，未畢，帝自西門出，詔戴休顏守奉天。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhen to alert the defenses. Before it was finished the emperor went out the west gate and issued an edict to Dai Xiuyan to guard Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zhen to ready the defenses, but before the order was complete he slipped out the west gate and left Dai Xiuyan to hold Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 懷光遣將孟廷寶、惠靜壽、孫福率輕騎趨南山，糧料使張增遇之。

translations.literal: Huai'guang sent the generals Meng Tingbao, Hui Jingshou, and Sun Fu with light cavalry toward the Southern Mountains, and Commissary Zhang Zeng met them.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang sent Meng Tingbao, Hui Jingshou, and Sun Fu with light horse toward the southern hills; Zhang Zeng, the supply officer, ran into them.

sentences.zh: 三人計曰：「吾屬以叛聞，不如緩軍，彼怒，不過不吾將耳。」

translations.literal: The three plotted: "We are already known as rebels. Better to slow the army; if he is angry, at most he will not employ us."
translations.idiomatic: The three conspired: "We are already marked as traitors. Better to drag our feet—at worst he stops using us."

sentences.zh: 使增紿眾曰：「由此東，吾有見糧可食也。」

translations.literal: They had Zeng deceive the troops: "East from here I have grain in sight that can be eaten."
translations.idiomatic: They had Zeng trick the men: "Grain lies just ahead to the east."

sentences.zh: 廷寶等引而東，縱卒大掠，而百官遂入駱谷。

translations.literal: Tingbao and the others led them east, let the soldiers plunder on a great scale, and the officials then entered Luogu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbao led them east and let them loot freely while the court party escaped into Luogu Valley.

sentences.zh: 追帝不及。

translations.literal: They could not overtake the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They failed to catch the emperor.

sentences.zh: 還白懷光，懷光怒，悉罷其兵。

translations.literal: Returning they reported to Huai'guang. Huai'guang was enraged and dismissed all their troops.
translations.idiomatic: They returned and told Huai'guang, who in rage stripped them of command.

sentences.zh: 懷光乃奪李建徽、陽惠元等軍，屯好畤，然其下稍稍攜貳。

translations.literal: Huai'guang then seized the armies of Li Jianhui, Yang Huiyuan, and others, camped at Haozhi, yet his subordinates gradually wavered in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang then took over Li Jianhui's and Yang Huiyuan's forces and encamped at Haozhi, but his men slowly fell away.

sentences.zh: 泚始憚之，至是欲遂臣懷光。

translations.literal: Ci had initially feared him; by now he wished to make Huai'guang his subject.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had once feared him; now he wanted Huai'guang to submit.

sentences.zh: 懷光怒，告絕，益不安，乃引兵掠涇陽、三原、富平，遂如河中，留張昕守咸陽。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was enraged, broke off relations, grew still more uneasy, then led troops to plunder Jingyang, Sanyuan, and Fuping, went on to Hezhong, and left Zhang Xin to guard Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang raged, broke with him, grew more unsettled, marched to ravage Jingyang, Sanyuan, and Fuping, then moved on Hezhong, leaving Zhang Xin at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 而孟涉、段威勇擁兵降李晟，韓遊瑰殺昕，以邠州歸。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Meng She and Duan Weiyong led their troops in surrender to Li Sheng; Han Yougui killed Xin and returned Binzhou to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Meng She and Duan Weiyong meanwhile surrendered to Li Sheng; Han Yougui killed Zhang Xin and brought Bin back to the throne.

sentences.zh: 戴休顏自奉天令於軍曰：「懷光反。」

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan, holding command at Fengtian, proclaimed to the army: "Huai'guang has rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan, magistrate of Fengtian, announced to the troops: "Huai'guang has turned traitor."

sentences.zh: 乃城守。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fortified the city and held defense.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison then walled the city and stood on the defense.

sentences.zh: 有詔以懷光為太子太保，許其麾下擇功高者一人統其兵。

translations.literal: An edict made Huai'guang Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and permitted one man of high merit among his subordinates to command his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and allowed him to choose one accomplished subordinate to take command of his army.

sentences.zh: 不奉詔。

translations.literal: He did not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the order.

sentences.zh: 懷光至河中，取同、絳二州，按兵觀望。

translations.literal: Huai'guang reached Hezhong, took Tong and Jiang prefectures, and held his troops in observation without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang withdrew to Hezhong, seized Tong and Jiang, and camped his forces in watchful waiting.

sentences.zh: 京師平，命給事中孔巢父、中人啖守盈召之，皆為懷光帳下所害，於是繕兵嚴守。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, the emperor ordered Supervising Secretary Kong Chaofu and the palace attendant Dan Shouying to summon him; both were killed by men under Huai'guang's tent, whereupon he drilled troops and tightened defense.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was secured, the emperor sent Supervising Secretary Kong Chaofu and the eunuch Dan Shouying to summon him. Huai'guang's camp had them killed; he then rearmed his men and shut the gates.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣渾瑊討之。

translations.literal: The emperor then dispatched Hun Jian to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Hun Jian against him.

sentences.zh: 度支欲罷其軍歲中稟賜，帝曰：「朔方軍累有功，豈以懷光拒命而眾不被恩邪？」

translations.literal: The Revenue Board wished to cut off the army's mid-year ration grants. The emperor said: "The Shuofang army has repeatedly achieved merit—shall the host go unrewarded because Huai'guang defies orders?"
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Board wanted to suspend the Shuofang troops' mid-year stipends. The emperor said, "That army has served the throne again and again—are its soldiers to lose their pay because Huai'guang rebels?"

sentences.zh: 詔所司別貯縑錢，須事定乃給。

translations.literal: He ordered the relevant offices to store silk and coin separately; payment would come only after affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ministries to set silk and cash aside in a separate fund and pay only once the crisis ended.

sentences.zh: 瑊破同州，屯軍不得進，數為懷光所衄。

translations.literal: Jian took Tongzhou but his encamped army could not advance and was repeatedly repulsed by Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian captured Tongzhou, yet his stalled camp could not push forward and was beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝以河東節度使馬燧威名白著，乃拜副元帥，與瑊及鎮國駱元光、邠寧韓遊瑰、鄜坊唐朝臣會兵進討。

translations.literal: Because Hedong Military Commissioner Ma Sui's martial renown was manifest everywhere, he was appointed deputy commander-in-chief; with Jian and Zhenguo's Luo Yuanguang, Binning's Han Yougui, and Zhengfang's Tang Zhaochen he joined forces to advance in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui of Hedong was famed across the realm, so the emperor made him deputy commander-in-chief. He marched with Jian, Luo Yuanguang of Zhenguo, Han Yougui of Binning, and Tang Zhaochen of Zhengfang to press the campaign.

sentences.zh: 燧拔絳州，諸軍遂圍河中。

translations.literal: Sui captured Jiangzhou; the allied armies then besieged Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Sui took Jiangzhou, and the combined hosts closed on Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年八月，朔方部將牛名俊斬懷光，傳首以獻，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhenyuan, the Shuofang officer Niu Mingjun beheaded Huai'guang and sent the head as tribute. He was fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhenyuan 1, the Shuofang officer Niu Mingjun killed Huai'guang and presented his head. He was fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 帝念其功，詔許一子嗣，賜莊、第各一區，聽以禮葬，妻王徙澧州。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of his merit, permitted one son to succeed, granted one manor and one mansion each, allowed burial with full rites, and moved his wife Wang to Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of past service, the emperor allowed one son to inherit, granted a manor and a mansion, permitted a state funeral, and sent his wife Wang to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，懷光死，其子隹盡殺其弟乃死，故懷光無後。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huai'guang died, his son Wei had slain all his younger brothers before himself dying, so Huai'guang had no heir.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, when Huai'guang fell, his son Wei had murdered every younger brother and then died himself, leaving the line extinct.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔曰：「懷舊念功，仁之大也；

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict read: "Cherishing the old and remembering merit is the height of benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict declared, "To honor old service and recall merit is the crown of benevolence;

sentences.zh: 興滅繼絕，義之至也。

translations.literal: raising what is fallen and continuing what is cut off is the utmost of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: to raise the fallen house and continue the severed line is the summit of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 昔蔡叔圯族，周封其子；

translations.literal: Of old, when Uncle Cai's clan was exterminated, Zhou enfeoffed his son;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou wiped out Uncle Cai's house, it still enfeoffed his son;

sentences.zh: 韓信幹紀，漢爵其孥；

translations.literal: when Han Xin violated the law, Han ennobled his kin;
translations.idiomatic: when Han Xin broke the statutes, Han ennobled his family;

sentences.zh: 侯君集不率，太宗存其祀。

translations.literal: when Hou Junji was unruly, Taizong preserved his sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: when Hou Junji rebelled, Taizong kept his line on the altars.

sentences.zh: 考先王之道，烈祖之訓，皆以刑佐德，俾人向方。

translations.literal: Examining the way of former kings and the instruction of the glorious ancestors, all used punishment to assist virtue and turn men toward the right.
translations.idiomatic: The ways of the ancient kings and the teaching of our founding emperors all joined punishment to virtue so men would face the right path.

sentences.zh: 曩者盜臣竊發，朕狩近郊，懷光夙駕千里，奔命行在，假雷霆之威，破虎狼之眾。

translations.literal: Not long ago a treacherous minister rose in secret rebellion; We hunted in the near suburbs. Huai'guang drove a thousand li at dawn to rush to the mobile court, borrowing thunder's might to shatter a host of wolves and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: When treason broke out and We withdrew to hunt the near suburbs, Huai'guang raced a thousand li at first light to the mobile court and, in thunder's fury, broke a wolfish rebel host.

sentences.zh: 守節靡終，潛構禍胎，大戮所加，自貽伊戚，孤魂無歸，懷之恍然。

translations.literal: He did not hold his integrity to the end, secretly bred the seeds of calamity, and when the supreme punishment fell brought sorrow on himself. His lonely spirit has nowhere to return; We are moved to dim reverie in recalling him.
translations.idiomatic: He could not keep faith to the end, secretly nursed rebellion, and when the great sentence fell brought grief on himself alone. His shade wanders homeless; We cannot recall him without a haze of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 宜以外孫燕賜姓李，名曰承緒，以左衛率府胄曹參軍繼懷光後。」

translations.literal: Let his grandson-by-marriage Yan be granted the surname Li and named Chengxu, and as Army Aide in the Left Guard command inherit Huai'guang's line."
translations.idiomatic: Let his grandson-by-marriage Yan take the surname Li and the name Chengxu, and as Army Aide in the Left Guard office succeed to Huai'guang's house."

sentences.zh: 乃賜錢百萬，置田墓側，以備祭享；

translations.literal: A million cash was granted, fields placed beside his tomb for offerings;
translations.idiomatic: A million cash was granted, fields set beside his tomb for sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 還妻王，使就養雲。

translations.literal: his wife Wang was restored and sent to receive provisioned retirement.
translations.idiomatic: his wife Wang was returned to a life of sheltered support.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊，博州博平人。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou—Chen Shaoyou was a native of Boping in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou was a man of Boping in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 幼習老子、莊周書，為崇玄生，諸儒推為都講。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the books of Laozi and Zhuangzi, became a Chongxuan student, and the scholars chose him as head lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he mastered Laozi and Zhuangzi, entered the Chongxuan academy, and the Confucians made him head lecturer.

sentences.zh: 有冒者欲對廣眾切問以屈少遊。

translations.literal: A brash man wished to grill him with pointed questions before the crowd to humiliate Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: A swaggering scholar meant to corner him with sharp questions before a great assembly.

sentences.zh: 及升坐，音吐清辯，據引淹該，問窮而對有餘。

translations.literal: When he took the seat his speech was clear and sharp, his citations broad and exhaustive; questioners were spent while his answers still had room.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, his voice rang clear and his citations ran deep; his challengers were exhausted while his replies still had margin.

sentences.zh: 大學士陳希烈高其能。

translations.literal: Grand Academician Chen Xilie admired his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academician Chen Xilie held his ability in high regard.

sentences.zh: 既擢第，補南平令，治有聲。

translations.literal: After passing the examinations he was made magistrate of Nanping, where his governance won repute.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his degree he was appointed magistrate of Nanping, where his rule won praise.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍御史、回紇糧料使，加檢校職方員外郎充使。

translations.literal: He rose to Attending Censor, commissioner for Uyghur grain supplies, with additional appointment as Acting Director of the Bureau of Appointments on mission.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Attending Censor and Uyghur grain commissioner to Acting Director of the Bureau of Appointments while on embassy.

sentences.zh: 檢校郎官自少遊始。

translations.literal: Acting director appointments in the Secretariat began with Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: The custom of acting Secretariat directors began with Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩表署河北副元帥判官，遷晉、鄭二州刺史。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en appointed him judge on the Hebei deputy commander's staff; he was transferred to govern Jin and Zheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en named him judge to the Hebei deputy command; he later governed Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 少遊長權變，所至一切幹濟，賄謝權幸，以是數遷。

translations.literal: Shaoyou excelled at expedients; wherever he went he managed every matter efficiently and bribed the powerful, and so shifted posts often.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou was skilled in shifts of fortune; in every post he made affairs run and paid off the powerful, and so climbed from office to office.

sentences.zh: 李抱玉表澤潞副使，為陳鄭留後。

translations.literal: Li Baoyu recommended him as Ze-Lu deputy commissioner; he became Chen-Zheng military governor in residence.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu nominated him Ze-Lu deputy commissioner; he served as Chen-Zheng acting governor.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，復奏為隴右行軍司馬，擢桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: In the Yongtai era he was again nominated as Longyou campaign staff officer and promoted to Guilin circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongtai period he was named Longyou campaign staff officer and then Guilin intendant.

sentences.zh: 少遊不樂遠去，規徙近鎮。

translations.literal: Shaoyou disliked a distant posting and schemed to move to a nearer command.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou hated exile to the far south and plotted a transfer to a nearer post.

sentences.zh: 時宦官董秀有寵，掌樞近，少遊乃宿其裏，候歸沐，入謁，因鄙語諂謂秀曰：「七郎親屬幾何？

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Dong Xiu was favored and held the inner pivot; Shaoyou lodged in his lane, waited until he returned from bathing, entered to pay court, and in coarse flattery said to Xiu: "Seventh Lord, how many kin do you have?
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Dong Xiu then held the emperor's ear. Shaoyou stayed in his quarter, caught him after his bath, and in blunt flattery asked, "Seventh Lord, how large is your clan?

sentences.zh: 月費幾何？」

translations.literal: How much do you spend each month?"
translations.idiomatic: What does a month cost you?"

sentences.zh: 秀謝曰：「族甚大，歲用常過百萬。」

translations.literal: Xiu declined: "The clan is very large; yearly outlay often exceeds a million."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu demurred, "The family is vast; yearly expenses often pass a million."

sentences.zh: 少遊曰：「審如是，奉入不足為數日費，當數外營乃辦耳。

translations.literal: Shaoyou said: "If that is so, your salary cannot cover even a few days' expense—you must raise funds outside to make ends meet.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou said, "Then your stipend will not last a week—you must raise money on the side.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不才，請獨取濟，歲輸錢五千萬。

translations.literal: Though I am without talent, let me alone supply your needs: fifty million cash each year.
translations.idiomatic: I am no great man, but I can keep you supplied—fifty million cash a year.

sentences.zh: 今具其半，請先入之。」

translations.literal: I now have half ready; please accept it in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Half is ready now; please take it first."

sentences.zh: 秀大喜，與厚相結。

translations.literal: Xiu was greatly pleased and bonded with him in deep friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was delighted and tied himself to Shaoyou in close alliance.

sentences.zh: 少遊因泣曰：「嶺南瘴癘，恐不得生還見顏色。」

translations.literal: Shaoyou wept and said: "The miasma of Lingnan—I fear I shall never return alive to see your face again."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou wept, "Lingnan's pestilence—I may never come back alive to see you."

sentences.zh: 秀遽曰：「公美才，不當遠出，請少待。」

translations.literal: Xiu said at once: "Your talent is too fine for distant exile; wait a little."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said at once, "A man of your gifts should not be sent so far—wait awhile."

sentences.zh: 時少遊已納賂元載子仲武，於是內外更薦之，改宣歙池觀察使。

translations.literal: By then Shaoyou had already bribed Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu; inside and outside court they pressed his name again and he was made Xuán-Qi-Chí intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He had already paid Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu; with inside and outside recommendation he was shifted to Xuan-She-Chi intendant.

sentences.zh: 大歷五年，徙浙東，封潁川縣子，遷淮南節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali he was moved to Zhedong, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yingchuan, and made Huainan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 5 he was transferred to Zhedong, enfeoffed Viscount of Yingchuan, and made Huainan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 喜譎數，行小惠，群吏任職。

translations.literal: He loved intrigue and small kindnesses; subordinates were left to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in schemes and petty favors and let his clerks handle their posts.

sentences.zh: 三總藩，皆天下富饒處，以是斂求貿易無虛日，積財寶巨億萬。

translations.literal: Three times he headed a province, each among the empire's richest; levies and trade filled every day without pause, and his hoard ran to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he governed the richest circuits in the realm; tolls and trade never rested, and his treasure mounted to hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 初結元載，賂金帛歲無慮十萬緡；

translations.literal: At first he attached himself to Yuan Zai and sent gold and silk gifts yearly of no less than a hundred thousand strings;
translations.idiomatic: He first courted Yuan Zai with yearly gifts of gold and silk worth at least a hundred thousand strings;

sentences.zh: 又事宦官駱奉先、劉清潭、吳承倩及秀，故能久其任。

translations.literal: he also cultivated the eunuchs Luo Fengxian, Liu Qingtan, Wu Chengqian, and Xiu, and therefore held office long.
translations.idiomatic: he also served the eunuchs Luo Fengxian, Liu Qingtan, Wu Chengqian, and Xiu, and so kept his post for years.

sentences.zh: 後載以過見疑，少遊亦疏之。

translations.literal: Later Zai fell under suspicion for faults, and Shaoyou too distanced himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai later fell under suspicion, Shaoyou drew away as well.

sentences.zh: 載子伯和謫揚州，少遊陽善之，陰奏其罪，代宗以為忠。

translations.literal: Zai's son Bohe was banished to Yangzhou; Shaoyou feigned kindness while secretly memorializing his crimes, and Daizong took this for loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zai's son Bohe was exiled to Yangzhou; Shaoyou played the friend while denouncing him in secret, and Daizong read it as loyalty.

sentences.zh: 建中初，朝廷經費不充，始請本道稅錢千增二百，鹽鬥加百錢，度支因請諸道並增焉。

translations.literal: Early in Jianzhong the court's funds ran short; it first asked this circuit to add two hundred per thousand on tax cash and a hundred cash per salt peck; the Revenue Board then asked every circuit to do the same.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong the treasury ran dry; this circuit was first told to add two hundred per thousand in tax and a hundred cash per peck of salt, and the Revenue Board soon demanded the same everywhere.

sentences.zh: 李納拒命，少遊出師收徐、海等州，俄棄之，退屯盱眙。

translations.literal: Li Na defied orders; Shaoyou marched to recover Xu, Hai, and other prefectures but soon abandoned them and withdrew to garrison at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na rebelled, Shaoyou marched to retake Xu, Hai, and neighboring prefectures, then dropped them and fell back on Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 累進檢校尚書左僕射，賜封戶三百，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to Acting Minister of the Left, granted three hundred fief households, and named Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Acting Minister of the Left, received three hundred fief households, and was made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時宰相關播、盧杞與少遊有雅故，故驟兼臺司。

translations.literal: The chancellors Guan Bo and Lu Qi were old friends of Shaoyou's, and so he swiftly gained a post at court as well.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Guan Bo and Lu Qi were his intimates, and so he suddenly held a seat in the central government too.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，度支汴東兩稅使包佶寓揚州，所儲財賦八百萬緡將輸京師，少遊意朱泚勢盛，不遽平，欲肋取其財，使判官崔䪻就佶索文簿，貸二百萬緡。

translations.literal: When Dezong fled to Fengtian, Bao Jie, commissioner for the Bian and Eastern dual-tax revenues, was lodged at Yangzhou with eight million strings in stored wealth bound for the capital. Shaoyou thought Zhu Ci too strong to be crushed soon and wanted to extort the funds; he sent judge Cui Bei to demand Jie's ledgers and borrow two million strings.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong withdrew to Fengtian, Bao Jie, commissioner for Bian and eastern dual-tax revenues, lay at Yangzhou with eight million strings bound for the capital. Shaoyou judged Zhu Ci too strong to fall quickly and meant to seize the hoard; he sent his judge Cui Bei to demand Jie's books and "borrow" two million strings.

sentences.zh: 佶以非敕命，拒之。

translations.literal: Jie refused, citing lack of imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Jie refused—there was no edict.

sentences.zh: 䪻怒曰：「君善，得為劉長卿；

translations.literal: Bei raged: "If you are good you may be like Liu Changqing;
translations.idiomatic: Bei snarled, "Behave, and you may end like Liu Changqing;

sentences.zh: 不爾，為崔眾矣！」

translations.literal: if not, you will be like Cui Zhong!
translations.idiomatic: misbehave, and you will be Cui Zhong!"

sentences.zh: 長卿嘗任租庸使，為吳仲孺所囚，崔眾以倨李光弼被殺，故䪻以為言。

translations.literal: Changqing had served as Rent and Corvée commissioner and was imprisoned by Wu Zhongru; Cui Zhong was killed for insolence toward Li Guangbi—hence Bei's threat.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing had been Rent and Corvée commissioner and was jailed by Wu Zhongru; Cui Zhong was executed for defying Li Guangbi—hence the threat.

sentences.zh: 佶謁少遊，欲諫止，不得語，即遣去，於是財用悉為少遊所掠。

translations.literal: Jie called on Shaoyou hoping to remonstrate but could not get a word in and was sent away; the wealth was entirely seized by Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Jie came to plead and could not speak; he was dismissed, and every coin went to Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 佶奔白沙，少遊遣幕中房孺復召之。

translations.literal: Jie fled to Baisha; Shaoyou sent his staff officer Fang Rufu to summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: Jie fled to Baisha; Shaoyou sent Fang Rufu of his staff to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 佶驚走度江，伏妻子案牘中以免。

translations.literal: Jie fled in panic across the river and hid wife and children among the document cases to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Jie ran across the river in terror and hid wife and children among the document chests to slip away.

sentences.zh: 佶有禦遏兵三千，令高越、元甫將焉，少遊奪之。

translations.literal: Jie had three thousand blocking troops under Gao Yue and Yuanfu; Shaoyou seized them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's three thousand blocking troops under Gao Yue and Yuanfu were taken over by Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 能隨佶者，至上元，復為韓滉所留。

translations.literal: Those who could follow Jie reached Shangyuan but were detained again by Han Huang.
translations.idiomatic: The handful who stayed with Jie reached Shangyuan and were held again by Han Huang.

sentences.zh: 佶但諸史如江、鄂州，以表內蠟丸以聞。

translations.literal: Jie sent only junior clerks to Jiang and Ezhou, reporting inside wax pellets sewn into memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Jie sent only minor clerks to Jiang and E prefectures, smuggling memorials in wax pellets.

sentences.zh: 會少遊使至，帝詰其事，辭以不知。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou's envoy arrived, the emperor questioned the affair and was told Shaoyou knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou's messenger came, the emperor asked after the seizure and was told Shaoyou knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 時禍難煽結，帝未能制，乃曰：「少遊，國守臣，取佶之財，防它盜耳，庸何傷！」

translations.literal: Disaster was spreading and the emperor could not yet restrain him, so he said: "Shaoyou is a pillar of the realm; taking Jie's wealth is only to keep it from other robbers—what harm in that!"
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion was spreading and the throne could not yet curb him, so the emperor said, "Shaoyou guards the state; taking Jie's funds only keeps them from worse thieves—what injury is there?"

sentences.zh: 遠近聞之，咸稱帝得其機雲。

translations.literal: Near and far heard this and all praised the emperor for reading the moment aright.
translations.idiomatic: Men near and far heard it and praised the emperor for seizing the moment with subtle judgment.

sentences.zh: 少遊聞之，果自安不疑。

translations.literal: Shaoyou heard it and was indeed reassured without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou heard the words and took comfort, suspecting nothing.

sentences.zh: 李希烈陷汴，聲言襲江淮。

translations.literal: Li Xilie took Bian and announced he would strike the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie seized Bian and threatened to sweep the Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 少遊懼，遣參謀溫述送款曰：「豪、壽、舒、廬，既韜刃卷鎧，惟君命。」

translations.literal: Shaoyou was afraid and sent staff officer Wen Shu with submission: "Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu have sheathed blade and furled armor—we await your command alone."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou, afraid, sent staff officer Wen Shu with surrender: "Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu have sheathed sword and stowed armor—we wait only on your command."

sentences.zh: 又使巡官趙詵如鄆州，厚結李納。

translations.literal: He also sent touring officer Zhao Shen to Yanzhou to bind Li Na with rich favors.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent touring officer Zhao Shen to Yanzhou to buy Li Na with heavy gifts.

sentences.zh: 希烈僭號，遣將楊豐賫偽赦令送少遊。

translations.literal: Xilie assumed imperial style and sent general Yang Feng bearing a false amnesty to Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie took the imperial title and sent Yang Feng with a forged amnesty for Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 壽州刺史張建封邏得之，斬豐，以偽赦送行在。

translations.literal: Shou prefect Zhang Jianfeng intercepted him in patrol, beheaded Feng, and sent the false amnesty to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Shou prefect Zhang Jianfeng caught him on patrol, killed Feng, and forwarded the forged amnesty to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 會佶入朝，具言少遊脅財賦狀。

translations.literal: When Jie came to court he detailed Shaoyou's extortion of revenues.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie reached court he laid out how Shaoyou had extorted the treasury.

sentences.zh: 少遊慚，上表言所取以贍軍興，請償之。

translations.literal: Ashamed, Shaoyou memorialized that what he had taken went to army expenses and asked to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Shaoyou memorialized that the money had gone to the war effort and offered repayment.

sentences.zh: 而州府殘破，不能償，乃與腹心吏設法重稅，民皆苦之。

translations.literal: But prefecture and circuit were ruined and could not repay; he and trusted clerks devised new heavy taxes and the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit lay in ruins and could not pay; he and his trusted clerks invented crushing levies until the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 劉洽取汴州，得希烈偽起居註，書「某月日，陳少遊上表歸順。」

translations.literal: Liu Qia captured Bianzhou and obtained Xilie's forged court diary, which recorded "On such-and-such a day Chen Shaoyou submitted a memorial of submission."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia took Bianzhou and found Xilie's forged court diary, which read, "On such-and-such a day Chen Shaoyou memorialized his submission."

sentences.zh: 少遊聞，羞悸發病死，年六十一，贈太尉。

translations.literal: On hearing this Shaoyou died of shame and shock at sixty-one; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached him, shame and dread killed him at sixty-one; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：懷恩與賊百戰，闔宗死事至四十六人，遂汛掃燕、趙無餘埃，功高威重，不能防患，凶德根於心，弗得其所輒發，果於犯上，惜哉！

translations.literal: The commentator says: Huai'en fought the rebels in a hundred battles; his whole clan died in service to forty-six persons; he then swept Yan and Zhao without a speck of dust remaining. Merit was high and authority heavy, yet he could not guard against disaster; vicious virtue took root in the heart, and when he did not get his way he erupted—bold in violating superiors—alas!
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal runs: Huai'en battled rebels a hundred times; forty-six of his clan died in the cause; he scoured Yan and Zhao clean. Such merit, such weight—and still he could not ward off ruin. Cruelty rooted in his heart; denied his will, he struck upward. A pity!

sentences.zh: 其母拔刀逐賊，烈婦人也。

translations.literal: His mother drew a blade to drive off the enemy—a woman of fierce honor.
translations.idiomatic: His mother seized a knife and chased the foe—a heroine in her own right.

sentences.zh: 懷光提萬眾，振天子於難，一為讒人所沮，忿戾不自還，身首殊分，然讒人亦可疾矣，所謂「交亂四國」者也。

translations.literal: Huai'guang raised ten thousand men and rescued the Son of Heaven in peril; once thwarted by slanderers he turned wrathful and could not turn back; body and head were separated—yet the slanderers too are to be detested. This is what is called "stirring chaos in four states."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang led ten thousand men and pulled the emperor from peril; one whisper from court turned his fury inward until he could not retreat; head and trunk were parted—yet those who whispered deserve blame as well. As the saying has it, they "threw four realms into turmoil."

sentences.zh: 李锜，淄川王孝同五世孫。

translations.literal: Li Qi—Li Qi was fifth-generation descendant of Prince Xiaotong of Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Xiaotong of Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 以父國貞蔭調鳳翔府參軍。

translations.literal: By his father Guozhen's privilege he was appointed staff officer at Fengxiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father Guozhen's yin privilege he entered service as an officer at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，遷至宗正少卿。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan he rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he became Vice Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 嘗與卿李幹爭議，锜以直不坐，德宗兩置之。

translations.literal: Once he disputed with Court Gentleman Li Gan; Qi was not punished for his bluntness and Dezong set the matter aside twice.
translations.idiomatic: He once quarreled with Court Gentleman Li Gan; Qi's bluntness went unpunished, and Dezong dropped the case twice.

sentences.zh: 自雅王傅出為杭、湖二州刺史。

translations.literal: Leaving the post of tutor to the Prince of Ya, he became prefect of Hang and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the tutorship of the Prince of Ya, he governed Hang and Hu.

sentences.zh: 方李齊運用事，锜以賂結其歡，居三歲，遷潤州刺史、浙西觀察、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: While Li Qiyun held power Qi bribed his favor; after three years he was made Runzhou prefect, Zhexi intendant, and salt-and-iron transport commissioner for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Qiyun ruled the inner court, Qi bought his goodwill; in three years he was Runzhou prefect, Zhexi intendant, and commissioner of salt, iron, and transport for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 多積奇寶，歲時奉獻，德宗昵之。

translations.literal: He amassed rare treasures and sent them as seasonal gifts; Dezong grew fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: He hoarded curios and sent them as seasonal tribute; Dezong grew fond of him.

sentences.zh: 锜因恃恩驁橫，天下攉酒漕運，锜得專之，故朝廷用事臣，锜以利交，餘皆乾沒於私，國計日耗。

translations.literal: Emboldened by favor he turned arrogant; the empire's wine monopoly and transport fell entirely to him, so court ministers in power traded profit with Qi while the rest was swallowed for private gain and state revenues dwindled daily.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk on favor, he turned arrogant; the realm's wine monopoly and canal transport passed wholly into his hands. Ministers in power traded profit with him; the rest he skimmed, and the treasury thinned day by day.

sentences.zh: 浙西布衣崔善貞上書闕下暴其罪，帝械以賜锜；

translations.literal: Commoner Cui Shanzhen of Zhexi memorialized at the gate exposing his crimes; the emperor had him fettered and given to Qi;
translations.idiomatic: A Zhexi commoner, Cui Shanzhen, petitioned at the palace gate to expose his crimes; the emperor had him shackled and handed over to Qi;

sentences.zh: 锜豫浚大坎，至則並械瘞坎中，聞者切齒。

translations.literal: Qi had dug a great pit in advance; on arrival he buried him still in irons in the pit, and those who heard gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had already dug a deep pit; when Cui arrived he was buried in his chains, and listeners ground their teeth in rage.

sentences.zh: 锜得志，無所憚，圖久安計，乃益募兵，選善射者為一屯，號「挽硬隨身」，以胡、奚雜類虬須者為一將，號「蕃落健兒」，皆锜腹心，稟給十倍，使號锜為假父，故樂為其用。

translations.literal: Flush with success and fearless, Qi plotted a lasting hold: he recruited more troops, picked marksmen for one battalion called "Draw-Hard Bodyguard," and men of mixed Hu and Xi with bristling whiskers for another called "Tribal Toughs"—all his intimates, paid tenfold rations, made to call him foster father, and so eager to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in power and afraid of nothing, he planned for the long term: he raised more troops, formed a corps of crack archers called "Draw-Hard Personal Guard," and another of Hu and Xi men with fierce beards called "Frontier Braves"—all his creatures, paid tenfold, taught to call him foster father, and glad to obey.

sentences.zh: 帝於是復鎮海軍，以锜為節度使，罷領鹽鐵轉運。

translations.literal: The emperor then restored the Zhenhai army command, made Qi its commissioner, and removed him from salt-and-iron transport.
translations.idiomatic: The court then restored the Zhenhai army, made Qi its commissioner, and stripped him of the transport post.

sentences.zh: 锜喜得節，而忘其權去，暴踞日甚，屬吏死不以過甚眾；

translations.literal: Qi rejoiced in gaining the commission but forgot his authority was departing; his violent dominance grew daily, and many subordinates were put to death without real offense;
translations.idiomatic: Delighted with his new commission, Qi forgot that real power was slipping away. His tyranny deepened by the day, and he executed subordinates on slight pretexts until the toll was enormous.

sentences.zh: 又逼汙良家，寮佐力諫不能得，遽遁去。

translations.literal: He also forced himself on respectable families; staff urged him strenuously without effect and fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: He preyed on respectable households as well. His aides pleaded with all their strength and gained nothing, then fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，不假借方鎮，故倔強者稍稍入朝。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne he indulged military commissioners no longer, so the stubborn ones gradually came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong's accession brought no more indulgence for recalcitrant governors, and the stiff-necked among them began drifting back to court.

sentences.zh: 锜不自安，亦三請覲。

translations.literal: Qi felt ill at ease and thrice requested an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Qi asked three times to be received at court.

sentences.zh: 有詔拜尚書左僕射，以御史大夫李元素代之。

translations.literal: An edict made him Minister of the Left and replaced him with Censor-in-Chief Li Yuansu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named him Minister of the Left and sent Censor-in-Chief Li Yuansu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 中使馳驛勞問，兼撫慰其軍。

translations.literal: A palace envoy came at post-horse speed with condolences and to soothe his army.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy raced the post roads with greetings and orders to reassure the army.

sentences.zh: 锜署判官王淡為留後。

translations.literal: Qi appointed his judge Wang Dan acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Qi named his chief judge Wang Dan acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 锜無入朝意，稱疾遷延不即行。

translations.literal: Qi had no mind to enter court, pleaded illness, and delayed without departing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had no intention of going to the capital. He pleaded illness and lingered.

sentences.zh: 淡及中使數趣之，锜不悅，乘淡視事有所變更者，諷親兵圖淡。

translations.literal: Dan and the envoy urged him repeatedly; Qi was displeased, and when Dan in conducting affairs made changes, he hinted to his personal troops to plot against Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and the envoy pressed him again and again until Qi grew angry. When Dan altered something in the course of business, Qi whispered to his personal guard to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 因給冬服，锜坐幄中，以挽硬、蕃落自衛，淡與中使入謁，既出，眾持刃謾罵，殺淡食之。

translations.literal: On the occasion of issuing winter uniforms Qi sat in his tent screened by Draw-Hard and Tribal guards; when Dan and the envoy came to pay respects and had left, the crowd drew blades with abuse, killed Dan, and ate him.
translations.idiomatic: At the distribution of winter kit Qi sat in his pavilion behind Draw-Hard and Tribal troops. Dan and the envoy came in to pay their respects; once they had left, the men drew steel, cursed them, killed Dan, and devoured his body.

sentences.zh: 監軍使遣牙將趙琦慰諭，又食之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor sent military adjutant Zhao Qi to console them; he too was killed and eaten.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor sent adjutant Zhao Qi to calm the troops. They killed and ate him as well.

sentences.zh: 以兵註中使頸，锜陽驚扈解，乃囚別館。

translations.literal: They held blades to the envoy's neck; Qi feigned shock and escorted him away, then detained him in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Blades were laid to the envoy's throat. Qi pretended alarm, escorted him aside, and then held him prisoner in a guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 蕃落兵，薛頡主之；

translations.literal: The Tribal troops were commanded by Xue Jie;
translations.idiomatic: The Tribal corps answered to Xue Jie;

sentences.zh: 挽硬兵，李鈞主之。

translations.literal: the Draw-Hard by Li Jun.
translations.idiomatic: the Draw-Hard to Li Jun.

sentences.zh: 又以公孫玠、韓運分總餘軍。

translations.literal: Gongsun Jie and Han Yun were set to divide command of the remaining forces.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Jie and Han Yun were given joint command of the rest of the army.

sentences.zh: 室五劍，授管內鎮將，令殺五州刺史。

translations.literal: He housed five swords, granted them to territorial garrison commanders, and ordered them to kill the five prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He kept five swords on hand, gave them to the circuit's garrison commanders, and ordered the five prefects killed.

sentences.zh: 屬別將庾伯良兵三千築石頭城，謀據江左。

translations.literal: He assigned deputy general Yu Bolang three thousand men to build Stone City, plotting to hold the lower Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He put deputy commander Yu Bolang in charge of three thousand men to raise Stone City, intending to seize the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 常州刺史顏防用其客李雲謀，矯詔稱招討副使，殺鎮將李深，傳檄蘇、杭、湖、睦四州同討锜。

translations.literal: Changzhou prefect Yan Fang used his retainer Li Yun's plan, forged an edict styling himself deputy pacification commissioner, killed garrison commander Li Shen, and issued proclamations calling Su, Hang, Hu, and Mu to join in attacking Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou prefect Yan Fang took a scheme from his client Li Yun, forged an edict naming himself deputy pacification commissioner, killed garrison commander Li Shen, and called on Su, Hang, Hu, and Mu to march against Qi.

sentences.zh: 湖州辛秘亦殺鎮將趙惟忠。

translations.literal: In Huzhou Xin Mi also killed garrison commander Zhao Weizhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Huzhou, Xin Mi killed garrison commander Zhao Weizhong as well.

sentences.zh: 而蘇州李素為鎮將姚誌安所執，釘舷上，獻於锜，锜敗而免。

translations.literal: But Suzhou's Li Su was seized by garrison commander Yao Zhian, nailed to the gunwale, and presented to Qi—Qi fell before he could act and Li Su was spared.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzhou, Li Su was taken by garrison commander Yao Zhian, nailed to a boat's side, and sent up to Qi. Qi fell before the order could be carried out, and Li Su survived.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以淮南節度使王鍔為諸道行營兵馬招討處置使，中官薛尚衍為都監招討宣慰使，發宣武、武寧、武昌、淮南、宣歙、江西、浙東兵，自宣、杭、信三州進討。

translations.literal: Xianzong made Huainan Military Commissioner Wang E grand pacification and disposal commissioner for all circuits' armies, eunuch Xue Shangyan director and pacification envoy, and launched troops from Xuanwu, Wuning, Wuchang, Huainan, Xuan-She, Jiangxi, and Zhedong to advance from Xuan, Hang, and Xin in joint attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong named Huainan commissioner Wang E overall pacification commissioner, made eunuch Xue Shangyan his overseer and consolation envoy, and sent armies from Xuanwu, Wuning, Wuchang, Huainan, Xuan-She, Jiangxi, and Zhedong to close from Xuan, Hang, and Xin.

sentences.zh: 初，锜以宣州富饒，遣四院隨身兵馬使張子良、李奉仙、田少卿領兵三千分下宣、歙、池，锜甥裴行立雖預謀，而欲效順，故相與約還兵執锜，行立應於內。

translations.literal: Earlier Qi, because Xuanzhou was rich, had sent Four-Yard personal guard envoys Zhang Ziliang, Li Fengxian, and Tian Shaoqing with three thousand men into Xuan, She, and Chi; his nephew Pei Xingli had joined the plot yet wished to submit, so they agreed to return with the troops and seize Qi while Xingli acted within.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had thought Xuanzhou rich and sent Zhang Ziliang, Li Fengxian, and Tian Shaoqing of his Four-Yard guard with three thousand men into Xuan, She, and Chi. His nephew Pei Xingli had helped plan the revolt but meant to turn loyal, so they agreed to bring the troops back, seize Qi, and let Xingli strike from inside.

sentences.zh: 子良等既行，其夕，諭軍中曰：「僕射反矣，精兵四面皆至，常、湖鎮將幹首通衢，勢蹙且敗，吾輩徒死，不如轉禍希福。」

translations.literal: After Ziliang and the rest had marched out, that evening he addressed the army: "The Commissioner has rebelled. Elite troops are closing in on every side; Chang and Hu garrison commanders hang severed heads in the thoroughfares. We are cornered and doomed. To die for nothing is folly—better turn disaster into fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The night they marched out, Ziliang told the troops: "The Commissioner has rebelled. Crack armies are closing in from every quarter; Chang and Hu have garrison heads on poles in the streets. We're trapped and finished. A pointless death gains nothing—better trade ruin for reward."

sentences.zh: 部眾大悅，遂回趣城。

translations.literal: The host was greatly pleased and turned back toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: The men roared approval and wheeled back on the city.

sentences.zh: 行立舉火，內外合噪，行立攻牙門。

translations.literal: Xingli raised fire; inside and outside joined in clamor; Xingli attacked the headquarters gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xingli lit signal fires. Inside and out the camp erupted. He stormed the headquarters gate.

sentences.zh: 锜大驚，左右曰：「城外兵馬至。」

translations.literal: Qi was greatly alarmed; those beside him said: "Outside the walls horsemen have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Qi panicked. Someone at his side said, "Horsemen are outside the walls."

sentences.zh: 锜曰：「何人邪？」

translations.literal: Qi said: "Who are they?"
translations.idiomatic: "Who?" Qi demanded."

sentences.zh: 曰：「張中丞也。」

translations.literal: They said: "Vice Commissioner Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: "Vice Commissioner Zhang," came the answer."

sentences.zh: 锜怒甚，曰：「門外兵何人也？」

translations.literal: Qi was furious and said: "Who are the men outside the gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi, enraged, asked, "And who stands at the gate?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「裴侍御也。」

translations.literal: They said: "Attendant Pei."
translations.idiomatic: "Attendant Pei," they said."

sentences.zh: 锜拊膺曰：「行立亦叛吾邪！」

translations.literal: Qi clutched his breast and said: "Has Xingli betrayed me too!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi struck his chest. "Xingli has turned on me as well!"

sentences.zh: 跣足逃於女樓下。

translations.literal: He fled barefoot to the women's quarters below.
translations.idiomatic: Barefoot, he ran to the women's pavilion below.

sentences.zh: 李鈞引兵三百趨出庭院格鬥，行立兵貫出其中，斬鈞，傳首城下。

translations.literal: Li Jun led three hundred men rushing into the courtyard to fight; Xingli's troops pierced through them, beheaded Jun, and sent the head below the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jun rushed three hundred men into the courtyard to fight. Xingli's soldiers cut through them, took Jun's head, and flung it over the wall.

sentences.zh: 锜聞之，舉族慟哭。

translations.literal: When Qi heard it, the whole clan wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi heard the news and his household broke into wailing.

sentences.zh: 子良以監軍命曉諭城中逆順，且呼锜束身還朝，左右以幕縋而出之。

translations.literal: Ziliang, by the army supervisor's order, called through the city on loyalty and rebellion and summoned Qi to bind himself and return to court; attendants lowered him with a curtain rope.
translations.idiomatic: By the supervisor's commission Ziliang preached loyalty and treason through the streets and called on Qi to surrender for the capital. His men let him down on ropes from a canopy.

sentences.zh: 锜以僕射召，數日而反狀至，下詔削官爵，明日而敗，送京師。

translations.literal: Qi was summoned as Minister; within days word of rebellion arrived, an edict stripped rank and title, and on the morrow he was defeated and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had been summoned as Minister of the Left. Within days his rebellion was reported; an edict stripped his offices. The next day he was broken and sent east to the capital.

sentences.zh: 神策兵自長樂驛護至闕下，帝御興安門問罪，對曰：「張子良教臣反，非臣意也。」

translations.literal: Shence troops escorted him from Changle Post to below the palace gate; the emperor sat at Xing'an Gate to question his crime. Qi answered: "Zhang Ziliang taught me to rebel—it was not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Shence guards brought him from Changle Post to the palace. The emperor sat at Xing'an Gate to hear his crime. Qi said, "Zhang Ziliang urged me to rebel. It was never my wish."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾以宗臣為節度使，不能斬子良然後入朝邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You were a kinsman made military commissioner—could you not have beheaded Ziliang before coming to court?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You were a royal clansman made commissioner. Could you not have killed Ziliang before you came?"

sentences.zh: 锜不能對。

translations.literal: Qi could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had no reply.

sentences.zh: 以其日與子師回腰斬於城西南，年六十七。

translations.literal: That same day he and Zishi Hui were executed by waist-severing southwest of the city. He was sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: That day he and Zishi Hui were cut in two at the waist southwest of the walls. He was sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 屍數日，帝出黃衣二襲，葬以庶人禮。

translations.literal: After several days the emperor sent out two yellow robes and he was buried with commoner rites.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the emperor sent two yellow robes, and he was buried as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 擢子良檢校工部尚書、左金吾將軍，封南陽郡王，賜名奉國；

translations.literal: Ziliang was promoted Acting Minister of Works and Left Golden Guard general, enfeoffed Prince of Nanyang, and granted the name Fengguo;
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was made Acting Minister of Works and general of the Left Golden Guard, enfeoffed Prince of Nanyang, and given the name Fengguo;

sentences.zh: 田少卿檢校左散騎常侍、左羽林將軍，代國公；

translations.literal: Tian Shaoqing Acting Left Regular Attendant and Left Forest general, Duke of Dai;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shaoqing Acting Left Regular Attendant and Left Forest Guard general, Duke of Dai;

sentences.zh: 李奉仙檢校右常侍、右羽林將軍，邠國公；

translations.literal: Li Fengxian Acting Right Attendant and Right Forest general, Duke of Bin;
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengxian Acting Right Attendant and Right Forest Guard general, Duke of Bin;

sentences.zh: 裴行立泌州刺史。

translations.literal: Pei Xingli Bian prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingli was made prefect of Bian.

sentences.zh: 贈王淡給事中，趙琦和州刺史，崔善貞睦州司馬。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was posthumously made Supervising Secretary; Zhao Qi Hezhou prefect; Cui Shanzhen Muzhou aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was posthumously honored as Supervising Secretary; Zhao Qi made prefect of He; Cui Shanzhen made aide at Mu.

sentences.zh: 削锜屬籍，從弟宋州刺史铦、通事舍人銑、從子師偃流嶺南。

translations.literal: Qi's clan register was struck; his cousin Songzhou prefect Qian, Palace Service Officer Qian, and nephew Shiyan were exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was struck from the imperial genealogy. His cousin Songzhou prefect Qian, Palace Service Officer Qian, and nephew Shiyan were banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：語曰「出入之吝，謂之有司」，賤之也。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The saying runs, "Stinginess in outlay and intake is called keeping accounts"—it is contempt for petty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The proverb calls tightfisted bookkeeping "having a clerk's mind"—and means to despise it.

sentences.zh: 德宗平朱泚，京師府藏耗竭，諸道始有進奉助經費，而詔書亦往往宣索於天下。

translations.literal: After Dezong pacified Zhu Ci the capital treasury was drained; circuits first sent tribute to aid expenses, yet edicts also repeatedly demanded levies across the empire.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong crushed Zhu Ci, the capital stores were empty. Circuits began sending tribute to cover costs, yet edicts still reached everywhere with fresh demands.

sentences.zh: 以人主規規財利，下行有司之事，天下無事，賦取猶不息。

translations.literal: When the sovereign himself scrabbled for profit and descended to clerks' work, though the realm was at peace the levies never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Once the throne itself haggled over cash and did a clerk's work, peace brought no pause in exaction.

sentences.zh: 劍南、江西有日月之進，杜亞、劉贊、王緯及锜歲時進奉，以固其寵，號稱「賦外羨餘」。

translations.literal: Jiannan and Jiangxi sent monthly offerings; Du Ya, Liu Zan, Wang Wei, and Qi sent seasonal tribute yearly to secure favor, styled "surplus beyond the tax."
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan and Jiangxi sent monthly gifts. Du Ya, Liu Zan, Wang Wei, and Qi sent seasonal tribute to hold imperial favor, calling it "surplus beyond the levy."

sentences.zh: 又亦托中旨，以盜庫物。

translations.literal: They also used forged palace orders to plunder the storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: They also forged inner-court orders to loot the treasuries.

sentences.zh: 然獻才十二三，餘皆私之。

translations.literal: Yet only a tenth or twelfth reached the throne; the rest they kept.
translations.idiomatic: Only a tenth or so ever reached the emperor. The rest they kept.

sentences.zh: 江、淮以南，物力大屈，人人憔然忘生。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze and Huai, material strength was broken; every man looked haggard and forgot what living meant.
translations.idiomatic: South of the rivers, the land was bled white. Men grew gaunt and forgot what it was to live.

sentences.zh: 貞元以後，中官市物都下，謂之「宮市」，不持符牒，口含詔命，取濫縑惡布紅紫之，倍其估，裂以償直。

translations.literal: After Zhenyuan, palace eunuchs bought goods in the capital, called "palace market"; without warrants they carried oral edicts, took coarse silk and bad cloth dyed red and purple, doubled the price, and tore cloth to pay.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenyuan, eunuchs bought in the capital under the name "palace market." Without documents they spoke edicts from memory, seized cheap, shoddy cloth dyed scarlet and purple, doubled the valuation, and paid by ripping yardage.

sentences.zh: 市之良賈精貨，皆逃去不出；

translations.literal: Good merchants with fine goods all fled and would not appear;
translations.idiomatic: Honest traders with quality goods vanished from the stalls;

sentences.zh: 列廛闬者，惟粗雜苦窳而已。

translations.literal: those who lined the market had only coarse, shoddy rubbish.
translations.idiomatic: only coarse, worthless junk remained in the lanes.

sentences.zh: 又有強驅入禁中，罄所車輦，賣者不平，因共歐笞之。

translations.literal: There were also cases of forced entry into the forbidden palace, emptying whole carts; sellers who protested were beaten together.
translations.idiomatic: Some were driven into the palace and stripped of entire carts. Merchants who resisted were beaten in gangs.

sentences.zh: 蒼頭女奴，名馬工車，惴惴常畏捕取。

translations.literal: Servants and slave girls, famous horses and craftsmen's carts—all lived in constant fear of seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Servants, slave girls, prize horses, and craftsmen's wagons—all lived in dread of being taken.

sentences.zh: 而德宗蔽於左右前後，莫知也。

translations.literal: Yet Dezong was screened by those before and behind him and never knew.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong, walled in by attendants, never learned of it.

sentences.zh: 故善貞因锜並論其事，卒不知锜顓鹽鐵之利，以養兵圖叛，曾不及庸有司之吝遠甚。

translations.literal: Thus Shanzhen, linking Qi, spoke of these matters together, yet never grasped that Qi monopolized salt-and-iron profit to feed troops and plot rebellion—far worse than any petty clerk's stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: So Shanzhen, in denouncing Qi, spoke of these abuses together, yet never saw that Qi had seized the salt-and-iron monopoly to arm rebellion—a miserliness of petty clerks was nothing beside that.

sentences.zh: ◎叛臣下李忠臣李忠臣，本董秦也，幽州薊人。

translations.literal: ◎ Rebellious Ministers, Part Two — Li Zhongchen. Li Zhongchen was originally Dong Qin, a man of Ji in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Rebellious Ministers, Part Two — Li Zhongchen. Li Zhongchen had been Dong Qin, born in Ji, Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 少籍軍，以材力奮，事節度使薛楚玉、張守珪、安祿山等，甄勞至折沖郎將。

translations.literal: Young he entered the army and rose by strength; he served military commissioners Xue Chuyu, Zhang Shougui, An Lushan, and others, and through merit reached Colonel of the Broken-Charge.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the ranks young and fought his way up under commissioners Xue Chuyu, Zhang Shougui, An Lushan, and others until merit made him Colonel of the Broken Charge.

sentences.zh: 平盧軍先鋒使劉正臣殺偽節度呂知晦，擢秦兵馬使，攻長楊，戰獨山，襲榆關、北平，殺賊將申子貢、榮先欽，執周釗送京師。
