translations.literal: When Pinglu vanguard Liu Zhengchen killed the false commissioner Lü Zhihui, Qin was raised army commander; he attacked Changyang, fought at Dushan, raided Yuguan and Beiping, killed rebel generals Shen Zigong and Rong Xianqin, and sent Zhou Zhao captive to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Pinglu vanguard Liu Zhengchen killed the puppet commissioner Lü Zhihui, Qin became army commander. He stormed Changyang, fought at Dushan, hit Yuguan and Beiping, killed rebel generals Shen Zigong and Rong Xianqin, and sent Zhou Zhao to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 從正臣赴難，復敗李歸仁、李鹹、白秀芝等。

translations.literal: He followed Zhengchen in the emergency and again defeated Li Guiren, Li Xian, Bai Xiuzhi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhengchen in the crisis and again routed Li Guiren, Li Xian, Bai Xiuzhi, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 潼關失守，秦整軍北還。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass fell Qin gathered the army and marched north.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Pass fell, Qin drew the army north.

sentences.zh: 奚王阿篤孤初引眾與正臣合，已而紿約皆攻范陽，至後城，夜乘間襲秦。

translations.literal: The Xi king Adugu at first led his host to join Zhengchen, then deceived them with a pact to attack Fanyang together; reaching Houcheng he struck Qin by night in a gap.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi chieftain Adugu first marched with Zhengchen, then tricked him with talk of a joint strike on Fanyang. At Houcheng he hit Qin's camp in a night gap.

sentences.zh: 秦接戰，敗之，追奔至溫泉山，禽首領阿布離，斬以釁鼓。

translations.literal: Qin met the fight, defeated them, pursued to Wenquan Mountain, captured the chieftain Abu Li, and beheaded him to blood the drums.
translations.idiomatic: Qin met them, broke them, chased to Wenquan Mountain, seized the chieftain Abu Li, and beheaded him to stain the drums.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，節度使王玄誌使秦率兵三千自雍奴桴葦絕海，擊賊將石帝廷、烏承洽，轉戰累日，拔魯城、河間、景城，收糧貲以實軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide Commissioner Wang Xuanzhi sent Qin with three thousand men from Yongnu by raft and reed across the sea to strike rebel generals Shi Diting and Wu Chengqia, fighting day after day; he took Lucheng, Hejian, and Jingcheng and gathered grain stores to fill the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2, Commissioner Wang Xuanzhi sent Qin with three thousand men from Yongnu. They poled rafts of reeds across the sea, struck rebel generals Shi Diting and Wu Chengqia, and fought for days until Lucheng, Hejian, and Jingcheng fell. He seized grain to feed the host.

sentences.zh: 又與田神功下平原、樂安，禽偽刺史以獻。

translations.literal: With Tian Shengon he took Pingyuan and Le'an and presented the false prefects captive.
translations.idiomatic: With Tian Shengon he took Pingyuan and Le'an and sent the puppet prefects up as captives.

sentences.zh: 於是防河招討使李銑承制假秦德州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon River-Defense Pacification Commissioner Li Xian by provisional order made Qin Dezhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: River-Defense pacification commissioner Li Xian then named Qin prefect of De by emergency warrant.

sentences.zh: 史思明自歸，河南節度使張鎬督秦軍合諸將平河南州縣，與裨將陽惠元破安慶緒將王福德於舒舍，肅宗下詔褒諭，令屯濮州，又徙韋城。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming returned to allegiance, Henan Commissioner Zhang Hao directed Qin's army with other generals to pacify Henan's prefectures and counties; with lieutenant Yang Huiyuan he defeated An Qingxu's general Wang Fude at Shushe. Suzong issued praise and ordered him to garrison at Puzhou, then moved him to Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming submitted, Henan commissioner Zhang Hao led Qin's troops with other commanders to recover Henan's prefectures. With lieutenant Yang Huiyuan he beat An Qingxu's general Wang Fude at Shushe. Suzong praised him by edict and posted him at Pu, then at Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 從郭子儀圍相州，軍潰，秦至滎陽，破賊將敬釭，取糧艘二百柁以餉汴軍。

translations.literal: Following Guo Ziyi in the siege of Xiangzhou the army collapsed; Qin reached Xingyang, defeated rebel general Jing Gang, and took two hundred grain barges to feed the Bian army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Ziyi against Xiangzhou; when the army broke, Qin reached Xingyang, killed rebel general Jing Gang, and seized two hundred grain barges for the Bian force.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授濮州刺史，屯杏園渡。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Pu prefect and garrisoned at Xingyuan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named Pu prefect and held Xingyuan Ford.

sentences.zh: 許叔冀以汴下史思明，秦力屈，亦降。

translations.literal: When Xu Shuji faced Shi Siming below Bian, Qin's strength gave way and he too submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shuji faced Shi Siming below Bian, Qin's strength failed and he surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 思明撫背曰：「始吾有左手，得公今完矣！」

translations.literal: Siming clapped his back and said: "At first I had only my left hand—now with you it is whole!"
translations.idiomatic: Siming clapped his shoulder and said, "I once had only my left hand. With you I am whole again!"

sentences.zh: 與俱寇河陽，秦夜挈五百人冒圍歸李光弼。

translations.literal: Together they raided Heyang; Qin by night led five hundred men through the encirclement back to Li Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Heyang together. Qin slipped five hundred men through the lines by night and rejoined Li Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 詔加殿中監，封戶二百，召至京師，賜今氏名，給良馬、甲第。

translations.literal: An edict added Palace Supervisor, granted two hundred households, summoned him to the capital, bestowed his present surname, and gave fine horses and a mansion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Palace Supervisor, granted two hundred households, called him to court, gave him the surname he bears today, and rewarded him with fine horses and a house.

sentences.zh: 時陜西、神策兩節度使郭英乂、衛伯玉屯陜，故以忠臣為兩軍兵馬使，戰永寧、莎柵，與賊將李感義等數十遇，皆破之。

translations.literal: As Shaanxi and Shence commissioners Guo Yingyi and Wei Boyu were garrisoned at Shan, Zhongchen was made army commander of both forces; at Yongning and Shazha he met rebel generals Li Ganyi and others dozens of times and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: With Guo Yingyi and Wei Boyu holding Shan for Shaanxi and Shence, Zhongchen commanded both armies. At Yongning and Shazha he fought rebel generals like Li Ganyi dozens of times and won each clash.

sentences.zh: 淮西節度使王仲升為賊執，以忠臣為汝、仙、蔡六州節度使，兼安州。

translations.literal: When Huaixi Commissioner Wang Zhongsheng was captured by rebels, Zhongchen was made commissioner of Ru, Xian, Cai, and six other prefectures, with An added.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaixi commissioner Wang Zhongsheng was taken by rebels, Zhongchen was made commissioner of Ru, Xian, Cai, and six neighboring prefectures, with An added.

sentences.zh: 合諸軍平東都，進御史大夫。

translations.literal: Joining the allied armies he pacified the eastern capital and was advanced to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the allied armies that recovered the eastern capital and rose to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 回紇可汗既歸，留其下安恪、石帝廷居河陽守貲廥，因是招亡命為盜，道路畏澀。

translations.literal: After the Uyghur qaghan returned, his subordinates An Ke and Shi Diting remained at Heyang guarding stores; they recruited fugitives as bandits and the roads grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: After the Uyghur qaghan went home, his men An Ke and Shi Diting stayed at Heyang guarding depots. They drew deserters into banditry until travel grew perilous.

sentences.zh: 詔忠臣討定之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhongchen to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Zhongchen to crush them.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃犯京師，天子追兵，秦方宴鞠場，使者至，即整師引道。

translations.literal: When Tibetans struck the capital the Son of Heaven recalled troops; Qin was at the ball ground feasting when the messenger came and he at once formed ranks and marched.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet raided the capital the emperor recalled armies. Qin was feasting on the polo ground when the messenger arrived; he formed ranks at once and marched.

sentences.zh: 諸將白：「須良日。」

translations.literal: The generals said: "We must wait for an auspicious day."
translations.idiomatic: His officers said, "We must wait for a lucky day."

sentences.zh: 忠臣怒曰：「君父在難，方擇日救患乎？」

translations.literal: Zhongchen raged: "Our lord and father are in peril—shall we pick a day to save them?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen snapped, "The Son of Heaven is in danger, and you would choose a calendar day?"

sentences.zh: 時召兵無先忠臣至者。

translations.literal: At the summons no troops reached the emperor before Zhongchen.
translations.idiomatic: No summoned force reached the throne before his.

sentences.zh: 代宗嘉之，加本道觀察使，賚與倍等。

translations.literal: Daizong praised him, added intendant of his own circuit, and doubled his gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong praised him, made him intendant of his own circuit as well, and doubled his rewards.

sentences.zh: 周智光為帳下所殺，忠臣提兵入華州，所過大掠，自赤水距潼關二百里無居人。

translations.literal: When Zhou Zhiguang was killed by men under his tent Zhongchen led troops into Hua; wherever he passed he plundered heavily, and from Chishui to Tong Pass for two hundred li there was no one living.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Zhiguang was killed by his own men, Zhongchen marched into Hua and plundered every step. From Chishui to Tong Pass, two hundred li lay empty of inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 大歷五年，加蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali he was made Cai prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 5 he was named prefect of Cai.

sentences.zh: 陜虢李國清為下所逐，掠府庫，國清遍拜諸將乃免。

translations.literal: Shaan-Guo Li Guoqing was driven out by his subordinates, who looted the treasury; Guoqing bowed to every general before they spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guoqing of Shaan-Guo was expelled by his troops, who sacked the treasury. He bowed to each general in turn before they let him live.

sentences.zh: 會忠臣入朝，次陜，詔訊於眾。

translations.literal: When Zhongchen came to court he stopped at Shan; an edict questioned the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen came to court and halted at Shan. An edict put the matter to the troops.

sentences.zh: 眾懼忠臣，不敢搖，即圍棘，約士投所掠物圍中，一日盡獲。

translations.literal: The crowd feared Zhongchen and dared not stir; they ringed thorn hedges and pledged that whoever had looted would cast the goods into the ring; in one day all was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The men feared Zhongchen and would not move. They fenced a thorn ring and swore that anyone who had stolen must throw the goods inside. In a day everything was back.

sentences.zh: 討李靈耀也，戰西梁固，敗之。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Li Lingyao he fought at Xilianggu and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Li Lingyao, he fought at Xilianggu and won.

sentences.zh: 復與馬燧軍合，敗賊於汴州。

translations.literal: He joined Ma Sui's army and defeated the rebels at Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Ma Sui and broke the rebels at Bian.

sentences.zh: 田悅以援兵三萬屯汴郛，忠臣勒裨將李重倩夜率百騎襲之，貫其營而還，殺數十百人。

translations.literal: Tian Yue camped thirty thousand relief troops at the Bian suburbs; Zhongchen ordered lieutenant Li Chongqian to lead a hundred horsemen by night to strike them, pierced their camp, and returned, killing several tens and hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue held thirty thousand reinforcements outside Bian. Zhongchen sent lieutenant Li Chongqian with a hundred horsemen to strike by night, run their camp through, and withdraw, killing scores on the way.

sentences.zh: 悅間道走，靈耀開城亡去，軍遂潰。

translations.literal: Yue fled by a side road; Lingyao opened the city and fled; the army then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue slipped away by a back road. Lingyao opened the gates and ran. The rebel army dissolved.

sentences.zh: 以忠臣為汴州刺史，加檢校司空、同中書門下平章事，封西平郡王。

translations.literal: Zhongchen was made Bian prefect, added Acting Minister of Works and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen was named Bian prefect, made Acting Minister of Works and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 忠臣資婪沓嗜色，將士婦女逼與亂，所至人苦之。

translations.literal: Zhongchen was greedy, grasping, and lustful; he forced soldiers' wives to lie with him, and wherever he went people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen was greedy, grasping, and lecherous. He took soldiers' wives by force, and every place he touched groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 以女弟妻張惠光，用為牙將，恃勢殘克。

translations.literal: He married his younger sister to Zhang Huiguang and used him as military adjutant; relying on power he extorted cruelly.
translations.idiomatic: He married his younger sister to Zhang Huiguang and made him a camp adjutant. Backed by that tie, Huiguang robbed and bullied without mercy.

sentences.zh: 或白忠臣，不之信。

translations.literal: Someone informed Zhongchen, but he did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: People warned Zhongchen, but he would not believe them.

sentences.zh: 又以惠光子居牙下，愈橫肆。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Huiguang's son held a post under the adjutant staff, he became all the more violent and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Huiguang's son served on Zhongchen's staff, and grew even more brazen.

sentences.zh: 十四年，大將李希烈因眾怒，與少將丁暠、賈子華等共斬惠光父子，以兵脅逐忠臣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Grand General Li Xilie, rousing the troops' anger, together with junior generals Ding Hao, Jia Zihua, and others jointly beheaded Huiguang father and son, and with troops compelled Zhongchen to flee.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Li Xilie, the army's senior commander, stirred the men's wrath. With junior officers Ding Hao, Jia Zihua, and others he cut down Huiguang and his son, then drove Zhongchen out at spearpoint.

sentences.zh: 跳奔京師，帝素寵之，不責也。

translations.literal: He fled leaping to the capital; the emperor had always favored him and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He bolted for the capital. The emperor had always doted on him and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 復授檢校司空、同中書門下平章事，奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Acting Minister of Works, Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Acting Minister of Works, Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs, and a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，散騎常侍張涉以贓得罪，帝怒不赦。

translations.literal: When Dezong acceded, Imperial Attendant Zhang She was guilty of corruption; the emperor was angry and would not pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong took the throne, Imperial Attendant Zhang She was convicted of graft. The emperor was furious and refused mercy.

sentences.zh: 涉故侍讀東宮者，忠臣曰：「陛下貴為天子，先生以乏財觸法，非過也。」

translations.literal: She had formerly been tutor in the Eastern Palace. Zhongchen said: "Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven; the Master touched the law only for want of funds—it is not a fault.
translations.idiomatic: She had once been the crown prince's reader. Zhongchen said, "Your Majesty stands above all men as Son of Heaven. The Master broke the law only because he lacked money—that is no true crime."

sentences.zh: 帝意解，免涉歸田裏。

translations.literal: The emperor's mood eased; She was pardoned and sent home to the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger cooled. She was spared and sent back to her village.

sentences.zh: 湖南觀察使辛京杲私怒部曲，殺之，有司劾當死。

translations.literal: Hunan Observation Commissioner Xin Jinggao killed a soldier in private anger; the authorities impeached him as deserving death.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Jinggao, observation commissioner of Hunan, killed a soldier in a private fit of rage. The judicial offices charged him with a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 忠臣曰：「京杲應死久矣！」

translations.literal: Zhongchen said: "Jinggao ought to have died long ago!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen said, "Jinggao should have been put to death long ago!"

sentences.zh: 帝問故，對曰：「京杲諸父戰某所死，兄弟戰某所死，渠從行獨得存，以故知之。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked why. He replied: "Jinggao's uncles died fighting at such-and-such a place, his brothers died fighting at such-and-such a place; only he among those on campaign survived—I know it for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. He answered, "Jinggao's uncles fell in battle here, his brothers fell there. Of all who marched, only he came back alive. That is how I know."

sentences.zh: 帝淒然悟，釋之，下除王傅。

translations.literal: The emperor sadly understood, released him, and demoted him to Wang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grasped it with sorrow and set him free, demoting him to Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 忠臣戇直不通書。

translations.literal: Zhongchen was blunt and obstinate and did not understand books.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen was rough, obstinate, and illiterate.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂：「卿耳大，真貴兆。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said: "Your ears are large—a true mark of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him, "Your ears are large—a sure sign of high fortune."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞驢耳大，龍耳小。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I have heard that donkeys have large ears and dragons small ones.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have heard donkeys have large ears and dragons small ones."

sentences.zh: 帝喜其野而誠。

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in his rustic honesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased by his rustic candor.

sentences.zh: 然既失兵，怫郁不顧藉。

translations.literal: Yet having lost his army, he was sullen and heedless of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: But he had lost his command, and brooded in sullen disregard of decorum.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，偽署司空兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he was falsely appointed Minister of Works and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rose in rebellion, Ci gave him the false titles of Minister of Works and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 泚攻奉天，以忠臣居守。

translations.literal: When Ci attacked Fengtian, he had Zhongchen hold the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci marched on Fengtian, he left Zhongchen to hold Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 泚敗，系有司，與其子俱斬。

translations.literal: When Ci was defeated, he was held by the authorities and beheaded together with his son.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci fell, the authorities seized him and beheaded him with his son.

sentences.zh: 喬琳喬琳，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Qiao Lin—Qiao Lin was a man of Taiyuan, Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Lin. Qiao Lin came from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤苦誌學，擢進士第。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned and destitute, he devoted himself to learning and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he bent himself to study and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 性誕蕩無禮檢。

translations.literal: His nature was wild, dissolute, and without ritual restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He was reckless, dissolute, and without the least restraint of ritual.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀表為朔方府掌書記。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi recommended him as secretary of the Shuofang headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi recommended him as secretary at the Shuofang command.

sentences.zh: 與聯舍畢曜相掉訐，貶巴州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He crossed accusations with fellow lodger Bi Yao and was demoted to Ba prefecture Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: He traded accusations with his barracks-mate Bi Yao and was demoted to registrar of Ba prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷果、綿、遂、懷四州刺史，治寬簡，不親事。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Guo, Mian, Sui, and Huai; his governance was lenient and simple, and he did not attend to affairs personally.
translations.idiomatic: He held the prefectures of Guo, Mian, Sui, and Huai in turn. His rule was loose and light; he never troubled himself with the work.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂錄事參軍任紹業曰：「子綱紀一州，能劾刺史乎？」

translations.literal: He once said to Registrar Ren Shaoye: "You govern a whole prefecture—can you impeach the prefect?"
translations.idiomatic: He once asked his registrar Ren Shaoye, "You keep order for a whole prefecture. Could you impeach the prefect?"

sentences.zh: 紹業出條所失示之，驚曰：「能知吾失，御史材也。」

translations.literal: Shaoye brought out a list of his faults and showed them. He exclaimed: "To know my faults—material for the censorate."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoye produced a written list of his failings. Lin started in alarm. "To know my faults—that is censorate timber."

sentences.zh: 琳素善蒲人張涉。

translations.literal: Lin had long been on good terms with Zhang She of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had always been close to Zhang She of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 涉以國子博士侍太子讀，太子即位，召訪政事，不淹日，詔入翰林，遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: She, as a National University erudite, attended the crown prince's lectures; when the prince succeeded, he was summoned to discuss state affairs. Within days an edict brought him into the Hanlin Academy, and he was promoted to Imperial Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: She served the crown prince as a National University erudite. When the prince took the throne, he was called in to discuss policy. Within days an edict placed him in the Hanlin Academy, then made him Imperial Attendant.

sentences.zh: 薦琳任宰相，乃拜御史大夫、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He recommended Lin for the chancellorship; Lin was then appointed Censor-in-Chief and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Lin for the chancellorship. Lin was made Censor-in-Chief and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天下矍然駭之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven started in sudden alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was suddenly appalled.

sentences.zh: 琳年高且聵，每進封失次，所言不厭帝旨，在位閱八旬，以工部尚書罷。

translations.literal: Lin was old and hard of hearing; each time he presented memorials he lost the order, and what he said did not please the emperor. After eighty days in office he was dismissed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was elderly and deaf. His memorials came out of order, and his words never pleased the throne. After eighty days he was removed as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝由是亦疏涉。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby also grew distant from She.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew cool toward She as well.

sentences.zh: 琳從幸奉天，再遷太子少師；

translations.literal: Lin followed the court in flight to Fengtian and was twice promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Lin followed the emperor to Fengtian and was twice promoted, ending as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 進幸梁州，次盩厔，詭言馬殆不進。

translations.literal: When the court advanced to Liangzhou and halted at Zhouzhi, he falsely claimed his horse was exhausted and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the court pressed on to Liangzhou and stopped at Zhouzhi, he lied that his horse was spent and refused to go farther.

sentences.zh: 帝素以舊老禮之，給乘輿馬，辭病力。

translations.literal: The emperor had always treated him with the courtesy due an old minister and offered him an imperial carriage horse; he pleaded illness with great insistence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who had always honored him as an elder, offered a horse from the imperial train. Lin pleaded illness with stubborn force.

sentences.zh: 帝賜所執策曰：「勉為良圖，與卿別矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor gave him the whip he held and said: "Do your best—this is farewell!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed him the whip he carried and said, "Make what plans you can. This is where we part!"

sentences.zh: 不數日，祝髯發舍仙遊佛廬。

translations.literal: Within days he shaved his beard, let down his hair, and took lodging at the Xianyou Buddhist monastery.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he shaved his beard, unbound his hair, and moved into the Xianyou monastery.

sentences.zh: 泚聞，遣數十騎取之，署吏部尚書，令姻家源休衣以朝服，食以肉，琳亦不辭。

translations.literal: When Ci heard, he sent several dozen horsemen to fetch him, appointed him Minister of Personnel, had his in-law Yuan Xiu dress him in court robes, and fed him meat; Lin did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Ci heard and sent several dozen riders to seize him. He named him Minister of Personnel, had his kinsman by marriage Yuan Xiu robe him for court, and set meat before him. Lin accepted all of it.

sentences.zh: 士有訴官非便者，琳曰：「子謂此選便乎？」

translations.literal: When an official complained that his post was unsuitable, Lin said: "Do you think this appointment is suitable?
translations.idiomatic: When one official protested that his post was wrong, Lin said, "Do you call this selection fitting?"

sentences.zh: 及收京師，李晟憫其老，表貰死。

translations.literal: When the capital was recovered, Li Sheng pitied his age and memorialized to spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was retaken, Li Sheng pitied his years and petitioned to commute the death sentence.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「琳，故宰相，失節背義，不可赦。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Lin was once chancellor; he lost his integrity and turned against righteousness—he cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Lin was a former chancellor. He broke faith and betrayed the throne. He cannot be spared."

sentences.zh: 臨刑嘆曰：「我以七月七日生，以此日死，非命耶？」

translations.literal: At execution he sighed: "I was born on the seventh day of the seventh month; to die on this day—is it not fate?"
translations.idiomatic: On the scaffold he sighed, "I was born on the seventh day of the seventh month. To die on this day—is that not destiny?"

sentences.zh: 時又有蔣鎮者，洌子也，與兄鏈俱以文辭顯。

translations.literal: At that time there was also Jiang Zhen, son of Jiang Li, who with his elder brother Lian had won fame through literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time there was Jiang Zhen, son of Jiang Li. He and his elder brother Lian were known for their writing.

sentences.zh: 擢賢良方正科，累轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He passed the Exemplary and Direct recruitment examination and rose through remonstrance and policy posts.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Exemplary and Direct examination and advanced to remonstrance and policy offices.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，淫雨壞河中鹽池，味苦惡。

translations.literal: In the Dali era prolonged rain ruined the salt ponds of Hezhong; the brine turned bitter and foul.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dali, long rains wrecked the Hezhong salt pools and the brine turned bitter and foul.

sentences.zh: 韓滉判度支，慮減常賦，妄言池生瑞鹽，王德之美祥。

translations.literal: Han Huang, as fiscal commissioner, feared a cut in regular revenue and falsely claimed the ponds had produced auspicious salt—a fine omen from Heaven's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, judging fiscal affairs, feared the regular levy would fall. He falsely reported that the pools had yielded auspicious salt, a blessed sign of royal virtue.

sentences.zh: 代宗疑不然，命鎮馳驛按視。

translations.literal: Suzong doubted it and ordered Zhen to ride post-haste to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong doubted the story and sent Zhen by urgent relay to inspect on the spot.

sentences.zh: 鎮內欲結滉，故實其事，表置祠房，號池曰「寶應靈慶」雲。

translations.literal: Zhen wished inwardly to win Huang's favor, so he confirmed the tale, memorialized to build a shrine, and named the pool "Treasured Response, Spiritual Blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen meant to curry favor with Huang, so he swore the tale true, memorialized for a shrine, and named the pool "Treasured Response, Spiritual Blessing."

sentences.zh: 再進工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 妹婿源溥者，休弟也，故鎮與休交。

translations.literal: His sister's husband was Yuan Pu, younger brother of Yuan Xiu; thus Zhen was friendly with Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: His sister's husband was Yuan Pu, Xiu's younger brother, so Zhen was on close terms with Xiu.

sentences.zh: 泚叛，竄於鄠，傷足不能進。

translations.literal: When Ci rebelled, he fled into hiding at E and injured his foot so he could not go on.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci rebelled, he hid out in E, but a wounded foot kept him from fleeing farther.

sentences.zh: 泚先得鏈，而鎮左右逃歸，語所在，源休聞，白泚，以二百騎求得之。

translations.literal: Ci had already seized Lian; Zhen's attendants escaped back and told where he was. Xiu heard and informed Ci, who sent two hundred horsemen to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Ci had already taken Lian. Zhen's servants slipped away, reported his whereabouts, and Xiu told Ci. Two hundred riders were sent and found him.

sentences.zh: 知不免，懷刃將自刺，鏈止之。

translations.literal: Knowing he could not escape, he hid a blade to stab himself; Lian stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, he tucked a blade to kill himself. Lian restrained him.

sentences.zh: 復謀出奔，懦不決。

translations.literal: They plotted flight again, but cowardice left them unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted to run once more, but fear would not let them choose.

sentences.zh: 中朝臣遁伏者，休多所誅殺，賴鎮救原十五。

translations.literal: Court officials in hiding whom Xiu killed in great numbers—thanks to Zhen, fifteen were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu slaughtered many hidden court officials. Through Zhen's pleas, fifteen were spared.

sentences.zh: 初，洌與弟渙在安史時皆汙偽官，鏈兄弟復屈節於賊雲。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li and his younger brother Huan had both held false rebel offices in the An Lushan era; the Lian brothers again bowed to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li and his brother Huan had both taken false rebel posts in the An Lushan years, and the Lian brothers had again submitted to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 高駢高駢，字千里，南平郡王崇文孫也。

translations.literal: Gao Pian—Gao Pian, style name Qianli, was grandson of Prince Nanping, Chongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian. Gao Pian, style name Qianli, was grandson of Prince Nanping, Gao Chongwen.

sentences.zh: 家世禁衛，幼頗修飭，折節為文學，與諸儒交，硁硁譚治道，兩軍中人更稱譽之。

translations.literal: His family for generations served in the palace guard; in youth he was quite self-disciplined, bent his conduct toward letters, consorted with Confucian scholars, spoke obstinately of governing the Way, and men of both armies praised him ever more.
translations.idiomatic: His house had long served in the palace guards. As a youth he was strict with himself, turned to letters, kept company with scholars, lectured stubbornly on statecraft, and men in both armies praised him without end.

sentences.zh: 事朱叔明為司馬。

translations.literal: He served Zhu Shuming as military aide.
translations.idiomatic: He served Zhu Shuming as army secretary.

sentences.zh: 有二雕並飛，駢曰：「我且貴，當中之。」

translations.literal: Two hawks flew together; Pian said: "I am about to rise in honor—I shall strike the middle one.
translations.idiomatic: Two hawks flew side by side. Pian said, "I am soon to be exalted. I shall hit the one between."

sentences.zh: 一發貫二雕焉，眾大驚，號「落雕侍御」。

translations.literal: One shot pierced both hawks; the crowd was greatly startled and called him "Falling-Hawk Attendant."
translations.idiomatic: One arrow ran through both hawks. The company was thunderstruck and named him "Falling-Hawk Attendant."

sentences.zh: 後歷右神策軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Later he served as chief adjutant of the Right Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: He later became chief adjutant of the Right Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 党項叛，率禁兵萬人戍長武。

translations.literal: When the Tangut rebelled, he led ten thousand palace troops to garrison Changwu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut rose, he led ten thousand palace troops to hold Changwu.

sentences.zh: 是時諸將無功，唯駢數用奇，殺獲甚多。

translations.literal: At that time the generals won no success; only Pian repeatedly used surprise tactics and killed and captured in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals won nothing, but Pian again and again struck by stratagem and piled up kills and captives.

sentences.zh: 懿宗嘉之，徙屯秦州，即拜刺史兼防禦使。

translations.literal: Yizong was pleased and moved his camp to Qinzhou, appointing him prefect and defense commissioner on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong was pleased, shifted his camp to Qinzhou, and at once named him prefect and defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 取河、渭二州，略定鳳林關，降虜萬餘人。

translations.literal: He took He and Wei prefectures, roughly secured Fenglin Pass, and reduced more than ten thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He seized He and Wei prefectures, roughly pacified Fenglin Pass, and accepted the surrender of more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，帝將復安南，拜駢為都護，召還京師，見靈臺殿。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era, when the emperor meant to recover Annan, Pian was made Protector-General and recalled to the capital to appear at Lingtai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong, when the throne planned to recover Annan, Pian was made Protector-General, recalled to the capital, and received at Lingtai Hall.

sentences.zh: 於是容管經略使張茵不討賊，更以茵兵授駢。

translations.literal: The Rongguan frontier commissioner Zhang Yin would not pursue the bandits; his troops were instead given to Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yin, frontier commissioner of Rongguan, would not hunt the rebels, so his troops were transferred to Pian.

sentences.zh: 駢過江，約監軍李維周繼進。

translations.literal: Pian crossed the river and arranged with Military Commissioner Li Weizhou to follow in support.
translations.idiomatic: Pian crossed the river and arranged for Military Commissioner Li Weizhou to come after him.

sentences.zh: 維周擁眾壁海門，駢次峰州，大破南詔蠻，收所獲贍軍。

translations.literal: Weizhou held his force behind the seawall at Haimen; Pian halted at Fengzhou and smashed the Nanzhao barbarians, using the spoils to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou camped his men behind the seawall at Haimen. Pian stopped at Fengzhou, broke the Nanzhao tribes, and used the booty to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 維周忌之，匿捷書不奏。

translations.literal: Weizhou envied him and hid the victory memorials, not reporting them.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou resented him and suppressed the victory reports.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不知駢問百餘日，詔問狀。

translations.literal: For more than a hundred days the court had no word and ordered an inquiry into conditions.
translations.idiomatic: For over a hundred days the court heard nothing and sent orders asking for a report.

sentences.zh: 維周劾駢玩敵不進，更命右武衛將軍王晏權往代駢。

translations.literal: Weizhou impeached Pian for toying with the enemy and not advancing; the throne then named Right Martial Guard General Wang Yanquan to replace Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou charged Pian with dallying before the enemy and refusing to advance. The court named Right Martial Guard General Wang Yanquan to replace him.

sentences.zh: 俄而駢拔安南，斬蠻帥段酋遷，降附諸洞二萬計。

translations.literal: Soon Pian took Annan, beheaded the barbarian chief Duan Qiuchuan, and counted some twenty thousand cave settlements that submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Pian recovered Annan, beheaded the tribal chief Duan Qiuchuan, and tallied some twenty thousand cave settlements that came in.

sentences.zh: 晏權方挾維周發海門，檄駢北歸。

translations.literal: Yanquan was just setting out with Weizhou from Haimen when an order recalled Pian north.
translations.idiomatic: Yanquan was only just leaving Haimen with Weizhou when a dispatch ordered Pian back north.

sentences.zh: 而駢遣王惠贊傳酋遷首京師，見艟艫甚盛，乃晏權等，惠贊懼奪其書，匿島中，間關至京師。

translations.literal: But Pian had sent Wang Huizan to carry Qiuchuan's head to the capital; seeing a great fleet of warships, Huizan realized it was Yanquan and the others. Fearful they would seize his documents, he hid on an island and at last reached the capital by a hard road.
translations.idiomatic: Pian had already sent Wang Huizan with Qiuchuan's head to the capital. Huizan saw a vast line of warships and knew it was Yanquan. Afraid they would take his papers, he hid on an island and at last reached the capital by a desperate route.

sentences.zh: 天子覽書，禦宣政殿，群臣皆賀，大赦天下。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven read the memorial at Xuanzheng Hall; the ministers all congratulated him, and a great amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven read the memorial in Xuanzheng Hall. The ministers all offered felicitations, and a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 進駢檢校刑部尚書，仍鎮安南，以都護府為靜海軍，授駢節度，兼諸道行營招討使。

translations.literal: Pian was promoted to Acting Minister of Justice and still held Annan; the Protectorate was made the Jinghai Army, and Pian was given the command seal as military commissioner and commander-in-chief over all expeditionary forces.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was made Acting Minister of Justice and kept at Annan. The protectorate became the Jinghai Army. He received the command seal as military commissioner and overall expedition commander.

sentences.zh: 始築安南城。

translations.literal: He first built the city of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: He built the city of Annan for the first time.

sentences.zh: 由安南至廣州，江漕梗險，多巨石，駢募工刂治，由是舟濟安行，儲餉畢給。

translations.literal: From Annan to Guangzhou the river transport was choked by peril; many huge stones blocked the way. Pian hired labor to cut them away, so that boats could pass in safety and stores were fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: From Annan to Guangzhou the river route was treacherous and choked with boulders. Pian hired workers to cut them, so boats could run safely and supplies flowed without fail.

sentences.zh: 又使者歲至，乃鑿道五所，置兵護送。

translations.literal: Imperial envoys also came each year; he then opened five roads and posted troops to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Because imperial envoys came every year, he cut five roads and stationed soldiers to guard each.

sentences.zh: 其徑青石者，或傳馬援所不能治。

translations.literal: Among the routes, one of blue stone was said in tradition to be beyond even Ma Yuan's power to clear.
translations.idiomatic: On one stretch of blue stone, tradition said even Ma Yuan had failed to clear it.

sentences.zh: 既攻之，有震碎其石，乃得通，因名道曰「天威」雲。

translations.literal: Once he attacked it, thunder shattered the rock and a passage was gained; he therefore named the road "Heaven's Might."
translations.idiomatic: When he attacked it, thunder shattered the stone and a way opened. He named the road "Heaven's Might."

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was further made Acting Minister of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Acting Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 駢之戰，其從孫潯常先鋒冒矢石以勸士。

translations.literal: In Pian's battles his nephew Sun Xun often led the van, braving arrows and stones to hearten the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In battle his nephew Sun Xun often took the van, braving arrows and stones to steel the men.

sentences.zh: 駢徙節天平，薦潯自代，詔拜交州節度使。

translations.literal: When Pian was transferred to the Pingping command, he recommended Xun to succeed him; an edict made Xun military commissioner of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Pian moved to the Pingping command, he urged Xun as his successor. An edict made Xun military commissioner of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗立，即其軍加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Xizong acceded, he was given the same army rank as Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong took the throne, he was made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs while keeping his army.

sentences.zh: 南詔寇巂州，掠成都，徙駢劍南西川節度，乘傳詣軍。

translations.literal: When Nanzhao raided Xi prefecture and plundered Chengdu, Pian was moved to military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit and rode post-haste to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao attacked Xi and looted Chengdu. Pian was shifted to military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit and rode post-haste to join the army.

sentences.zh: 及劍門，下令開城，縱民出入。

translations.literal: At Jianmen he ordered the gates opened and the people allowed to come and go freely.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianmen he ordered the gates opened and let the people pass in and out.

sentences.zh: 左右諫：「寇在近，脫大掠，不可悔。」

translations.literal: His attendants remonstrated: "The enemy is near—if they plunder on a great scale, it cannot be undone.
translations.idiomatic: His staff warned, "The raiders are close. If they sack the city, there will be no undoing it."

sentences.zh: 駢曰：「屬吾在安南破賊三十萬，驃信聞我至，尚敢邪！」

translations.literal: Pian said: "When I was in Annan I broke three hundred thousand rebels. Even if Biaoxin hears I have come, would he dare act wrongly!
translations.idiomatic: Pian said, "In Annan I smashed three hundred thousand rebels. When Biaoxin hears I am here, will he still dare mischief!"

sentences.zh: 當是時，蠻攻雅州，壁廬山，聞駢至，亟解去。

translations.literal: At that time the tribes were attacking Ya prefecture and camped on Mount Lu; when they heard Pian had arrived, they hurriedly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the tribes were pressing Ya and had walled up on Mount Lu. When word came that Pian was near, they broke camp at once.

sentences.zh: 駢即移檄驃信，勒兵從之。

translations.literal: Pian at once sent a proclamation to Biaoxin and pressed the army after him.
translations.idiomatic: Pian immediately sent a summons to Biaoxin and drove the army in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 驃信大懼，送質子入朝，約不敢寇。

translations.literal: Biaoxin was greatly afraid, sent a hostage son to court, and pledged not to raid again.
translations.idiomatic: Biaoxin was terrified, sent a royal hostage to court, and swore not to raid again.

sentences.zh: 蜀有突將，分左右二廂，廂有虞候，詰火督盜賊，有兵馬虞候，主調發。

translations.literal: Shu had shock troops divided into left and right wings; each wing had a duty officer who inspected fires and pursued bandits, and a horse-and-arms duty officer who handled deployments.
translations.idiomatic: Shu kept crack troops in left and right wings. Each wing had a duty officer to watch fires and hunt thieves, and a horse-and-arms officer to handle mobilization.

sentences.zh: 駢罷其一，各置一虞候。

translations.literal: Pian abolished one wing and set a single duty officer for each.
translations.idiomatic: Pian abolished one wing and placed one duty officer over each side.

sentences.zh: 又以蜀兵孱，詔蠻新定，人未安業，罷突將月稟並餐錢，約曰：「府庫完，當如舊。」

translations.literal: Again, because Shu troops were weak and the edict had only just pacified the tribes, the people had not yet settled into their livelihoods, he abolished the shock troops monthly stipends and meal money, stipulating: "When the treasury is full again, things will be as before."
translations.idiomatic: Again, because Shu forces were depleted and the court had only just pacified the tribes, the people had not yet returned to their trades. He cut the shock troops monthly pay and meal allowance, promising: "When the treasury is whole again, pay will be restored."

sentences.zh: 又團練兵戰者，厚其衣稟；

translations.literal: Also, for militia who fought in battle, he increased their clothing rations;
translations.idiomatic: He also gave heavier clothing allotments to militia who saw combat;

sentences.zh: 不團練者，但掌文書、倉庫，衣稟減焉。

translations.literal: those not in the militia, who only handled documents and storehouses, had their clothing rations reduced.
translations.idiomatic: those who did not drill, and only kept papers and warehouses, had their allotments cut.

sentences.zh: 駢曰：「皆王卒，命均之。」

translations.literal: Pian said: "They are all the king's soldiers; treat them equally."
translations.idiomatic: Pian said, "They are all the king's soldiers—share alike."

sentences.zh: 戰士大望。

translations.literal: The warriors were deeply disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: The fighters were bitterly let down.

sentences.zh: 於時天平、昭義、義成戍軍合蜀兵凡六萬。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison troops of Tianping, Zhaoyi, and Yicheng, together with Shu forces, totaled sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tianping, Zhaoyi, and Yicheng garrisons together with Shu troops numbered sixty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 駢之自將出屯也，突將亂，乘門以入，駢匿於圊，求不得。

translations.literal: When Pian was personally leading troops out to camp, the shock troops mutinied, burst through the gates, and Pian hid in the privy; they could not find him.
translations.idiomatic: When Pian led the army out to camp in person, the shock troops rioted, forced the gates, and Pian hid in the latrine—they could not find him.

sentences.zh: 天平軍聞變，其校張桀以士五百格戰，不勝。

translations.literal: When the Tianping army heard of the disturbance, its officer Zhang Jie took five hundred men to block and fight; they could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianping troops heard the uproar. Their officer Zhang Jie took five hundred men to meet them in battle and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 監軍慰撫之，皆曰：「州雖更蠻亂，戶口尚完，府庫方實，公削軍稟以自養，不堪其虐，故亂。」

translations.literal: The army supervisor soothed them; they all said: "Though the prefecture has suffered repeated tribal turmoil, the households are still largely intact and the treasury is still full. You cut army rations to enrich yourself—we cannot bear such cruelty, hence the mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor tried to calm them. They said, "The prefecture has seen tribal raids again and again, yet households remain and the treasury is still stocked. You shaved army pay to feed yourself—we cannot endure such abuse, and so we rose."

sentences.zh: 監軍懼，講解之。

translations.literal: The supervisor was afraid and negotiated a settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor was afraid and talked them into standing down.

sentences.zh: 取役夫數百，名叛卒，藉斬其首，乃定。

translations.literal: He took several hundred laborers, called them rebel soldiers, and used this pretext to behead them; only then was order restored.
translations.idiomatic: He seized several hundred laborers, called them mutineers, and beheaded them on that pretext; only then did calm return.

sentences.zh: 駢徐出，以金帛厚賞士，開府庫悉還其衣稟。

translations.literal: Pian slowly emerged, rewarded the troops lavishly with gold and silk, opened the treasury, and fully restored their clothing rations.
translations.idiomatic: Pian came out at last, heaped gold and silk on the men, opened the treasury, and paid back every clothing allotment.

sentences.zh: 然密籍所給姓名，夜遣牙將擊殺之，夷其族，雖孕者不貰，投屍於江。

translations.literal: Yet he secretly recorded the names of those who had received rewards, and at night sent adjutants to hunt them down and kill them, exterminating their clans—even the pregnant were not spared—and cast the bodies into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he secretly listed every name that had taken payment, and at night sent adjutants to strike them down and wipe out their families—even women with child were not spared—and threw the corpses into the river.

sentences.zh: 有一婦方踞而乳子，將就刑，媼傷之，疑其畏死，謂曰：「以子丐我，一詣曹司也。」

translations.literal: There was one woman squatting to nurse her child about to be executed; an old woman took pity, thinking she feared death, and said: "Give me your child—I will go once to the authorities for you."
translations.idiomatic: One woman was squatting to nurse her child when the execution came. An old woman pitied her, thinking she clung to life, and said, "Give me the boy—I will plead once before the magistrate."

sentences.zh: 婦蹶起曰：「我知之，且飽吾子，不可使以饑就戮也。」

translations.literal: The woman sprang up and said: "I understand. Let me first feed my child—I cannot let him go to the execution starving."
translations.idiomatic: The woman leapt up and said, "I know. Let me feed my child first—I will not send him to the blade hungry."

sentences.zh: 見刑者拜曰：「渠有節度使奪戰士食，一日忿怒，淫刑以逞，國家法令何有也？

translations.literal: She bowed to the executioners and said: "That man is a military commissioner who stole the warriors' food; in a day's wrath he indulged in cruel punishments—where are the nation's laws now?
translations.idiomatic: She bowed to the headsman and said, "That creature is a commissioner who stole the soldiers food. In one days rage he poured out obscene punishments—where are the laws of the realm?

sentences.zh: 我死當訴於天，使此賊闔門如今日冤也！」

translations.literal: When I die I shall plead before Heaven, that this villain's whole house may suffer today's injustice!"
translations.idiomatic: When I die I will accuse him before Heaven, that this villain's whole clan may know today's wrong!"

sentences.zh: 逮死，神色晏然。

translations.literal: When death came, her countenance was serene.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, her face was calm.

sentences.zh: 蜀人聞者為垂泣。

translations.literal: Shu people who heard of it wept.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it in Shu wept.

sentences.zh: 駢復錄突將戍還者，丸名貯器中，意不懌，則探之，或十或五，授將李敬全斬決。

translations.literal: Pian again recorded the shock troops returning from garrison duty, rolled their names into balls and kept them in a vessel; when displeased he would draw some—ten or five—and hand them to the general Li Jingquan for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Pian again registered shock troops returning from garrison, rolled their names into balls in a jar, and when his mood turned foul would draw out ten or five and hand them to Li Jingquan to behead.

sentences.zh: 親吏王殷說駢曰：「突將在行者，初不知謀，公當赦之。」

translations.literal: His intimate clerk Wang Yin urged Pian: "The shock troops still on campaign knew nothing of the plot at first—you should pardon them."
translations.idiomatic: His close clerk Wang Yin urged him, "The shock troops still in the field knew nothing of the plot at first—you should spare them."

sentences.zh: 駢悅，投丸池中，人乃安。

translations.literal: Pian was pleased, threw the balls into the pool, and the men were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was pleased, cast the balls into a pool, and the men were reassured.

sentences.zh: 蜀之土惡，成都城歲壞，駢易以磚甓，陴堞完新，負城丘陵悉墾平之，以便農桑。

translations.literal: Shus soil was poor; Chengdus walls collapsed yearly. Pian replaced them with brick, making battlements whole and new; hills close to the city he had all leveled for farming.
translations.idiomatic: Shu soil was treacherous and Chengdus walls crumbled every year. Pian rebuilt them in brick, making parapets whole and new, and leveled every hillock by the walls for farming.

sentences.zh: 訖功，筮之得《大畜》。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, divination yielded the hexagram Great Taming.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done, divination gave the hexagram Great Taming.

sentences.zh: 駢曰：「畜者，養也。

translations.literal: Pian said: "To tame is to nourish.
translations.idiomatic: Pian said, "To tame is to nourish.

sentences.zh: 濟以剛健篤實，輝光日新，吉孰大焉！

translations.literal: Joined with firm strength, sincerity, and substance, brilliance renewed day by day—what fortune could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Joined with firm strength, sincerity, and weight, brilliance renewed day by day—what blessing could be greater!

sentences.zh: 文宜去下存上。」

translations.literal: In the character wen one should remove the lower part and keep the upper."
translations.idiomatic: In the character wen, take away what is below and keep what is above."

sentences.zh: 因名大玄城。

translations.literal: He therefore named it the Great Mystery City.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore named it the Great Mystery City.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司徒，封燕國公，徙荊南節度。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan, and transferred to Jingnan command.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Acting Minister of Works, enfeoffed Duke of Yan, and moved to the Jingnan command.

sentences.zh: 梁纘者，本以昭義兵西戍，駢表隸麾下。

translations.literal: Liang Zuan had originally come west with Zhaoyi troops on garrison duty; Pian memorialized to have him under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zuan had come west with Zhaoyi troops on garrison duty. Pian memorialized to place him under his command.

sentences.zh: 王仙芝之敗，殘黨過江，帝以駢治鄆威化大行，且仙芝黨皆鄆人，故授駢鎮海節度使。

translations.literal: After Wang Xianzhi's defeat, remnants crossed the river. The emperor, because Pian's governance at Yan had spread great reform, and because Xianzhi's followers were all men of Yan, appointed Pian military commissioner of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xianzhi was broken, remnant bands crossed the river. The emperor, seeing how Pian's rule at Yan had spread reform far and wide, and that Xianzhi's partisans were all men of Yan, made Pian military commissioner of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 駢遣將張潾與纘分兵窮討，降其驍帥畢師鐸數十人，賊走嶺表。

translations.literal: Pian sent Zhang Lin and Zuan with divided forces in relentless pursuit, accepting the surrender of dozens of their fiercest chiefs including Bi Shiduo; the rebels fled beyond the Lingnan passes.
translations.idiomatic: Pian sent Zhang Lin and Zuan with split columns in relentless pursuit, accepting the surrender of dozens of their fiercest chiefs, among them Bi Shiduo; the rebels fled beyond the passes into Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 帝美其功，加諸道行營都統、鹽鐵轉運等使。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his merit and added the posts of overall expedition commander and salt-and-iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his merit and added overall expedition commander and salt-and-iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又詔駢料官軍義營鄉團，歸其老弱傷夷，裁制軍食；

translations.literal: He also ordered Pian to assess government troops, volunteer camps, and local militias, send home the aged, weak, and wounded, and regulate army provisions;
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Pian to review government troops, volunteer camps, and local militias, send home the aged, weak, and wounded, and trim army rations;

sentences.zh: 刺史以下小罪輒罰，大罪以聞。

translations.literal: minor offenses by prefects and below he might punish directly; major ones were to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: for prefects and below, minor crimes he might punish at once; major ones he was to report.

sentences.zh: 賊更推黃巢南陷廣州，駢建遣潾以兵五千屯郴扼賊西路，留後王重任以兵八千並海進援循、潮，自將萬人繇大庾擊賊廣州，且請起荊南王鐸兵三萬壁桂、永，以邕管兵五千壁端州，則賊無遺類。

translations.literal: The rebels then elevated Huang Chao, who marched south and took Guangzhou. Pian proposed sending Lin with five thousand men to camp at Chen to block the western route, the deputy Wang Zhongren with eight thousand along the coast to relieve Xun and Chao, himself leading ten thousand through Dayu to strike Guangzhou, and also requesting Wang Duo in Jingnan to raise thirty thousand to wall up Gui and Yong, with five thousand Yongguan troops at Duanzhou—then not a rebel would remain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then set up Huang Chao, who marched south and took Guangzhou. Pian proposed sending Lin with five thousand to hold Chen and choke the western road, deputy Wang Zhongren with eight thousand along the coast to relieve Xun and Chao, and himself leading ten thousand through Dayu to strike Guangzhou—while asking Wang Duo in Jingnan to raise thirty thousand to fortify Gui and Yong and five thousand Yongguan troops to hold Duanzhou, so that no rebel would escape.

sentences.zh: 帝納其策，而駢卒不行。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted the plan, but in the end Pian never carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the plan, but Pian never moved.

sentences.zh: 俄徙淮南節度副大使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred as deputy military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was shifted to deputy military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 駢繕完城壘，募軍及土客，得銳士七萬，乃傳檄召天下兵共討賊，威震一時，天子倚以為重。

translations.literal: Pian repaired walls and ramparts, recruited soldiers and locals, mustered seventy thousand elite troops, then issued proclamations calling all forces under heaven to join in suppressing the rebels. His prestige shook the age; the Son of Heaven relied on him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Pian repaired walls and ramparts, recruited soldiers and locals, and raised seventy thousand crack troops. He then issued proclamations summoning armies from across the realm to join in suppressing the rebels. His prestige shook the age, and the Son of Heaven leaned on him as a pillar.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，潾破賊大雲倉，詐降巢。

translations.literal: Early in the Guangming reign, Lin defeated the rebels at Great Cloud Granary and feigned surrender to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangming era, Lin smashed the rebels at Great Cloud Granary and pretended to surrender to Chao.

sentences.zh: 巢不意其襲，遂大奔，引殘黨壁上饒，然眾亡幾。

translations.literal: Chao did not expect the surprise attack and fled in rout, leading remnants to hold the heights at Shangrao, but his host was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Chao did not expect the ambush and broke into flight, leading the remnant host to hold the heights at Shangrao, but his force was nearly spent.

sentences.zh: 會疫癘起，人死亡，潾進擊之，巢大懼，以金啖潾，騰書於駢，丐歸命。

translations.literal: Pestilence broke out and men died in droves; Lin pressed the attack. Chao was greatly afraid, bribed Lin with gold, and sent a swift letter to Pian begging to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Plague broke out and men died in heaps. Lin pressed the attack. Chao was terrified, stuffed Lin with gold, and sent a swift letter to Pian begging to submit.

sentences.zh: 駢信之，許為求節度。

translations.literal: Pian believed him and promised to seek a command seal for him.
translations.idiomatic: Pian believed him and promised to seek a command seal on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 當此時，昭義、武寧、義武兵數萬赴淮南，駢欲專己功，即奏賊已破，不須大兵。

translations.literal: At this time tens of thousands from Zhaoyi, Wuning, and Yiwu were hurrying to Huainan. Pian wished to monopolize the credit and memorialized that the rebels were already broken and great armies were unnecessary.
translations.idiomatic: Just then tens of thousands from Zhaoyi, Wuning, and Yiwu were marching to Huainan. Pian wanted the glory for himself alone and memorialized that the rebels were already broken and no great force was needed.

sentences.zh: 有詔班師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the armies to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 巢知兵罷，即絕駢請戰，擊殺潾，乘勝度江攻天長。

translations.literal: Chao knew the armies had departed, broke off his plea to Pian, resumed fighting, killed Lin, and crossing the river in victory attacked Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chao learned the armies had stood down, broke off his plea to Pian, resumed fighting, killed Lin, and in victory crossed the river to attack Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 始，巢在廣州，求天平節度，宰相廬攜善駢，以有討賊功，不肯赦巢，與鄭畋爭於朝，故巢怨不得節度。

translations.literal: Initially, when Chao was at Guangzhou he had sought the Tianping command. Chancellor Lu Xi favored Pian; because Pian had merit in suppressing rebels, Xi refused to pardon Chao and quarreled with Zheng Yin at court—hence Chao's grudge at not receiving a command.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Chao was at Guangzhou he had asked for the Tianping command. Chancellor Lu Xi favored Pian; because Pian had merit in hunting rebels, Xi would not pardon Chao and quarreled with Zheng Yin in court—so Chao nursed a grudge at being denied a seal.

sentences.zh: 而駢聞議不一，亦不平，至是欲縱賊以聳朝廷，然後立功。

translations.literal: Pian heard the court was divided and was himself resentful; now he wished to let the rebels grow to alarm the court, then win merit by defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Pian heard the court was split and was himself aggrieved. Now he meant to let the rebels swell to frighten the throne, then win fresh merit by crushing them.

sentences.zh: 畢師鐸諫曰：「朝廷所恃，誰易於公？

translations.literal: Bi Shiduo remonstrated: "On whom does the court rely if not you?
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shiduo urged him, "On whom does the court lean if not you?

sentences.zh: 制賊要害，莫先淮南。

translations.literal: To check the rebels vital point, nothing comes before Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: To choke the rebels, no ground matters before Huainan.

sentences.zh: 今不據要津以滅賊，使得北度，必亂中原。」

translations.literal: If you do not hold the strategic crossings now to destroy them and let them cross north, they will surely throw the central plains into chaos."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not hold the crossings now and wipe them out, but let them cross north, the heartland will surely fall into chaos."

sentences.zh: 駢矍然，下令將出師。

translations.literal: Pian started awake and ordered his generals to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: Pian jolted awake and ordered his generals to march.

sentences.zh: 嬖將呂用之畏師鐸有功，諫曰：「公勛業極矣，賊未殄，朝廷且有口語。

translations.literal: His favorite Lü Yongzhi feared Shiduo's merit and urged: "Your achievements have reached their height; if the rebels are not yet wiped out, the court will surely find fault in words.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite Lü Yongzhi feared Shiduo's rising credit and urged, "Your merit has reached its peak. If the rebels are not yet destroyed, the court will already murmur against you.

sentences.zh: 況賊平，挾震主之威，安所稅駕？

translations.literal: Moreover, once the rebels are pacified, bearing the awe of a ruler whom you yourself saved—where would you rein yourself in?
translations.idiomatic: And once the rebels are gone, you will hold the awe of a sovereign you yourself rescued—where then will you rein yourself in?

sentences.zh: 不如觀釁求福，為不朽資也。」

translations.literal: Better to watch for openings and seek fortune—making capital for lasting renown."
translations.idiomatic: Better to watch for chance and hoard blessing, building capital for a name that will not die."

sentences.zh: 駢入其計，托疾未可以出屯，嚴兵保境。

translations.literal: Pian took his counsel, pleaded illness as reason not to camp out, and held his border with strict troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pian took his advice, pleaded illness as reason not to camp out, and kept his border under tight guard.

sentences.zh: 巢據滁、和，去廣陵才數百里，乃求援陳許。

translations.literal: Chao held Chuzhou and Hezhou, only a few hundred li from Guangling, yet sought aid from Chenxu.
translations.idiomatic: Chao held Chuzhou and Hezhou, only a few hundred li from Guangling, yet still begged aid from Chenxu.

sentences.zh: 巢逼揚州，眾十五萬。

translations.literal: Chao pressed Yangzhou with a host of one hundred fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chao pressed on Yangzhou with a host of one hundred fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 駢將曹全晸以兵五千戰不利，壁泗州以待援，駢兵終不出。

translations.literal: Pian's general Cao Quanzhen fought with five thousand men without success, walled up at Sizhou awaiting relief—Pian's army never came out.
translations.idiomatic: Pian's general Cao Quanzhen fought with five thousand men and failed, walled up at Sizhou waiting for relief—yet Pian's army never stirred.

sentences.zh: 賊北趨河洛，天子遣使者促駢討賊，冠蓋相望也。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed north toward the Yellow and Luo; the Son of Heaven sent envoys urging Pian to attack—the roads were crowded with officials.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drove north toward the Yellow and Luo. The Son of Heaven sent envoy after envoy to hurry Pian to strike—the roads were thick with official coaches.

sentences.zh: 俄而兩京陷，天子猶冀駢立功，眷寄未衰，詔刺史若諸將有功，自監察御史至常侍，許墨制除授。

translations.literal: Soon both capitals fell; the emperor still hoped Pian would win merit, and his favor had not waned. An edict allowed military commissioners and generals with merit to appoint from Secretariat Drafter through Regular Attendant by ink edict.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both capitals fell. The emperor still hoped Pian would win merit, and his favor had not cooled. An edict allowed commissioners and generals with merit to appoint men from Secretariat Drafter through Regular Attendant by ink edict.

sentences.zh: 尋進檢校太尉，東面都統，京西、京北神策軍諸道兵馬等使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Grand Marshal, Eastern Commander-in-Chief, and commissioner over the Jingxi and Jingbei Shence armies and all circuit forces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Acting Grand Marshal, Eastern Commander-in-Chief, and commissioner over the Jingxi and Jingbei Shence armies and all circuit troops.

sentences.zh: 會二雉雊署寢，占者曰：「軍府將空。」

translations.literal: Two pheasants crowed in his headquarters bedroom; the diviner said: "The military prefecture will be emptied."
translations.idiomatic: Two pheasants crowed in his headquarters bedroom. The diviner said, "The military prefecture will be emptied."

sentences.zh: 駢惡之，悉兵出營東塘，舟二千艘，戈鎧完銳，日討金鼓，以侈士誌。

translations.literal: Pian hated the omen and moved all troops to camp at East Bund—two thousand boats, complete sharp armor, daily drills with gongs and drums to inflame the soldiers spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Pian hated the omen and moved every soldier to camp at East Bund—two thousand boats, armor complete and sharp, daily drills with gongs and drums to fire the men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 與浙西節度使周寶檄，欲連和而西，寶大喜。

translations.literal: He exchanged proclamations with Zhou Bao, military commissioner of Zhexi, intending to join forces and march west; Bao was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged proclamations with Zhou Bao, military commissioner of Zhexi, intending to join forces and march west. Bao was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 有謂寶：「彼欲並江東為孫策三分計。」

translations.literal: Someone told Bao: "He intends to swallow Jiangdong in Sun Ce's plan to divide the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Bao, "He means to swallow Jiangdong in Sun Ce's scheme to split the realm three ways."

sentences.zh: 寶未之信。

translations.literal: Bao did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Bao did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 俄而駢請寶至軍議事，寶怒，辭疾不出，釁隙遂構。

translations.literal: Soon Pian asked Bao to come to camp for council; Bao was angry, declined on grounds of illness, and enmity took shape.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pian asked Bao to come to camp for council. Bao was furious, pleaded illness, and would not go; bad blood formed.

sentences.zh: 駢屯東塘百日，托以寶及浙東劉漢宏將為不利，乃還，以應其變。

translations.literal: Pian camped at East Bund a hundred days, then pleaded that Bao and Liu Hanhong of eastern Zhejiang meant him harm and returned—to meet whatever shift might come.
translations.idiomatic: Pian camped at East Bund a hundred days, then pleaded that Bao and Liu Hanhong of eastern Zhejiang meant him harm and withdrew—to answer whatever turn might come.

sentences.zh: 帝知駢無出兵意，天下益殆。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Pian had no mind to send troops; the realm grew more perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Pian had no will to march; the realm grew more desperate.

sentences.zh: 乃以王鐸代為都統，以崔安潛副之。

translations.literal: Wang Duo was made commander-in-chief in his place, with Cui Anqian as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo was made commander-in-chief in his stead, with Cui Anqian as deputy.

sentences.zh: 詔韋昭度領諸道鹽鐵轉運使，加駢侍中，增實戶一百，封渤海郡王。

translations.literal: Wei Zhaodu was ordered to lead salt-and-iron transport for all circuits; Pian was made Palace Attendant, given a hundred additional taxable households, and enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu was ordered to lead salt-and-iron transport for all circuits. Pian was made Palace Attendant, given a hundred added taxable households, and enfeoffed Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 駢失兵柄利權，攘袂大詬，即上書謾言不恭，詆鐸乃敗軍將，而安潛狼貪，有如橈敗，詒千古之悔。

translations.literal: Stripped of military power and profit, Pian flung up his sleeves and cursed loudly, then memorialized with reckless disrespect, slandering Duo as a defeated general and Anqian as greedy as a wolf, like a rotted oar ruining the boat—bequeathing regret for a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of command and profit, Pian flung up his sleeves and cursed aloud, then memorialized in reckless insolence, calling Duo a beaten general and Anqian a wolfish glutton—like a rotted oar that sinks the boat, bequeathing shame for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 又引更始刮席、子嬰軹道事以激帝。

translations.literal: He also cited how Gengshi Emperor scraped his seat and how Ziying met the chariot on the road—to goad the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited how the Gengshi Emperor scraped his seat and how Ziying met the chariot on the road—to sting the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下詔切責。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and issued an edict of sharp rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and sent down an edict of sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 當此時，王室微，不絕如帶。

translations.literal: At this time the royal house was feeble, hanging by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the royal house was frail, hanging by a thread.

sentences.zh: 駢都統三年，無尺寸功，幸國顛沛，大料兵，陰圖割據，一旦失勢，威望頓盡，故肆為醜悖，脅邀天子，冀復故權。

translations.literal: Pian had been commander three years without the slightest merit, while the state tottered in ruin; he had mustered great armies and secretly plotted to carve out territory. Once his power slipped, his prestige collapsed at once—so he indulged in ugly outrage, coerced and importuned the Son of Heaven, hoping to win back his old authority.
translations.idiomatic: Pian had held command three years without a hair's breadth of merit while the realm stumbled in ruin. He had raised vast armies and secretly plotted to carve out his own ground. Once power slipped from his hands, his prestige collapsed at once—so he poured out ugly outrage, coerced and importuned the Son of Heaven, hoping to win back his old sway.

sentences.zh: 而吳人顧雲以文辭緣澤其奸，偃然無所忌畏。

translations.literal: Yet the Wu man Gu Yun used polished prose to gloss his treachery, and stood at ease without the least fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Wu man Gu Yun used polished prose to varnish his treachery, and stood at ease without the least fear.

sentences.zh: 又請帝南幸江淮。

translations.literal: He also urged the emperor to tour south to the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to tour south to the Yangtze and Huai.

sentences.zh: 會平賊，駢聞，縮氣悵恨，部下多叛去，郁郁無聊，乃篤意求神仙，以軍事屬用之。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Pian heard and shrank in spirit, full of bitter regret; many of his followers deserted. Despondent and at loose ends, he devoted himself to seeking immortals and left military affairs to Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, Pian heard and shrank in spirit, bitter and aggrieved. Many of his followers deserted. Despondent and idle, he turned his heart to immortals and left military affairs to Yongzhi.

sentences.zh: 用之者，鄱陽人，世為商儈，往來廣陵，得諸賈之。

translations.literal: Yongzhi was a man of Poyang; his family for generations were merchants traveling to Guangling, knowing all the traders.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi was a man of Poyang. His family for generations were merchants who traveled to Guangling and knew every trader there.

sentences.zh: 既孤，依舅家，盜私其室，亡命九華山，事方士牛弘徽，得役鬼術，賣藥廣陵市。

translations.literal: Orphaned, he lived with his mother's kin, stole from their house, fled to Mount Jiuhua, served the adept Niu Honghui, learned arts to command ghosts, and sold medicine in Guangling market.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned, he lived with his mother's kin, stole from their house, fled to Mount Jiuhua, served the adept Niu Honghui, learned arts to command ghosts, and sold medicine in the Guangling market.

sentences.zh: 始詣駢親將俞公楚，驗其術，因得見駢，署幕府，稍補右職。

translations.literal: At first he went to Pian's intimate officer Yu Gongchu to demonstrate his arts, thus gained audience with Pian, entered his staff, and was gradually promoted to higher posts.
translations.idiomatic: At first he went to Pian's intimate officer Yu Gongchu to prove his arts, and so gained audience with Pian, entered his staff, and was slowly raised to higher posts.

sentences.zh: 用之既少賤，具知閭裏利病、吏得失，頗班班言政事，以將左道，駢愈器之。

translations.literal: Yongzhi, having been humble in youth, knew thoroughly neighborhood grievances and officials failings, and spoke often and clearly on government; combined with his heterodox arts, Pian valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi, having been lowborn, knew every neighborhood grievance and every officials failing, and spoke often and plainly on government. Together with his heterodox arts, Pian prized him all the more.

sentences.zh: 乃廣樹朋黨，刺知駢動息，持金帛還結左右，日為誕妄以動駢。

translations.literal: He then spread a wide clique, spied on Pian's every move, brought gold and silk to win over those around him, and daily spun wild tales to sway Pian.
translations.idiomatic: He then spread a wide clique, spied on Pian's every move, used gold and silk to bind those around him, and daily spun wild tales to move Pian.

sentences.zh: 又薦狂人諸葛殷、張守一為長年方，並署牙將。

translations.literal: He also recommended the madmen Zhuge Yin and Zhang Shouyi as longevity masters, and both were named adjutant generals.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended the madmen Zhuge Yin and Zhang Shouyi as longevity masters, and both were made adjutant generals.

sentences.zh: 初，殷將見，用之紿曰：「上帝以公為人臣，慮機事廢，使神人來備羽翼，且當以職縻之。」

translations.literal: When Yin was first to appear, Yongzhi deceived Pian: "Heaven, seeing you as a minister and fearing state business would fail, sent a divine man to support you—you should bind him with office."
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was first to appear, Yongzhi tricked Pian: "Heaven, seeing you as a minister and fearing state business would fail, sent a divine man to brace you—you should tie him down with office."

sentences.zh: 明日，殷以褐衣見，辯詐無窮，駢大驚，號「葛將軍」。

translations.literal: Next day Yin appeared in coarse cloth, his sophistry endless; Pian was greatly startled and called him "General Ge."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yin came in coarse cloth, his sophistry endless. Pian was thunderstruck and called him "General Ge."

sentences.zh: 其陰狡過用之遠甚。

translations.literal: His secret cunning far exceeded Yongzhi's.
translations.idiomatic: His secret cunning far outstripped Yongzhi's.

sentences.zh: 有大賈居第華壯，殷求之不得，謂駢曰：「城中且有妖，當築壇禳卻之。」

translations.literal: A great merchant had a splendid mansion; Yin could not obtain it and told Pian: "There is a demon in the city—we must build an altar to exorcise it."
translations.idiomatic: A great merchant had a splendid mansion. Yin could not get it and told Pian, "There is a demon in the city—we must build an altar to drive it off."

sentences.zh: 因指賈居。

translations.literal: He pointed at the merchant's house.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed at the merchant's house.

sentences.zh: 駢敕吏即日驅徙，殷入居之。

translations.literal: Pian ordered officials to drive the family out that very day; Yin moved in.
translations.idiomatic: Pian ordered officials to drive the family out that very day. Yin moved in.

sentences.zh: 駢造迎仙等樓，皆廣高八十尺，飾以金珠渠玉，侍女衣羽衣，新聲度曲，以擬鈞天，薰齋其上，祈與仙接。

translations.literal: Pian built towers such as Welcome to the Immortals, each eighty feet broad and high, adorned with gold, pearls, jade, and tracery; serving girls wore feather robes; new tunes were composed in the mode of Heaven's Harmony; he fumigated and fasted on the heights, praying to join the immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Pian built towers such as Welcome to the Immortals, each eighty feet broad and high, adorned with gold, pearls, jade, and inlay. Serving girls wore feather robes; new tunes were set in the mode of Heaven's Harmony. He burned incense and fasted on the heights, praying to meet the immortals.

sentences.zh: 用之自謂與仙真通，對駢叱咤風雨，或望空顧揖再拜，語言俚近，左右或竊議，輒殺之，後無敢出口者。

translations.literal: Yongzhi claimed communion with true immortals, shouted at wind and rain before Pian, or gazed into the sky bowing again and again; his speech was vulgar and coarse. If attendants whispered, he had them killed—after that none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi claimed to speak with true immortals, shouted at wind and rain before Pian, or gazed into the sky bowing again and again. His speech was coarse and low. If attendants whispered, he had them killed—after that none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 蕭勝納賄用之，求鹽城監，駢不肯。

translations.literal: Xiao Sheng bribed Yongzhi to seek the salt-works post at Yancheng; Pian refused.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sheng bribed Yongzhi to seek the salt-works post at Yancheng. Pian refused.

sentences.zh: 用之曰：「仙人言鹽城有寶劍，須真人取之，唯勝可往。」

translations.literal: Yongzhi said: "The immortals say Yancheng holds a treasure sword; only a true man can fetch it—only Sheng may go."
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi said, "The immortals say Yancheng holds a treasure sword. Only a true man can fetch it—only Sheng may go."

sentences.zh: 駢許諾。

translations.literal: Pian consented.
translations.idiomatic: Pian agreed.

sentences.zh: 數月，勝獻銅匕首，用之曰：「此北帝所佩也，得之者兵不敢犯。」

translations.literal: Months later Sheng presented a bronze dagger; Yongzhi said: "This was worn by the North Emperor—whoever holds it, armies dare not attack."
translations.idiomatic: Months later Sheng presented a bronze dagger. Yongzhi said, "This was worn by the North Emperor. Whoever holds it, armies dare not attack."

sentences.zh: 駢寶秘之，常持以坐起。

translations.literal: Pian treasured it in secret and kept it always in hand, sitting or rising.
translations.idiomatic: Pian treasured it in secret and kept it always in hand, sitting or rising.

sentences.zh: 用之憚其術窮且見詰，乃刻青石手板為龍蛇隱起，文曰：「帝賜駢。」

translations.literal: Yongzhi feared his tricks would run out and he would be questioned; he carved a green stone tally with raised dragon and serpent designs, inscribed: "The Emperor bestows upon Pian—"
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi feared his tricks would run dry and he would be called to account. He carved a green stone tally with raised dragon and serpent designs, inscribed: "The Emperor bestows upon Pian—"

sentences.zh: 使人潛植機上，駢得之大喜。

translations.literal: He had someone secretly fix it to the mechanism; when Pian obtained it he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He had someone secretly fix it to the rigging. When Pian found it he was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 為寓鵠廷中，設機關，觸人則飛動，駢衣羽服，乘之作仙去狀。

translations.literal: He placed a mechanical swan in the courtyard and set up gears; when touched it would fly and move. Pian wore feather robes and rode it in the manner of an immortal departing.
translations.idiomatic: He set a mechanical swan in the courtyard with hidden gears that stirred when touched. Pian donned feather robes and rode it, playing at ascending as an immortal.

sentences.zh: 用之懼有擿其奸者，乃曰：「仙人當下，但患學者真氣虧沮耳。」

translations.literal: Yongzhi feared someone would expose his fraud and said: "The immortal should descend, but one only worries that the student's vital qi is depleted."
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi feared someone would expose his fraud and said, "The immortal ought to descend—but only if the student's vital breath has not been drained away."

sentences.zh: 駢始棄人間事，絕妾媵，雖將吏不得見。

translations.literal: Pian then began to abandon worldly affairs, cut off concubines, and even generals and clerks could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Pian then turned his back on worldly affairs, dismissed his concubines, and would not even receive his generals and staff.

sentences.zh: 客至，先遣薰濯，詣方士祓除，謂之解穢，少選即引去。

translations.literal: When guests arrived he first sent for fumigation and washing, had them go to adepts for exorcism—called "removing pollution"—and shortly led them away.
translations.idiomatic: When guests came he had them fumigated and washed first, then sent them to adepts for purification—"removing defilement"—and dismissed them before long.

sentences.zh: 自是內外無敢言者，惟梁纘屢為駢言，駢不聽。

translations.literal: From then within and without none dared speak; only Liang Zuan repeatedly spoke on Pian's behalf, and Pian would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: After that none inside or outside dared speak up. Only Liang Zuan pleaded with Pian again and again, and Pian would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 纘懼，解所領兵，駢還其軍於昭義，纘不復事矣。

translations.literal: Zuan feared, resigned the troops he commanded; Pian returned his army to Zhaoyi, and Zuan no longer served.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan grew afraid, gave up the troops he commanded, and Pian returned his army to Zhaoyi. Zuan never served again.

sentences.zh: 用之既自任，淫刑重賦，人人思亂。

translations.literal: Yongzhi, once confident in himself, used lewd punishments and heavy levies; everyone thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yongzhi felt secure in power, he imposed cruel punishments and crushing taxes until everyone yearned for revolt.

sentences.zh: 乃擢廢吏百餘，號「察子」，厚稟食，令居衢哄間，凡民私鬩隱語莫不知，道路箝口。
