translations.literal: He then promoted over a hundred dismissed officials, called them "Inspectors," gave them thick grain rations, and ordered them to live in the bustling streets; no private quarrel or whisper of the people escaped them, and the roads fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: He raised more than a hundred cashiered clerks, called them "Inspectors," paid them generously, and posted them in the crowded streets. No private quarrel or whisper escaped them, and people sealed their lips on the roads.

sentences.zh: 誅所惡者數百族。

translations.literal: He executed the clans of those he hated—hundreds of families.
translations.idiomatic: He wiped out the clans of hundreds whom he hated.

sentences.zh: 又募卒二萬，為左、右「鏌邪軍」，與守一分總，置官屬如駢府。

translations.literal: He also recruited twenty thousand soldiers as the Left and Right "Moye Armies," sharing command with Shouyi's division, and set up officials like Pian's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He also raised twenty thousand men as the Left and Right "Moye Armies," sharing command with Shouyi's division, and staffed them with officers mirroring Pian's own establishment.

sentences.zh: 用之每出入，騶禦至千人；

translations.literal: Whenever Yongzhi went in or out, his escort reached a thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yongzhi went abroad, his escort ran to a thousand men;

sentences.zh: 建大第，軍胥營署皆備。

translations.literal: he built a great mansion with military clerks, camps, and offices all complete.
translations.idiomatic: he built a great mansion with military clerks, camps, and offices all in place.

sentences.zh: 建百尺樓，托雲占星，實窺伺城中之有變者。

translations.literal: He built a hundred-foot tower, pretending to read the stars through clouds, but in truth to spy on anyone in the city who showed change.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hundred-foot tower, claiming to read the stars through the clouds, but in truth to watch for trouble in the city.

sentences.zh: 左右姬侍百餘，皆娟秀光麗，善歌舞，巾束帶以侍。

translations.literal: Over a hundred maid attendants at his side were all graceful, bright, and lovely, skilled in song and dance, with headcloths and sashes to serve.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred maid attendants at his side were graceful and radiant, skilled in song and dance, with scarves and sashes as they waited on him.

sentences.zh: 月二十宴，其費仰於民，不足，至苛留度支運物。

translations.literal: Twenty banquets a month—their cost borne by the people; when that was not enough, he even harshly detained goods shipped by the treasury bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He held twenty feasts a month, paid for by the people; when that was not enough, he even seized goods in transit from the treasury bureau.

sentences.zh: 誘人上變，則許入貲產贖罪。

translations.literal: He enticed people to lodge denunciations, then allowed them to enter property to redeem their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He baited people into lodging denunciations, then let them buy their way out with property.

sentences.zh: 俞公楚數規戒其失，不聽。

translations.literal: Yu Gongchu repeatedly admonished him about his faults; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gongchu warned him again and again of his errors, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 姚歸禮謀殺之，弗克。

translations.literal: Yao Guili plotted to kill him but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guili plotted to kill him but failed.

sentences.zh: 用之因譖二人於駢，使以驍雄兵三千督盜於外，密使兵襲之，舉師殲焉。

translations.literal: Yongzhi therefore slandered the two men to Pian, had them with three thousand fierce troops supervise bandits outside, secretly sent soldiers to attack, and annihilated the whole force.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi slandered the two to Pian, sent them with three thousand crack troops to police bandits in the field, then secretly attacked and wiped out the entire command.

sentences.zh: 駢從子澞密疏用之罪，諫駢曰：「不除之，高氏且無種。」

translations.literal: Pian's nephew Yu secretly memorialized Yongzhi's crimes and admonished Pian: "If he is not removed, the Gao clan will soon have no descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Pian's nephew Yu secretly reported Yongzhi's crimes and warned Pian, "Unless you remove him, the Gao line will be extinguished."

sentences.zh: 駢怒，命左右扶出，以狀授用之。

translations.literal: Pian was angry, ordered attendants to haul him out, and gave the memorial to Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Pian flew into a rage, had attendants drag him out, and handed the memorial to Yongzhi.

sentences.zh: 用之誣澞貣貰不能滿，故妄言。

translations.literal: Yongzhi slandered Yu, saying his bribes could not satisfy him, and so he spoke falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi claimed Yu's greed for bribes had gone unsatisfied and that he had lied out of spite.

sentences.zh: 因出澞筆驗之，駢敕吏禁澞出入。

translations.literal: He then produced Yu's handwriting to verify it; Pian ordered officials to forbid Yu from entering or leaving.
translations.idiomatic: He produced samples of Yu's hand to prove it, and Pian ordered officials to confine Yu.

sentences.zh: 俄署舒州刺史，未幾為下所逐，用之構之也。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Shuzhou; not long after he was driven out by subordinates below—Yongzhi had engineered it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yu was named prefect of Shuzhou, but before long his own men drove him out—Yongzhi had engineered it.

sentences.zh: 駢使人殺澞。

translations.literal: Pian sent men to kill Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Pian had Yu killed.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王煴之亂，駢上書勸進，偽假駢中書令、諸道兵馬都統、江淮鹽鐵轉運使，以用之為嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: In the disturbance of the Heir Apparent Prince of Xiang, Yun, Pian memorialized urging his advance; they falsely granted Pian Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits' Armies, and Jiang-Huai Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, with Yongzhi as Military Commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: During the revolt of the Heir Apparent Prince of Xiang, Li Yun, Pian memorialized urging his enthronement. The puppet regime named Pian Grand Counselor, supreme commander of all circuits' armies, and Jiang-Huai salt commissioner, and made Yongzhi military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 駢久觖望，至是大喜，貢賦不絕。

translations.literal: Pian had long nursed thwarted ambition; at this he was greatly pleased, and tribute and levies never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Pian had long nursed thwarted ambitions; now he was overjoyed, and tribute and levies flowed without end.

sentences.zh: 用之始開府置官屬，禮與駢均矣。

translations.literal: Yongzhi for the first time opened an office and set up officials; his ceremonial standing equaled Pian's.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi for the first time opened his own office and staffed it; his ceremonial rank now matched Pian's.

sentences.zh: 以鄭杞、董僅、吳邁為腹心，駢之親信皆偪使附己，政事未嘗關決駢。

translations.literal: He took Zheng Qi, Dong Jin, and Wu Mai as his inner circle; Pian's intimates were all forced to attach to him, and government affairs never passed to Pian for decision.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zheng Qi, Dong Jin, and Wu Mai his inner circle, bullied Pian's confidants into siding with him, and never let Pian decide a matter of state.

sentences.zh: 駢內悔，欲收其權，不能也。

translations.literal: Pian inwardly regretted and wished to reclaim his authority but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Pian regretted it inwardly and tried to take back power, but could not.

sentences.zh: 用之問計於杞、僅，謀請駢齋於其第，密縊之，紿為升天，事不克。

translations.literal: Yongzhi asked Qi and Jin for a plan: invite Pian to fast at his mansion, secretly strangle him, and deceive people that he had ascended to heaven—the affair did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi asked Qi and Jin for counsel: lure Pian to fast at his mansion, strangle him in secret, and claim he had ascended as an immortal. The plot failed.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年，蔡賊孫儒兵略定遠，聲言涉淮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangqi, the Cai rebel Sun Ru's army roughly pacified Dingyuan and proclaimed that it would cross the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangqi, the Cai rebel Sun Ru's army overran Dingyuan and announced that it would cross the Huai.

sentences.zh: 壽州刺史張翺奔告駢，命畢師鐸率騎三百戍高郵。

translations.literal: Shouzhou Prefect Zhang Ao fled to report to Pian; he ordered Bi Shiduo to lead three hundred horsemen to garrison Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou prefect Zhang Ao fled to warn Pian, who ordered Bi Shiduo to take three hundred horsemen and hold Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 師鐸者，故仙芝黨，以善騎射稱。

translations.literal: Shiduo had been of Zhang Xianzhi's faction and was famed for skill in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo had belonged to Zhang Xianzhi's faction and was famed as a mounted archer.

sentences.zh: 駢敗巢於浙西，用其力，故寵待絕等。

translations.literal: Pian defeated Huang Chao in Zhexi and used his strength, so his favor and treatment were unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Pian had defeated Huang Chao in Zhexi with his help and favored him beyond all others.

sentences.zh: 用之厚啖以利，欲其諧附，然不肯情。

translations.literal: Yongzhi fed him thickly with profit, wishing him to harmonize and attach, yet he would not yield affection.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi heaped profit on him to win his loyalty, but Shiduo would not warm to him.

sentences.zh: 師鐸有妾美，用之請見，不可，狙其出，觀焉，怒而棄之；

translations.literal: Shiduo had a beautiful concubine; Yongzhi asked to see her and was refused. He spied when she went out, looked at her, and in anger abandoned her;
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo had a beautiful concubine. Yongzhi asked to see her and was refused. He spied on her when she went out, stared at her, and in a rage cast her off;

sentences.zh: 內忿懼，為子結婚於高郵將張神劍，陰倚為援。

translations.literal: inwardly resentful and afraid, he had his son marry the daughter of Gaoyou officer Zhang Shenjian and secretly relied on him as support.
translations.idiomatic: burning with fear and resentment inside, he married his son to the daughter of the Gaoyou officer Zhang Shenjian and quietly looked to him for backing.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠方攻秦宗權，駢慮其奔突，使師鐸率兵逾都梁山，不見賊還。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then attacking Qin Zongquan; Pian feared he would raid in a rush and had Shiduo lead troops over Duliang Mountain. He saw no bandits and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong was attacking Qin Zongquan. Fearing a sudden raid, Pian sent Shiduo with troops over Duliang Mountain. He found no enemy and came back.

sentences.zh: 師鐸見駢府宿將多以讒死，憂甚。

translations.literal: Shiduo saw that many veteran generals of Pian's mansion had died by slander and was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo saw how many of Pian's veteran generals had been destroyed by slander and grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 用之益加禮，師鐸愈恐，謀於神劍。

translations.literal: Yongzhi increased his courtesy all the more; Shiduo grew more fearful and plotted with Shenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi heaped still more honors on him. Shiduo grew more afraid and took counsel with Shenjian.

sentences.zh: 神劍不然其言，而猜嫌日結。

translations.literal: Shenjian did not agree with his words, yet suspicion and resentment daily tightened.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjian did not accept his plan, yet suspicion between them deepened day by day.

sentences.zh: 用之亦慮其變，內欲除之，亟請罷屯。

translations.literal: Yongzhi also feared his mutiny, inwardly wished to eliminate him, and urgently requested that the garrison be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi also feared a revolt and inwardly meant to destroy him, urgently pressing to withdraw the garrison.

sentences.zh: 其母密擿師鐸使去，曰：「毋顧家室。」

translations.literal: His mother secretly urged Shiduo to go, saying: "Do not care for wife and household."
translations.idiomatic: His mother secretly urged him to flee, saying, "Do not think of wife or home."

sentences.zh: 師鐸憂，未知所出。

translations.literal: Shiduo was anxious and did not know where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo was torn with anxiety and did not know what course to take.

sentences.zh: 而駢子怒用之專恣，覬師鐸與諸將發其奸，遣使謂師鐸曰：「用之欲因此行圖君，既授書神劍矣，君其備之！」

translations.literal: But Pian's son, angry at Yongzhi's arbitrary power, hoped Shiduo with the generals would expose his fraud and sent a messenger telling Shiduo: "Yongzhi wishes to use this expedition to plot against you; he has already given a letter to Shenjian—you must prepare!"
translations.idiomatic: Pian's son, furious at Yongzhi's arrogance, hoped Shiduo and the other generals would expose his crimes. He sent a messenger who told Shiduo, "Yongzhi means to use this march to destroy you. He has already written to Shenjian. You must be ready!"

sentences.zh: 師鐸驚，軍中稍稍傳言。

translations.literal: Shiduo was startled, and in the army rumors gradually spread.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo was shaken, and whispers began to spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 諸將介而見，請殺神劍，並其軍，驅市人以濟亂。

translations.literal: The generals came in armor to audience and asked to kill Shenjian, take his army, and drive market people to aid the disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The generals came before him in armor and urged him to kill Shenjian, seize his troops, and rouse the townspeople to join the revolt.

sentences.zh: 師鐸曰：「不可，我若重擾百姓，復一用之也。

translations.literal: Shiduo said: "It cannot be done. If I again trouble the common people, I become another Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo said, "No. If I terrorize the people again, I am no better than Yongzhi.

sentences.zh: 鄭漢璋素與我善，兵精士強，以用之用事，常不平。

translations.literal: Zheng Hanzhang has always been on good terms with me; his troops are elite and his soldiers strong. Because Yongzhi holds power he is often discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hanzhang has always been friendly to me. His troops are first-rate and his men are strong. He has long resented Yongzhi's rule.

sentences.zh: 今若告之謀，彼必喜，則事濟矣。」

translations.literal: If we now tell him the plot, he will surely rejoice, and then the affair will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: If we tell him our plan now, he will surely join us, and the thing will be done."

sentences.zh: 眾然之。

translations.literal: The crowd agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The others agreed.

sentences.zh: 神劍未知，方椎牛釃酒，且將犒師。

translations.literal: Shenjian did not know; he was butchering cattle and pouring wine, about to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjian knew nothing of it. He was slaughtering cattle and broaching wine to feast his men.

sentences.zh: 師鐸潛師夜出，士皆絳繒抹首，且行且掠。

translations.literal: Shiduo secretly led troops out at night; the soldiers all wrapped their heads in crimson silk, marching and plundering as they went.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo stole away by night with his men, all with crimson silk bound about their heads, looting as they marched.

sentences.zh: 漢璋聞，以麾下出迎，師鐸諗以計，大喜。

translations.literal: Hanzhang heard and led his forces out to welcome him; Shiduo whispered the plan, and he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang heard and marched out with his men to meet him. When Shiduo confided the plan, Hanzhang was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 留其妻守淮口，帥兵及亡命數千至高郵，見神劍，詰其變，神劍辭不知。

translations.literal: He left his wife to guard Huaikou, led troops and several thousand fugitives to Gaoyou, saw Shenjian, and interrogated him about the change; Shenjian pleaded ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: He left his wife to hold Huaikou, led several thousand troops and outlaws to Gaoyou, confronted Shenjian, and demanded to know why he had turned. Shenjian swore he knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 師鐸語稍侵，神劍瞋目曰：「大夫何晚計！

translations.literal: Shiduo's words grew slightly invasive; Shenjian glared and said: "Sir, why so late in your reckoning!
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo's tone turned sharp. Shenjian glared and said, "Sir, why did you wait so long!

sentences.zh: 彼一妖人，前假嶺南節，不肯行，誌圖淮海，令君既奪魄，彼一日得誌，吾能握刀頭北面事之邪！

translations.literal: That one sorcerer before falsely took the Lingnan post and would not go, his ambition set on Huai and Hai. He has already stolen your spirit—if one day he succeeds, can I hold a blade and face north to serve him!
translations.idiomatic: That sorcerer was given a false post in Lingnan and would not leave. His aim is the Huai and the sea. He has already broken your nerve. If he ever gets his way, do you think I would sheath my sword and bow north to serve him?

sentences.zh: 吾前未量君意，故不出口，尚何疑？」

translations.literal: I before did not gauge your intent, so did not speak out—what doubt remains?"
translations.idiomatic: I did not know where you stood before, so I held my tongue. What is there left to doubt?"

sentences.zh: 漢璋喜，取酒割臂血而盟，推師鐸為大丞相，作誓告神，乃移檄州縣，以誅呂用之、張守一、諸葛殷為名。

translations.literal: Hanzhang rejoiced, took wine and cut arm blood to ally, pushed Shiduo as Great Chancellor, made oath and reported to the spirits, then moved proclamations to prefectures and counties in the name of executing Lü Yongzhi, Zhang Shouyi, and Zhuge Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang rejoiced. They poured wine, cut their arms, and mixed blood in oath. They made Shiduo Great Chancellor, swore before the gods, and issued proclamations to the prefectures and counties in the name of executing Lü Yongzhi, Zhang Shouyi, and Zhuge Yin.

sentences.zh: 神劍以高郵兵諸校倪詳、褾並以天長子弟會，唐宏為先鋒，駱玄真主騎，趙簡主徒，王朗為殿，得勝兵三千。

translations.literal: Shenjian with Gaoyou army various officers Ni Xiang and Biao, together with Tianchang district youths assembled; Tang Hong as vanguard, Luo Xuanzhen commanding cavalry, Zhao Jian infantry, Wang Lang rear guard—they obtained three thousand victorious troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjian rallied the Gaoyou garrison under officers Ni Xiang and Biao, joined by youths from Tianchang. Tang Hong led the van, Luo Xuanzhen the horse, Zhao Jian the foot, and Wang Lang the rear. They mustered three thousand seasoned men.

sentences.zh: 將發，神劍中悔，繆曰：「公兵雖精，然城堅，旬日不下則糧乏，眾心搖矣。

translations.literal: About to set out, Shenjian midway regretted and falsely said: "Your troops though elite, yet the walls are firm—if in ten days you do not take it, grain will be exhausted and hearts will waver.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to march, Shenjian had second thoughts and invented an excuse: "Your men are strong, but the walls are stout. If the city does not fall in ten days, grain will run out and morale will crack.

sentences.zh: 神劍請按軍高郵，為公聲援而督糧道。」

translations.literal: Shenjian asked to hold the army at Gaoyou, for you make sound support and supervise the grain route."
translations.idiomatic: Let me hold Gaoyou, he said, to support you from the rear and keep the supply line open."

sentences.zh: 師鐸曰：「民稟尚多，何患資儲？

translations.literal: Shiduo said: "The people's stores are still plentiful—what worry for provisions?
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo said, "The people's granaries are still full. Why worry about supplies?

sentences.zh: 城中攜離無鬥誌，何事聲援？

translations.literal: Within the city families are divided and there is no fighting will—what need for reinforcement?
translations.idiomatic: The city is already splitting apart and has no will to fight. What need is there for reinforcements?

sentences.zh: 君意不行，孰敢違？」

translations.literal: If your intent does not go, who dares disobey?"
translations.idiomatic: If you will not march, who dares defy you?"

sentences.zh: 漢璋內忌神劍，恐不為己下，勸許其計，約城破玉帛子女共之。

translations.literal: Hanzhang inwardly resented Shenjian, fearing he would not be beneath himself, urged agreeing to his plan, and pledged that when the city fell they would share jade, silk, women, and children.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang secretly resented Shenjian and feared he would not submit afterward. He urged Shiduo to accept the plan and promised that when the city fell they would divide the loot, silk, women, and children between them.

sentences.zh: 其四月，兵傅城，營其下。

translations.literal: In that fourth month the army approached the walls and camped below them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the army reached the walls and pitched camp beneath them.

sentences.zh: 城中駭亂，用之分兵守，且自督戰。

translations.literal: Within the city there was panic and chaos; Yongzhi divided troops to guard and himself supervised battle.
translations.idiomatic: Panic seized the city. Yongzhi divided his forces to man the defenses and took command of the fighting himself.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「斬一級，賞金一餅。」

translations.literal: His order said: "Cut off one head, reward one gold cake."
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed, "One head cut off, one gold cake in reward."

sentences.zh: 士多山東人，堅悍頗用命。

translations.literal: The soldiers were mostly men of Shandong, sturdy and fierce, and quite obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his men were Shandongers, hard and fierce, and they fought with grim obedience.

sentences.zh: 師鐸懼，退舍自固。

translations.literal: Shiduo feared and withdrew his camp to fortify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo grew afraid, pulled back, and entrenched his camp.

sentences.zh: 用之稍堙塞諸門。

translations.literal: Yongzhi gradually filled and blocked the various gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi began to fill in and seal the city gates one by one.

sentences.zh: 駢登延和閣，聞囂甚，左右告之故，大驚，召用之問狀，徐曰：「師鐸眾思歸，為門衛所軋，隨已處置，不爾，煩玄女一符耳！」

translations.literal: Pian ascended the Yanhe Pavilion, heard the uproar was extreme; attendants told him the reason and he was greatly startled. He summoned Yongzhi to ask the situation; slowly he said: "Shiduo's masses think of returning and were squeezed by gate guards—it has already been handled. Otherwise, it would trouble the Dark Lady for one talisman only!"
translations.idiomatic: Pian climbed the Yanhe Pavilion and heard a great uproar. When his attendants told him why, he was thunderstruck. He summoned Yongzhi and asked what was happening. Yongzhi said calmly, "Shiduo's men only wanted to go home and were stopped at the gates. It is already taken care of. Otherwise I would need but one talisman from the Dark Lady!"

sentences.zh: 駢曰：「吾覺爾之誕多矣，善自為之，勿使吾為周寶也！」

translations.literal: Pian said: "I feel your deceptions are many already—handle yourself well and do not make me become Zhou Bao!"
translations.idiomatic: Pian said, "I have caught you in too many lies already. See to it yourself, and do not make me another Zhou Bao!"

sentences.zh: 時寶已為下所逐出奔雲。

translations.literal: At that time Bao had already been driven out by subordinates below and fled to Yun.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhou Bao had already been driven out by his own men and fled toward Yun.

sentences.zh: 用之慚，不復有言。

translations.literal: Yongzhi was ashamed and had no more words.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi was shamed into silence.

sentences.zh: 師鐸見城未下，頗懼，求救於宣州秦彥，約事平迎以代駢。

translations.literal: Shiduo saw the city was not taken and was quite afraid; he begged rescue from Xuanzhou's Qin Yan and agreed that when the affair was pacified he would welcome him to replace Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo, seeing the city still untaken, grew afraid and begged Qin Yan of Xuanzhou for aid, promising to install him in Pian's place once the city fell.

sentences.zh: 駢數責用之曰：「始吾以心腹任君，君禦下無方，卒誤我。

translations.literal: Pian repeatedly blamed Yongzhi, saying: "At first I trusted you as heart-and-belly; you governed subordinates without method and finally wronged me.
translations.idiomatic: Pian rebuked Yongzhi again and again: "I once trusted you as my own flesh. You ruled your men without sense and have ruined me in the end.

sentences.zh: 今百姓饑饉，不可虐用，當遣大將賫吾書諭之，使罷兵。」

translations.literal: Now the common people are hungry in famine—you cannot cruelly use force. You should send a great general bearing my letter to instruct them and make them cease troops."
translations.idiomatic: The people are starving. You must not abuse them further. Send a senior general with my letter to order them to lay down arms."

sentences.zh: 用之疑諸將不為用，以其黨許戡奉書往。

translations.literal: Yongzhi suspected the generals would not obey him and sent his clique member Xu Kan to bear the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi feared the generals would not obey him and sent his own man Xu Kan with the letter.

sentences.zh: 始師鐸意駢令宿將勞軍，因得口陳用之罪。

translations.literal: At first Shiduo thought Pian had ordered veteran generals to console the army and thus he could mouth-state Yongzhi's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shiduo thought Pian had sent veteran generals to reason with the army so he could speak Yongzhi's crimes aloud.

sentences.zh: 及戡至，大怒曰：「梁纘、韓問安在？

translations.literal: When Kan arrived he was greatly angry and said: "Where are Liang Zuan and Han Wen'an?
translations.idiomatic: When Kan arrived, Shiduo flew into a rage and cried, "Where are Liang Zuan and Han Wen'an?

sentences.zh: 若何庸來！」

translations.literal: Why has this mediocre fellow come!"
translations.idiomatic: Why send this worthless man!"

sentences.zh: 即斬之。

translations.literal: He was immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He had Kan beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 乃系書射城內，用之不發，即火之。

translations.literal: He then tied the letter and shot it into the city; Yongzhi would not open it and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: He tied Pian's letter to an arrow and shot it into the city. Yongzhi would not open it and had it burned.

sentences.zh: 它日以甲士百人入謁，駢驚匿內寢，少選乃出，叱曰：「得非反邪？」

translations.literal: Another day he entered audience with a hundred armored soldiers; Pian startled hid in the inner chamber, and shortly after came out, shouting: "Could this be rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day Yongzhi entered with a hundred armored men. Pian fled in alarm to his inner chamber, then came out after a moment and shouted, "Are you rebelling?"

sentences.zh: 命左右驅出。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to drive them out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to throw them out.

sentences.zh: 用之至南門，舉策曰：「吾不復入是矣！」

translations.literal: Yongzhi reached the south gate, raised his whip, and said: "I will not enter this again!"
translations.idiomatic: At the south gate Yongzhi raised his whip and cried, "I will never pass through here again!"

sentences.zh: 始與駢貳。

translations.literal: He first parted ways with Pian.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment he and Pian were at odds.

sentences.zh: 師鐸壁揚子，發民廬舍治攻具。

translations.literal: Shiduo entrenched at Yangzi, mobilized the people's houses to repair siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo encamped on the Yangzi bank, tore down people's houses, and built siege engines.

sentences.zh: 用之大索居人馬及丁壯，驍將以長刀擁脅乘城，晝夜不得息。

translations.literal: Yongzhi greatly searched residents for horses and able-bodied men; fierce generals with long knives compelled them onto the walls day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi combed the city for horses and able-bodied men. Fierce officers drove them onto the walls at sword point, day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 又疑為間，數易區處，家有馌餉，皆相失，至饑死者相枕藉。

translations.literal: He also suspected them as spies and repeatedly changed their districts; families who had food carried to the walls all lost one another, until the starved dead lay head to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: He also suspected treachery and kept shifting people from quarter to quarter. Families bringing food to the walls lost one another, and the dead from hunger lay piled in heaps.

sentences.zh: 駢召大將古鍔賫師鐸母書及其子出諭，師鐸遣子還曰：「不敢負恩，朝斬兇人，夕還屯，願以妻子為質。」

translations.literal: Pian summoned great general Gu E to bear Shiduo's mother's letter and his son out to instruct him; Shiduo sent his son back saying: "I dare not betray grace—morning behead the villain, evening return to camp; I wish to offer wife and children as hostages."
translations.idiomatic: Pian sent the general Gu E with a letter from Shiduo's mother and with Shiduo's son to plead with him. Shiduo sent his son back with the reply, "I have not forgotten your kindness. Slay the villain at dawn and I will return to camp by dusk. Let my wife and children stand as hostages."

sentences.zh: 駢恐用之屠其家，乃收置署中。

translations.literal: Pian feared Yongzhi would slaughter his family and therefore collected and placed them in the office.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yongzhi would slaughter them, Pian took the family into his own compound for safekeeping.

sentences.zh: 會秦彥遣秦稠率兵與師鐸合，攻益急，守陴者夜焚南柵以應於外，師鐸入，守將張全乃戰死，用之距三橋，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: It happened that Qin Yan sent Qin Chou leading troops to unite with Shiduo; the attack grew more urgent. Wall defenders by night burned the south palisade to respond outside; Shiduo entered; defending general Zhang Quan then died in battle; Yongzhi resisted at Three Bridges, kill and wound equal.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan sent Qin Chou with reinforcements to join Shiduo, and the assault grew fiercer. Defenders burned the southern palisade by night to signal the allies outside. Shiduo broke in. The defender Zhang Quan fell fighting. Yongzhi held the Three Bridges, and casualties mounted on both sides.

sentences.zh: 駢從子傑率牙兵將執用之以畀師鐸，左鏌邪兵復斷其後，用之懼，乃出奔。

translations.literal: Pian's nephew Jie led palace guard soldiers about to seize Yongzhi to hand to Shiduo; the Left Moye Army again cut his rear; Yongzhi feared and then fled out.
translations.idiomatic: Pian's nephew Jie led the guard to seize Yongzhi and hand him to Shiduo, but the Left Moye Army cut off their rear. Yongzhi panicked and fled the city.

sentences.zh: 駢召梁纘謝曰：「初不用子計以及此，庸何追？」

translations.literal: Pian summoned Liang Zuan and apologized, saying: "At first I did not use your plan and reached this—what use in pursuing now?"
translations.idiomatic: Pian summoned Liang Zuan and said in apology, "I ignored your counsel and have come to this. What good is regret now?"

sentences.zh: 授以兵，使保子城。

translations.literal: He gave him troops and made him guard the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him troops and ordered him to hold the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 遲明師鐸縱火大掠，駢乃命徹備，改服須其入。

translations.literal: At dawn Shiduo set fires and plundered greatly; Pian then ordered defenses withdrawn, changed clothes, and awaited his entry.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Bi Shiduo set fire and looted the city. Gao Pian ordered the guard stood down, changed his robes, and waited for him to enter.

sentences.zh: 師鐸見延和閣，駢待之如賓，即署師鐸節度副使，漢璋、神劍以次授署，秦稠封府庫以待，師鐸去丞相號。

translations.literal: Shiduo came to Yanhe Pavilion; Pian received him as a guest; at once appointed Shiduo deputy military commissioner; Hanzhang and Shenjian received appointments in turn; Qin Chou sealed the treasury to await him; Shiduo removed the title Prime Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Shiduo came to the Yanhe Pavilion, where Pian received him as an honored guest. He at once made Shiduo his deputy commissioner, appointed Zheng Hanzhang and Zhang Shenjian in their turn, and had Qin Chou seal the treasury. Shiduo abandoned the title of prime minister.

sentences.zh: 於時何衛未謹，駢愛將申及說駢曰：「逆人兵少弛，願奉公夜出，發諸鎮兵，還刷大恥，賊不足平也。

translations.literal: At that time He Wei was not cautious; Pian's beloved general Shen Ji persuaded Pian, saying: "The rebel troops are somewhat relaxed; I wish to escort you out by night, raise the garrison armies, return to wipe away the great shame—the rebels are not enough to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: He Wei was then careless in his guard. Shen Ji, a favored general, urged Pian: "The rebels' lines have slackened. Let me lead you out by night, summon troops from the neighboring prefectures, and wash away this disgrace—the enemy will not stand.

sentences.zh: 若不決，則及將不得侍公。」

translations.literal: If you do not decide, then when it comes, your generals will not be able to attend you."
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate, your officers may no longer be able to reach you."

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: He wept.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down weeping.

sentences.zh: 駢恇怯不能用其策，及乃匿去。

translations.literal: Pian was cowardly and timid, could not use his stratagem; Ji then hid and left.
translations.idiomatic: Cowed and timid, Pian refused the plan. Shen Ji slipped away in secret.

sentences.zh: 師鐸誅用之支黨數十，使孫約迎秦彥。

translations.literal: Shiduo executed dozens from Yongzhi's faction and sent Sun Yue to welcome Qin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo executed dozens from Yongzhi's faction and sent Sun Yue to bring in Qin Yan.

sentences.zh: 彥者，徐州人，本名立，隸伍籍。

translations.literal: Yan—a man of Xuzhou, original name Li, enrolled under Wu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan was a native of Xuzhou, born Li, and had served under Wu Ji.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，以盜繫獄且死，夢謼曰：「秦彥，而從我去！」

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era, for theft he was imprisoned and about to die; he dreamed a voice shouting: "Qin Yan, you follow me away!"
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu reign he was jailed for robbery and doomed to die, but dreamed a voice crying, "Qin Yan, come away with me!"

sentences.zh: 寤而視械破，因得亡命，即名彥。

translations.literal: Waking he saw shackles broken, thus escaped with his life, and at once took the name Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He woke to find his fetters shattered, fled for his life, and took the name Yan.

sentences.zh: 聚徒百人，殺下邳令，取其貲，入黃巢黨中。

translations.literal: He gathered followers a hundred, killed the magistrate of Xiapi, took his goods, and entered Huang Chao's party.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered a hundred men, killed the magistrate of Xiapi and seized his goods, and joined Huang Chao's cause.

sentences.zh: 既敗，與許降駢，累表和州刺史。

translations.literal: After defeat, together with Xu he surrendered to Pian; through repeated memorials he became Hezhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat he surrendered with Xu to Pian and through repeated petitions became prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 中和初，宣歙觀察使竇潏病，彥襲而代之。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhonghe reign, Xuanshe observation commissioner Dou Yu fell ill; Yan attacked and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhonghe reign Dou Yu, commissioner of Xuanshe, fell ill; Yan seized the post and replaced him.

sentences.zh: 師鐸之召彥也，或計曰：「足下向誅妖人，故下樂從。

translations.literal: When Shiduo summoned Yan, someone strategized, saying: "Your Excellency formerly executed the demon-man, therefore the lower ranks gladly followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiduo summoned Qin Yan, an advisor said, "You slew the sorcerer and the men followed you gladly.

sentences.zh: 今軍府已安，宜還政高公，足下身典兵，權在掌握，四鄰聞之，不失大義，諸將未敢謀也。

translations.literal: Now the military office is already secure; you ought to return government to Lord Gao; your Excellency personally holds the army, power in your grasp; the four neighbors hearing it would not lose great righteousness; the generals would not dare to scheme.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters are secure. Restore authority to Lord Gao while you keep command—the neighbors will call it righteous and no officer will dare plot against you.

sentences.zh: 若令彥為帥，兵非足下有也。

translations.literal: If you make Yan commander, the troops will not be under your Excellency.
translations.idiomatic: If Yan becomes commander, the army will no longer be yours.

sentences.zh: 且秦稠封府庫，勢已相疑。

translations.literal: Moreover Qin Chou sealed the treasury—momentum already mutually suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Qin Chou has sealed the treasury—you are already at odds.

sentences.zh: 足下如厚德彥，宜以金玉子女報之，勿聽度江。

translations.literal: If your Excellency wishes thick virtue toward Yan, you ought to repay with gold, jade, sons and daughters; do not listen to crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: If you owe Yan a debt of gratitude, repay him with gold, jade, and marriage gifts, but do not let him cross the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 假足下能下彥，楊行密夕聞而朝必至。」

translations.literal: Supposing your Excellency could dismiss Yan, Yang Xingmi would hear by evening and by morning certainly arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Even if you could send Yan away, Yang Xingmi would hear by nightfall and be here by dawn."

sentences.zh: 師鐸不決，以告漢璋。

translations.literal: Shiduo could not decide and told Hanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo could not decide and consulted Hanzhang.

sentences.zh: 漢璋曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Hanzhang said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 師鐸出駢，囚南第。

translations.literal: Shiduo moved Pian out and imprisoned him in the southern residence.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo removed Pian and imprisoned him in the southern compound.

sentences.zh: 稠麾下求無厭，燒貢奉樓數十楹，取珍寶。

translations.literal: Chou's subordinates' demands were insatiable; they burned dozens of bays of the tribute lodge and took treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Chou's men were insatiable—they burned dozens of bays of the tribute hall and looted the treasures.

sentences.zh: 始駢自乾符以來，貢獻不入天子，貲貨山積，私置郊祀、元會供帳什器，殫極功巧，至是為亂兵所剽略盡。

translations.literal: From the beginning, since Pian from the Qianfu era onward tribute did not enter the Son of Heaven; goods and wealth piled like mountains; he privately set out suburban sacrifice and New Year assembly supply banners and utensils, exhausted with utmost craft—by this time rebel troops plundered it all.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qianfu era Pian had withheld tribute to the throne and heaped wealth like mountains, privately amassing regalia for state rites—all of it was now stripped bare by the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 師鐸徙駢東第。

translations.literal: Shiduo relocated Pian to the eastern residence.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo moved Pian to the eastern compound.

sentences.zh: 禽諸葛殷，腰下得金數斤，百姓交唾，拔須發無遺，再縊乃絕，仇家其目雲，市人投瓦礫擊屍，俄而成冢。

translations.literal: They captured Zhuge Yin; from his waist they obtained several jin of gold; common people together spat on him; they pulled out every hair and whisker; hanged him twice before he died; enemies gouged out his eyes it is said; market people threw tiles and stones striking the corpse; soon it became a mound.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Zhuge Yin and found several jin of gold on him. The crowd spat on him, tore out every hair and whisker, and hanged him twice before he died. Enemies gouged out his eyes, townsfolk pelted the corpse with rubble until it lay in a mound.

sentences.zh: 駢出金遺守者，師鐸知之，加兵苛督，復入囚署中，子弟十餘人同幽之。

translations.literal: Pian gave out gold to bribe the guards; Shiduo knew it, added troops with harsh supervision, thrust him back into imprisonment in the office; more than ten sons and younger brothers were confined together.
translations.idiomatic: Pian bribed his guards with gold. Shiduo found out, redoubled the watch, and thrust him back into the jail compound with more than a dozen kin imprisoned beside him.

sentences.zh: 顧雲入見，駢猶自若曰：「吾復居此，天時人事必有在。」

translations.literal: Gu Yun entered to see him; Pian was still composed and said: "I again dwell here—heaven's seasons and human affairs surely must have their place."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yun came to visit. Pian was still unruffled. "I will dwell here again—heaven and circumstance must yet have their turn."

sentences.zh: 意師鐸復推立之。

translations.literal: He intended that Shiduo would again elevate and establish him.
translations.idiomatic: He expected Bi Shiduo to restore him to power.

sentences.zh: 用之既出，以兵攻淮口未下，鄭漢璋擊之，遂奔天長。

translations.literal: Yongzhi having left, with troops attacked Huaikou but did not take it; Zheng Hanzhang struck him; then he fled to Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi had fled and was besieging Huaikou without success when Zheng Hanzhang routed him; he fled to Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 初，用之詐為駢書，召兵於廬、壽，城陷，而楊行密兵萬人次天長，用之自歸。

translations.literal: Initially Yongzhi forged Pian's letter, summoned troops from Lu and Shou; the city fell, while Yang Xingmi's ten-thousand troops garrisoned Tianchang; Yongzhi himself returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi had forged letters in Pian's name to summon troops from Lu and Shou. The city was lost, Yang Xingmi had ten thousand men at Tianchang, and Yongzhi surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 張神劍求賂於師鐸，辭以彥未至。

translations.literal: Zhang Shenjian sought bribes from Shiduo; he declined on grounds Yan had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shenjian demanded a payoff from Shiduo, who put him off saying Qin Yan had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 神劍怒，與別將高霸將攻師鐸。

translations.literal: Shenjian was angry; with deputy general Gao Ba he led troops to attack Shiduo.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjian flew into a rage and with the officer Gao Ba marched against Shiduo.

sentences.zh: 彥之來，召池州刺史趙锽守宣，自將入揚州，稱節度使，以師鐸為行軍司馬，居用之第，不得在牙中。

translations.literal: When Yan came, he summoned Chizhou prefect Zhao Wei to guard Xuan, himself led troops into Yangzhou, styled himself military commissioner, made Shiduo campaigning marshal, had him dwell in Yongzhi's residence, and barred him from headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan arrived, left Zhao Wei of Chizhou to hold Xuancheng, and entered Yangzhou in person as self-styled commissioner. He made Shiduo his campaigning marshal, gave him Yongzhi's old quarters, and barred him from headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師鐸怏怏失誌。

translations.literal: Shiduo resentfully lost his will.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo seethed, his ambition undone.

sentences.zh: 行密與神劍等連和，自江北至槐家橋，柵壘相聯。

translations.literal: Xingmi with Shenjian and others allied; from north of the river to Huaijia Bridge, palisades and ramparts linked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi joined Shenjian and the rest, ranging from the north bank to Huaijia Bridge with linked camps and palisades.

sentences.zh: 彥登城望之，色沮，乃授鄭漢璋、唐宏等兵屯門，樵蘇道絕，食且乏。

translations.literal: Yan ascended the wall to look; his color sank; then he entrusted Zheng Hanzhang, Tang Hong, and others with troops to garrison the gates; firewood and fodder routes were cut off; food was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan climbed the wall to look and his spirit faltered. He posted Zheng Hanzhang, Tang Hong, and others at the gates. Foraging routes were cut and provisions nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 稠及師鐸以勁卒八千出戰，大敗，稠死之，士奔溺死者十八。

translations.literal: Chou and Shiduo with crack troops eight thousand went out to battle and were greatly defeated; Chou died; of soldiers who fled, eight or nine in ten drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Chou and Shiduo led eight thousand elite troops out and were crushed. Chou was killed, and eight or nine in ten of the army drowned in flight.

sentences.zh: 彥大出金求救於張雄，雄引兵至東塘，得金，不戰去。

translations.literal: Yan greatly paid out gold to beg rescue from Zhang Xiong; Xiong led troops to Dongtang, got the gold, and left without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan poured out gold to beg Zhang Xiong for aid. Xiong marched to Dongtang, took the gold, and withdrew without fighting.

sentences.zh: 彥使師鐸率兵二萬陣城下，漢璋為前鋒，宏次之，駱玄真、樊約又次之，師鐸、王朗以騎為左右翼。

translations.literal: Yan ordered Shiduo to lead twenty thousand troops arrayed below the city; Hanzhang as vanguard; Hong next; Luo Xuanzhen and Fan Yue again next; Shiduo and Wang Lang with cavalry as left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan sent Shiduo with twenty thousand men to deploy beneath the walls—Hanzhang in the van, Hong behind him, then Luo Xuanzhen and Fan Yue, with Shiduo and Wang Lang commanding the cavalry wings.

sentences.zh: 既成列，久之，行密乃出，委輜重於壁，以羸兵守之，伏精卒數千其旁。

translations.literal: Having formed ranks, after a long while Xingmi then came out, left baggage and heavy goods at the rampart, used weak troops to guard them, and hid several thousand elite soldiers beside them.
translations.idiomatic: When the lines were set, Yang Xingmi at last came forth. He left his baggage at the wall with weak troops to guard it and hid several thousand veterans nearby.

sentences.zh: 行密先犯玄真，短兵接，偽北，師鐸諸軍奔其壁，爭取金玉貲糧。

translations.literal: Xingmi first struck Xuanzhen; close combat joined; he feigned retreat north; Shiduo's various armies ran to his rampart, scrambling for gold, jade, goods, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi engaged Xuanzhen in close fighting, then feigned retreat. Shiduo's entire host rushed the wall to seize gold, jade, grain, and stores.

sentences.zh: 伏噪而出，行密引輕兵躡其尾，俘殺旁午，橫屍十里。

translations.literal: The ambush cried out and emerged; Xingmi led light troops to tread their tail; captives and kills crisscrossed; corpses stretched across ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush erupted with a shout. Xingmi's light troops took them from behind. Captives and corpses piled up until the dead lay across ten li.

sentences.zh: 師鐸等奔還，玄真戰死。

translations.literal: Shiduo and others ran back; Xuanzhen died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo and the rest fled in rout. Xuanzhen was killed in the fight.

sentences.zh: 師鐸雅倚玄真驍敢能拒敵，既失之，惋沮彌日，不復議出戰矣。

translations.literal: Shiduo had always relied on Xuanzhen's fierce courage able to resist the enemy; having lost him, regret and dejection for days—no longer discussed going out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo had always leaned on Xuanzhen's fierce prowess in battle. With him gone, Shiduo brooded for days and would not speak of fighting again.

sentences.zh: 駢久囚拘，供億窘狹，群奴徹延和閣闌楯為薪，煮革帶以食。

translations.literal: Pian long imprisoned; supplies cramped; slave attendants dismantled Yanhe Pavilion balustrades and shields for fuel, boiled leather belts for food.
translations.idiomatic: Long confinement had left Pian destitute. His slaves tore down the Yanhe Pavilion's balustrades for firewood and boiled leather belts to eat.

sentences.zh: 駢召幕府盧涚曰：「予粗立功，比求清凈，非與此世爭利害，今而及此，神道何望邪？」

translations.literal: Pian summoned staff member Lu Song, saying: "I roughly established merit, lately sought purity and quiet—was not contending profit and harm with this world; now to reach this—what hope in the spirit way?"
translations.idiomatic: Pian summoned his aide Lu Song. "I won some merit and sought only peace, not strife with the world. That it has come to this—what can heaven intend?"

sentences.zh: 涕下不能已。

translations.literal: Tears flowed; he could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down without end.

sentences.zh: 師鐸既敗，慮駢內應。

translations.literal: Shiduo having been defeated, feared Pian might respond from within.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat Shiduo feared Pian might stir rebellion within the walls.

sentences.zh: 有女巫王奉仙謂師鐸曰：「揚州災，有大人死，可以厭。」

translations.literal: There was a shamaness Wang Fengxian who told Shiduo: "Yangzhou's disaster—a great man must die—can be appeased."
translations.idiomatic: A shamaness, Wang Fengxian, told Shiduo, "Yangzhou's doom requires a great man's death to lift the curse."

sentences.zh: 彥曰：「非高公邪？」

translations.literal: Yan said: "Is it not Lord Gao?"
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yan said, "Surely that means Lord Gao?"

sentences.zh: 命左右陳賞等往殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants Chen Shang and others to go kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chen Shang and his men to go and kill him.

sentences.zh: 侍者白有賊，駢曰：「此必秦彥來。」

translations.literal: Attendants reported there were bandits; Pian said: "This must be Qin Yan coming."
translations.idiomatic: A servant cried that bandits were approaching. Pian said, "That must be Qin Yan."

sentences.zh: 正色須之。

translations.literal: He composed his bearing and awaited him.
translations.idiomatic: He composed himself and waited.

sentences.zh: 眾入，駢罵曰：「軍事有監軍及諸將在，何遽爾？」

translations.literal: The crowd entered; Pian cursed: "Military affairs have the military supervisor and the various generals present—why so hastily thus?"
translations.idiomatic: They burst in. Pian shouted, "The army inspector and the generals still hold authority—what is this haste?"

sentences.zh: 眾辟易，有奮而擊駢者，曳廷下數之曰：「公負天子恩，陷人塗炭，罪多矣，尚何雲？」

translations.literal: The crowd shrank back; one who sprang forward struck Pian, dragged him below the hall and counted his crimes: "Lord, you betrayed the Son of Heaven's grace, plunged people into charcoal and flame—crimes are many; what more to say?"
translations.idiomatic: The mob fell back, then someone struck him, dragged him into the courtyard, and reviled him: "You betrayed the Son of Heaven and plunged the realm into misery—your crimes are beyond reckoning. What more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 駢未暇答，仰首如有所伺，即斬之。

translations.literal: Pian had no leisure to answer; he raised his head as if looking for something; then they beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could reply, he lifted his face as if watching the sky—and they struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 左右奴客遁歸行密，行密舉軍縞素，大臨而祭，獨用之缞服哭三日。

translations.literal: Left and right slave retainers escaped and returned to Xingmi; Xingmi raised the army in white hemp, held great mourning and sacrifice; only Yongzhi in hemp mourning garb wept three days.
translations.idiomatic: Pian's servants fled to Yang Xingmi, who draped his army in mourning white and held a grand memorial. Yongzhi alone wore hemp and mourned three days.

sentences.zh: 彥屢敗，軍氣摧喪，與師鐸抱膝相視無它略，更問奉仙，賞罰輕重皆自出。

translations.literal: Yan repeatedly defeated; army spirit crushed and lost; with Shiduo hugged knees gazing at each other without other stratagem; again asked Fengxian—rewards and punishments, light and heavy, all issued from her.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated defeats broke the army's spirit. Yan and Shiduo sat knee to knee with no plan left but to ask Fengxian again—for rewards and punishments alike followed her word.

sentences.zh: 彥遣漢璋擊神劍，破之。

translations.literal: Yan sent Hanzhang to strike Shenjian and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Hanzhang against Shenjian and routed him.

sentences.zh: 神劍奔高郵，漢璋欲窮追，會大雨還。

translations.literal: Shenjian fled to Gaoyou; Hanzhang wished to pursue to the end; met with great rain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjian fled to Gaoyou. Hanzhang meant to run him down but turned back in a torrential rain.

sentences.zh: 行密以城尚堅，師且老，議解去。

translations.literal: Xingmi because the city was still solid and troops were also weary, discussed lifting the siege and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi, seeing the walls still strong and his troops worn, considered raising the siege.

sentences.zh: 用之裨將晨伏兵四壕，伺守者休代，引而登，殺數十人於門，以招外兵。

translations.literal: Yongzhi's deputy at dawn hid troops at the four moats, watched for guards to rest at relief, led them up, killed several tens at the gate, to summon outer troops.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yongzhi's lieutenant hid men by the four ditches, waited until the reliefs rested, scaled the wall, killed dozens at the gate, and signaled the army outside.

sentences.zh: 守軍亦厭苦，皆委兵潰。

translations.literal: The defending army was also weary and bitter; all cast aside weapons and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders too were exhausted and threw down their arms in rout.

sentences.zh: 師鐸與其家及彥奔東塘，人爭出，相騰藉死，壕塹幾滿，王朗踣而殞。

translations.literal: Shiduo with his family and Yan fled to Dongtang; people scrambled to exit, trampling one another dead; moats and ditches nearly full; Wang Lang stumbled and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo fled with his kin and Qin Yan toward Dongtang. The crowd crushed one another at the gates until the moats nearly filled; Wang Lang was trampled to death.

sentences.zh: 行密既入，殺梁纘於牙門，以不死高氏難。

translations.literal: Xingmi having entered, killed Liang Zuan at the headquarters gate, using the grievance that he had not died with the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, Yang Xingmi slew Liang Zuan at headquarters as revenge for not dying with the Gao house.

sentences.zh: 韓問聞之，赴井死。

translations.literal: Han Wen heard it and threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wen heard of it and drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 居人臒惙奄奄，兵不忍加暴，反斥餘糧救之。

translations.literal: Residents were emaciated, gasping feebly; soldiers could not bear to add violence, instead distributed leftover grain to save them.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople were skeletal, barely breathing. The troops would not harm them further and instead shared spare grain to keep them alive.

sentences.zh: 彥、師鐸與唐宏、倪詳焚白砂，將度江，會秦宗權使孫儒引兵三萬襲揚州，次天長，彥等與之合，還攻行密，取行密輜重牛羊數千計。

translations.literal: Yan, Shiduo with Tang Hong and Ni Xiang burned Baisha and were about to cross the river; it happened Qin Zongquan sent Sun Ru leading thirty thousand troops to strike Yangzhou, garrisoned Tianchang; Yan and others joined him, returned to attack Xingmi, and took Xingmi's baggage, cattle and sheep by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Shiduo, Tang Hong, and Ni Xiang burned Baisha and were about to cross the river when Qin Zongquan sent Sun Ru with thirty thousand men against Yangzhou, halting at Tianchang. They joined Ru, turned on Xingmi, and seized thousands of his pack animals and cattle.

sentences.zh: 儒以食乏，乃屠高郵，據之。

translations.literal: Ru because food was scarce then slaughtered Gaoyou and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Ru, short of food, massacred Gaoyou and occupied it.

sentences.zh: 張神劍奔還，行密授之館，而高郵戍兵七百潰而來，行密責有謀，悉擊殺之，因殺神劍。

translations.literal: Zhang Shenjian fled back; Xingmi lodged him in a guesthouse; but Gaoyou garrison troops seven hundred scattered and came; Xingmi blamed them for plotting, all struck and killed; thereby also killed Shenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shenjian returned and Xingmi gave him quarters—but when seven hundred Gaoyou garrisoners fled in, he accused them of conspiracy, slaughtered them all, and killed Shenjian as well.

sentences.zh: 用之始詐行密曰：「廡下有瘞金五千斤，事平願備一日乏。」

translations.literal: Yongzhi at first deceived Xingmi, saying: "Beneath the corridor is buried gold five thousand jin; when the affair is settled I wish to supply one day's want."
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi had first tricked Xingmi: "Five thousand jin of gold lie buried under the hall—when all is settled let me provision you for a day."

sentences.zh: 行密掘地無埋金，但得銅人三尺，身桎梏，釘刺其口，刻駢名於背，蓋用蠱厭駢也。

translations.literal: Xingmi dug the earth—no buried gold, only obtained a bronze man three feet, body in shackles, nails piercing its mouth, Pian's name carved on the back—probably Yongzhi used sorcery to curse Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi dug and found no gold—only a three-foot bronze figure in shackles, nails through its mouth, and Pian's name on its back: Yongzhi's curse upon him.

sentences.zh: 行密責其罪，並張守一斬於三橋，妻子皆死，著其罪於路。

translations.literal: Xingmi blamed his crimes; together with Zhang Shouyi beheaded at Three Bridges; wife and children all died; posted his crimes on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi condemned his crimes and beheaded him with Zhang Shouyi at the Three Bridges; their families were executed and the charges posted along the road.

sentences.zh: 儒攻城未得誌，慮彥、師鐸有異謀，稍並其兵。

translations.literal: Ru besieged the city without achieving his aim, feared Yan and Shiduo had divergent schemes, and gradually absorbed their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru could not take the city and feared Yan and Shiduo might plot against him, so he steadily absorbed their troops.

sentences.zh: 唐宏度不免，即告儒曰：「師鐸密遣人至汴。」

translations.literal: Tang Hong judged escape impossible and immediately informed Ru: "Shiduo secretly sent men to Bian."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Hong, seeing no escape, told Ru, "Shiduo has secretly sent envoys to Bian."

sentences.zh: 儒大恐。

translations.literal: Ru was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Ru was terrified.

sentences.zh: 明日，召彥、師鐸、漢璋會軍中，彥、師鐸先至，壯士捽之至儒所，儒質彥反駢罪，斬之。

translations.literal: Next day he summoned Yan, Shiduo, and Hanzhang to meet in the army; Yan and Shiduo arrived first; strongmen seized them and brought them to Ru's place; Ru charged Yan with betraying Pian's crime and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ru summoned Yan, Shiduo, and Hanzhang. When Yan and Shiduo came first, braves dragged them to Ru, who accused Yan of turning on Pian and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 至師鐸，呼曰：「丈夫成則王，敗則虜，君何多責為？

translations.literal: When it came to Shiduo, he cried: "A man succeeding becomes king, failing becomes captive—why so many charges, lord?
translations.idiomatic: When Shiduo's turn came he shouted, "Success makes a king, failure a prisoner—why heap reproaches on me?

sentences.zh: 吾嘗將數萬兵，不死常人手，得公之劍，瞑目矣！」

translations.literal: I once commanded tens of thousands of troops, will not die by common men's hands—obtaining your lordship's sword, I can close my eyes!"
translations.idiomatic: I once led tens of thousands—I will not die by common hands. Your blade is enough; I can close my eyes."

sentences.zh: 儒罵曰：「庸賊欲汙我手邪！」

translations.literal: Ru cursed: "Vile bandit—wishes to stain my hands!"
translations.idiomatic: Ru spat, "Wretched thief—would you stain my sword?"

sentences.zh: 趣斬之。

translations.literal: He urged beheading him.
translations.idiomatic: And ordered him cut down.

sentences.zh: 漢璋至，奮臂擊殺數人，乃死，身首糜散。

translations.literal: Hanzhang arrived, swung his arms killing several men, then died; body and head scattered in pieces.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanzhang came he struck down several before he died—body and head torn apart.

sentences.zh: 儒使宏主騎兵，厚賜之。

translations.literal: Ru had Hong command the cavalry and richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru put Hong in charge of the cavalry and heaped rewards on him.

sentences.zh: 文德元年，儒諜知行密糧乏，自高郵襲之。

translations.literal: First year of Wende, Ru's spies knew Xingmi's grain was short; from Gaoyou he raided him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wende, Ru learned Yang Xingmi was short of grain and struck from Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 行密拔其眾還廬州，儒遂據揚州。

translations.literal: Xingmi withdrew his masses back to Luzhou; Ru then held Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi withdrew to Luzhou, and Ru took Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 駢之死，裹以故氈，與子弟七人一坎而瘞。

translations.literal: At Pian's death they wrapped him in old felt, with seven sons and younger brothers in one pit and buried.
translations.idiomatic: At his death they wrapped Gao Pian in old felt and buried him in one pit with seven kin.

sentences.zh: 行密擢駢孫愈為副使，令主喪事，未克葬，愈暴死，至是故吏鄺師虔收葬之。

translations.literal: Xingmi promoted Pian's grandson Yu as deputy commissioner, ordered him to preside over funeral affairs; before burial could be completed Yu died violently; in the end former clerk Kuang Shiqian collected and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi made Pian's grandson Yu his deputy and put him in charge of the funeral, but before burial Yu died suddenly; an old retainer, Kuang Shiqian, finally interred them.

sentences.zh: 揚州雄富冠天下，自師鐸、行密、儒叠攻叠守，焚市落，剽民人，兵饑相仍，其地遂空。

translations.literal: Yangzhou's might and wealth crowned all under heaven; from Shiduo, Xingmi, and Ru repeatedly attacking and repeatedly defending, burned markets and wards, plundered the people—army and famine following one another—the place was thus emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou had been the richest city under heaven, but Shiduo, Yang Xingmi, and Sun Ru attacked and defended it in turn, burning the markets and looting the people until famine and war left the land barren.

sentences.zh: 朱玫朱玫，邠州人。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei—Zhu Mei, a man of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei. Zhu Mei was a native of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以材武為州戍將。

translations.literal: In youth for talent and martial prowess he became the prefecture's garrison general.
translations.idiomatic: In youth his martial skill made him a garrison officer of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 黃巢盜長安，有王玫者為偽節度使，方調兵，玫陽事之，乘間斬王玫，以留後讓李重古，約合兵討巢。

translations.literal: Huang Chao's bandits seized Chang'an; there was a Wang Mei who served as false military commissioner, was just mobilizing troops; Mei outwardly served him, seized an interval and beheaded Wang Mei, yielded the acting post to Li Chonggu, agreed to unite troops to punish Chao.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an, a Wang Mei ruled Binzhou in rebellion and was raising troops. Zhu Mei feigned loyalty, struck when he could, beheaded Wang Mei, yielded the post to Li Chonggu, and pledged to join against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 廣明二年，玫襲賊，戰開遠門，槍洞咽，不死。

translations.literal: Second year of Guangming, Mei raided the bandits, fought at Kaiyuan Gate; a spear pierced his throat; he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangming he attacked the rebels at Kaiyuan Gate—a spear pierced his throat yet he lived.

sentences.zh: 以多擢晉州刺史，進邠寧節度使，合涇、原、岐、隴兵八萬屯興平，號定國砦。

translations.literal: For many feats he was promoted to Jinzhou prefect, advanced to Binning military commissioner, united Jing, Yuan, Qi, and Long troops eighty thousand encamped at Xingping, styled the Fortress of Stabilizing the State.
translations.idiomatic: For his valor he rose to Jinzhou prefect, then Binning commissioner, gathering eighty thousand men from Jing, Yuan, Qi, and Long at Xingping in a camp called the Fortress of Stabilizing the State.

sentences.zh: 戰澇上，敗走邠，詔益靈、鹽軍，拜河南都統。

translations.literal: He battled at Lao Shang, was defeated and fled to Bin; decree added Ling and Yan troops, appointed Grand Commander of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated on the Lao River he retreated to Bin; the court reinforced him with Ling and Yan troops and named him supreme commander of Henan.

sentences.zh: 引兵屯中橋，列五壁，進西北面都統。

translations.literal: He led troops to encamp at Middle Bridge, arrayed five ramparts, advanced to northwest front grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Middle Bridge with five walled camps and was promoted to commander of the northwest front.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授同中書門下平章事，封吳興侯。

translations.literal: Bandits pacified, he was conferred Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffed Marquis of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed he was made a grand councilor and enfeoffed Marquis of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 田令孜議討王重榮，以兵屬玫，合鄜、延、靈、夏軍三萬保沙苑。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi deliberated punishing Wang Chongrong, placed troops under Mei, united Fu, Yan, Ling, and Xia armies thirty thousand to guard Sha Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi planned to punish Wang Chongrong and gave Mei command of thirty thousand from Fu, Yan, Ling, and Xia to hold Sha Yuan.

sentences.zh: 重榮上疏乞誅玫、令孜。

translations.literal: Chongrong submitted a memorial begging to execute Mei and Lingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong memorialized the throne demanding the execution of Zhu Mei and Tian Lingzi.

sentences.zh: 既戰，玫輒北，因縱軍還掠。

translations.literal: Once battle joined, Mei would always flee north, and thus let his army turn back to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Once fighting began, Zhu Mei would retreat northward and allow his troops to turn back and loot.

sentences.zh: 僖宗蒼黃幸鳳翔避其鋒。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong in disarray hastened to Fengxiang to avoid his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong fled in panic to Fengxiang to escape Zhu Mei's assault.

sentences.zh: 玫反與重榮、李克用連和，請誅令孜。

translations.literal: Mei turned to ally with Chongrong and Li Keyong, requesting execution of Lingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei then allied with Wang Chongrong and Li Keyong, calling for Tian Lingzi's death.

sentences.zh: 宰相蕭遘密召玫迎帝，玫趨鳳翔，令孜劫乘輿走陳倉，遂至興元。

translations.literal: Chancellor Xiao Sui secretly summoned Mei to welcome the emperor; Mei rushed toward Fengxiang; Lingzi seized the imperial carriage and fled Chencang, then reached Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xiao Sui secretly summoned Zhu Mei to escort the emperor back; Mei hurried toward Fengxiang, but Tian Lingzi seized the imperial carriage and fled by way of Chencang to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 玫追不及，劫嗣襄王煴，奉為帝。

translations.literal: Mei could not overtake them; he seized the heir Prince of Xiang Li Yun and installed him as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei could not catch up, so he seized Li Yun, heir to the Prince of Xiang, and proclaimed him emperor.

sentences.zh: 玫自號大丞相，專決萬機。

translations.literal: Mei styled himself Grand Chancellor and solely decided the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei proclaimed himself Grand Chancellor and seized control of all government affairs.

sentences.zh: 始與李昌符共謀挾煴，至是反為讎，昌符乃自歸天子，人心浸離。

translations.literal: At first with Li Changfu he had plotted to hold Yun hostage; by then they became foes instead; Changfu then returned himself to the Son of Heaven, and hearts gradually deserted.
translations.idiomatic: He had first conspired with Li Changfu to control the puppet emperor, but they now turned on each other; Changfu submitted to the throne, and support for Zhu Mei steadily crumbled.

sentences.zh: 及王行瑜敗於大唐峰，懼歸且見殺，又聞購能得玫者以邠寧節度畀之，行瑜謂其下曰：「今敗歸必以無功死，若斬玫，與北軍迎天子，取富貴，可乎？」

translations.literal: When Wang Xingyu was defeated at Great Tang Peak, fearing return and imminent execution, and also hearing that a reward promised Binning military commissioner to whoever could capture Mei, Xingyu said to his men: "Now defeated and returning we shall surely die for achieving nothing—if we behead Mei and with the northern army welcome the Son of Heaven, seize wealth and honor—would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xingyu's defeat at Great Tang Peak, he feared execution on his return and heard that whoever captured Zhu Mei would receive the Binning commission. He told his men: "If we go back defeated, we'll be killed for accomplishing nothing. If we behead Zhu Mei and join the northern armies to welcome the emperor, we can win riches and rank—is that not better?"

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "We agree."
translations.idiomatic: His followers answered, "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 即勒兵倍道趨長安。

translations.literal: At once he drove the army double marches toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately forced his troops on a forced march toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 玫居孔緯第，方據幾署事，聞兵入，趣召行瑜叱曰：「公擅歸，反邪？」

translations.literal: Mei dwelt in Kong Wei's mansion, was just leaning on the desk handling affairs, heard troops enter, hurriedly summoned Xingyu and shouted: "You returned without orders—rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei was staying in Kong Wei's mansion, conducting affairs at his desk, when he heard soldiers approach. He summoned Wang Xingyu and demanded: "You returned without leave—are you rebelling?"

sentences.zh: 行瑜厲聲曰：「我非反者，將得君首為邠寧節度耳！」

translations.literal: Xingyu in a harsh voice said: "I am no rebel—I mean to take your head for Binning military commissioner!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu thundered back: "I'm no rebel—I'm going to take your head and win the Binning commission!"

sentences.zh: 玫遽起，左右斬之，殺其徒數百。

translations.literal: Mei sprang up; those at his sides beheaded him and killed his followers several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei leaped to his feet, but his guards were cut down; Wang Xingyu slew him and killed hundreds of his men.

sentences.zh: 諸軍遂大亂，燒京師。

translations.literal: The various armies then fell into great disorder and burned the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The armies then fell into chaos and burned the capital.

sentences.zh: 時盛寒，吏民被剽敓，僵死屍相藉。

translations.literal: It was bitter cold; officials and commoners were plundered; corpses frozen stiff lay heaped together.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of winter, officials and civilians were looted; frozen bodies lay heaped upon one another.

sentences.zh: 即傳首興元，帝為受俘馘。

translations.literal: At once they sent the head to Xingyuan; the emperor performed the rite of receiving captive spoils.
translations.idiomatic: His head was sent to Xingyuan, where the emperor received it in the ritual of triumph over rebels.

sentences.zh: 宦者偽樞密使王能著等皆坐誅。

translations.literal: Eunuchs falsely holding posts of Privy Council commissioners—Wang Nengzhu and others—all sat for execution.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Nengzhu, who had posed as acting commissioner of the Privy Council, and others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜王行瑜，邠州人。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu—Wang Xingyu, a man of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu. Wang Xingyu was a native of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 少隸軍，從朱玫為列校，討黃巢數有功。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the army, followed Zhu Mei as a company commander, and punished Huang Chao with many merits.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he joined the army, served under Zhu Mei as a company officer, and won repeated credit fighting Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 煴即位，授行瑜天平節度使，令率兵守大散關，為李鋋所破，即奉款行在，還取玫首以獻，擢邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: When Yun assumed the throne, Xingyu was appointed Tianping military commissioner, ordered to lead troops guarding Great Scatter Pass; he was broken by Li Gang, then submitted allegiance at the imperial camp, returned and took Mei's head to present, and was advanced to Binning military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yun was enthroned, Wang Xingyu was made commissioner of Tianping and ordered to hold Great Scatter Pass. Defeated by Li Gang, he submitted to the court, beheaded Zhu Mei and presented his head, and was promoted to Binning commissioner.

sentences.zh: 景福元年，與李茂貞、韓建及弟同州節度使行實請討楊守亮於山南，且言不敢仰度支費，止請假茂貞招討一節。

translations.literal: First year of Jingfu, with Li Maozhen, Han Jian, and younger brother Tongzhou military commissioner Xingshi he requested to punish Yang Shouliang in Shannan, and moreover said they dared not look up to the Department of Treasury for funds, only requesting to borrow Maozhen's punitive commissioner insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingfu he joined Li Maozhen, Han Jian, and his brother Wang Xingshi, commissioner of Tongzhou, in asking to campaign against Yang Shouliang in the south. They claimed they would not burden the treasury, requesting only that Li Maozhen lend them his expeditionary commission.

sentences.zh: 宦官難之，昭宗亦顧茂貞等得山南則益橫，不許。

translations.literal: Eunuchs made it difficult; Emperor Zhaozong also feared that if Maozhen and others gained Shannan they would grow more overbearing—permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs opposed it, and Emperor Zhaozong feared that if Li Maozhen held Shannan he would grow more powerful—permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 行瑜等因擅興軍擊取之。

translations.literal: Xingyu and others therefore on their own authority raised armies and seized it by attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu and his allies then marched on their own authority and seized the territory by force.

sentences.zh: 後茂貞拒覃王，殺宰相，行瑜參有力，得賜鐵券。

translations.literal: Later Maozhen resisted the Prince of Tan and killed chancellors; Xingyu shared strong power and received bestowal of an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Maozhen defied the Prince of Tan and killed chancellors, Wang Xingyu played a major part and was rewarded with an iron certificate of immunity.

sentences.zh: 稍憑兵跋扈，求為尚書令，宰相韋昭度執不可，但加號尚父，行瑜望甚。

translations.literal: Gradually relying on troops he acted overbearingly, sought to become Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Chancellor Wei Zhaodu held firm that it could not be, only added the title Exalted Father; Xingyu's hopes were deeply disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: He grew arrogant with military might and sought the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat. Chancellor Wei Zhaodu refused, granting only the honorific "Exalted Father." Wang Xingyu was deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 會河中王重榮喪，李克用請以其子珂嗣節度，而行瑜、建、茂貞請授王珙，因各以兵陳闕下，欲廢天子，不克，即殺昭度、李磎，留弟行約宿衛。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Chongrong of Hezhong died; Li Keyong requested his son Ke succeed the commission, while Xingyu, Jian, and Maozhen requested appointing Wang Gong; each deployed troops before the palace gates, wished to depose the Son of Heaven, did not succeed, then killed Zhaodu and Li Yong, left younger brother Xingyue as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chongrong of Hezhong died, Li Keyong asked that his son Wang Ke succeed the command. Wang Xingyu, Han Jian, and Li Maozhen supported Wang Gong instead. They massed troops at the palace gates in a bid to depose the emperor. When that failed, they killed Wei Zhaodu and Li Yong and stationed Wang Xingyu's brother Xingyue as palace guard.

sentences.zh: 克用悉兵度河問行瑜等罪，行實棄同州趨長安，與行約謀劫乘輿，又不克，皆奔邠州。

translations.literal: Keyong mustered all troops, crossed the river to inquire into Xingyu and others' crimes; Xingshi abandoned Tongzhou and rushed to Chang'an, with Xingyue plotted to seize the imperial carriage, again did not succeed, all fled to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong crossed the Yellow River at the head of his full army to punish them. Wang Xingshi abandoned Tongzhou for Chang'an, and he and Wang Xingyue plotted to seize the emperor. That too failed, and all fled to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 行瑜屯梨園，克用與戰，破行實等軍，執其母及行瑜子，俘大校。

translations.literal: Xingyu encamped at Pear Garden; Keyong battled him, broke Xingshi and others' army, seized his mother and Xingyu's son, captured great colonels.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu held Pear Garden. Li Keyong attacked, routed Wang Xingshi's force, captured Wang Xingyu's mother and son, and took many senior officers prisoner.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔削行瑜官爵。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict stripping Xingyu's offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Wang Xingyu of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 行瑜以銳卒五千營龍泉，茂貞壁其西。

translations.literal: Xingyu with sharp soldiers five thousand encamped at Dragon Spring; Maozhen walled west of him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu camped at Dragon Spring with five thousand elite troops; Li Maozhen fortified to his west.

sentences.zh: 克用夜發精騎擾餉道，岐軍走，行瑜歸邠州，嬰城守，厚賂克用求自歸。

translations.literal: Keyong by night sent crack cavalry to harass supply routes; Qi troops fled; Xingyu returned to Binzhou, nursed the city in defense, richly bribed Keyong begging to return of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent elite cavalry by night to cut their supply lines. The Qi forces fled. Wang Xingyu retreated to Binzhou and walled the city, offering Li Keyong rich bribes to let him surrender.

sentences.zh: 克用軍環其城，行瑜窮，登城哭語克用曰：「我無罪，昨殺大臣，脅天子，岐人也。

translations.literal: Keyong's army ringed his city; Xingyu at an end mounted the wall weeping and said to Keyong: "I am guiltless; yesterday killing great ministers and coercing the Son of Heaven—that was the Qi man.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong encircled the city. In desperation Wang Xingyu mounted the walls and called out: "I am innocent. It was the man of Qi who killed the ministers and threatened the emperor.

sentences.zh: 行實止宿衛，而有司妄以劫遷罪歸之，今公討亂者，當問茂貞，願得束身歸，聽命天子。」

translations.literal: Xingshi only held palace guard, yet the authorities wrongly returned the crime of seizing and moving the emperor upon him; now you punish rebels—you ought to question Maozhen; I wish to bind myself and return, obey the Son of Heaven's command."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingshi merely guarded the palace, yet the court wrongly blamed us for kidnapping the emperor. If you mean to punish rebels, you should question Li Maozhen. I am willing to surrender myself and await the emperor's judgment."

sentences.zh: 克用曰：「尚父何自卑？

translations.literal: Keyong said: "Exalted Father, why so humble yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong replied: "Exalted Father, why so humble?

sentences.zh: 吾被命討三賊，公其一也。

translations.literal: I received orders to punish three rebels—you are one of them.
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered to crush three rebels, and you are one of them.

sentences.zh: 如歸國者，當從中決，老夫敢專之邪？」

translations.literal: If returning to the state, the center must decide—would this old man dare decide alone?"
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to return to the throne's grace, the court must decide. How dare an old soldier like me judge alone?"

sentences.zh: 行瑜度不免，悉族奔慶州，為麾下斬於路，傳首京師，帝禦延喜門納之，於是乾寧二年也。

translations.literal: Xingyu judged he could not escape, with whole clan fled to Qingzhou, was beheaded on the road by subordinates, head sent to the capital; the emperor at Yanxi Gate received it—thus the second year of Qianning.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, Wang Xingyu fled with his clan toward Qingzhou. His own men cut him down on the road. His head reached Chang'an, and the emperor received it at Yanxi Gate—in the second year of Qianning.

sentences.zh: 其屬二百人，克用獻於朝。

translations.literal: His followers two hundred men, Keyong presented to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong presented two hundred of his followers to the court.

sentences.zh: 始，行瑜亂，宗正卿李涪盛陳其忠，必悔過。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Xingyu rebelled, Director of the Imperial Clan Li Fou earnestly stated his loyalty, surely would repent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Wang Xingyu's rebellion, Director of the Imperial Clan Li Fou had insisted on his loyalty and predicted he would repent.

sentences.zh: 至是帝怒，放死嶺南。

translations.literal: By then the emperor was enraged and exiled him to death in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor's wrath exiled Li Fou to Lingnan, condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄陳敬瑄，田令孜兄也。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan—Chen Jingxuan, elder brother of Tian Lingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan. Chen Jingxuan was the elder brother of Tian Lingzi.

sentences.zh: 少賤，為餅師，得隸左神策軍。

translations.literal: In youth lowly, he was a cake-maker and gained enrollment in the Left Divine Stratagem Army.
translations.idiomatic: Born to humble origins, he worked as a baker before joining the Left Divine Stratagem Army.

sentences.zh: 令孜為護軍中尉，敬瑄緣藉擢左金吾衛將軍、檢校尚書右僕射、西川節度使。

translations.literal: When Lingzi was protecting-army commissioner, Jingxuan by connection was promoted Left Golden Crow Guard general, acting Minister of Works of the Right, and Xichuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Lingzi became Commander and Commandant-in-ordinary of the Protecting Army, Chen Jingxuan rose through his patronage to General of the Left Imperial Insignia Guard, acting Inspector and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, a high official post, and military commissioner (jiedushi) of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 性畏慎，善撫士。

translations.literal: By nature timid and cautious, good at comforting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Timid by nature, he was skilled at winning soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 黃巢亂，僖宗幸奉天，敬瑄夜召監軍梁處厚，號慟奉表迎帝，繕治行宮。

translations.literal: During Huang Chao's disorder Emperor Xizong visited Fengtian; Jingxuan by night summoned military inspector Liang Chuhou, wailed and submitted a memorial welcoming the emperor, and repaired the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao's rebellion drove Emperor Xizong to Fengtian, Chen Jingxuan summoned the military inspector Liang Chuhou by night, wept as he memorialized to welcome the emperor, and prepared the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 令孜亦倡西幸，敬瑄以兵三千護乘輿。

translations.literal: Lingzi also advocated the western journey; Jingxuan with troops three thousand escorted the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi also urged the western flight; Chen Jingxuan escorted the imperial carriage with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 冗從內苑小兒先至，敬瑄知素暴橫，遣邏士伺之。

translations.literal: Idle attendants and inner-park boys arrived first; Jingxuan knew their usual violence and overbearing ways and sent patrol soldiers to watch them.
translations.idiomatic: Idle attendants and inner-park youths reached the palace first. Knowing their habitual violence, Chen Jingxuan sent patrols to watch them.

sentences.zh: 諸兒連臂歡咋行宮中，士捕系之，謼曰：「我事天子者！」

translations.literal: The boys linked arms shouting rowdily in the traveling palace; soldiers seized and bound them, crying: "We serve the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: The youths linked arms and caroused through the traveling palace. Soldiers seized them, shouting: "We serve the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 敬瑄殺五十人，屍諸衢，由是道路不嘩。

translations.literal: Jingxuan killed fifty men, corpses displayed at the thoroughfares; thereby the roads were not noisy.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan executed fifty of them and displayed the bodies in the streets, and the roads fell quiet.

sentences.zh: 帝次綿州，敬瑄謁於道，進酒，帝三舉觴，進檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor halted at Mianzhou; Jingxuan paid respects on the road and presented wine; the emperor thrice raised the cup and promoted him acting Left Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.
