translations.idiomatic: When the emperor halted at Mianzhou, Chen Jingxuan met him on the road and offered wine. The emperor raised his cup three times and promoted him to acting Left Minister of Works and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時雲南叛，請遣使與和親，乃聽命。

translations.literal: At the time Yunnan rebelled; he requested to dispatch an envoy for marriage alliance—then obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan rebelled, he asked to send an envoy to negotiate a marriage alliance and then obeyed the court's command.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄奉行在百官諸吏無敢乏，帝欲命判度支，固讓，再加檢校司徒兼侍中，封梁國公。

translations.literal: Jingxuan serving the traveling court—among the hundred officials none dared be lacking; the emperor wished to appoint him to oversee the Department of Treasury, he firmly declined; again added acting Defender-in-chief with Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the traveling court Chen Jingxuan supplied every need of the officials and clerks. When the emperor wished to put him in charge of the treasury, he firmly declined. He was then made acting Defender-in-chief and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 以弟敬珣為閬州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jingxun was made Langzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chen Jingxun was appointed prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 討定邛州首望阡能、涪州叛校韓秀升，再進兼中書令，封潁川郡王，實封四百戶，賜一歲上輸錢及上都田宅邸硙各十區，鐵券恕十死。

translations.literal: He subdued Qiongzhou chieftain Wang Qianneng and Fuzhou rebel officer Han Xiuzheng; again advanced to Chancellor, enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan commandery with actual fief four hundred households, bestowed one year's upper tribute money and capital estates, residences, and mills each ten parcels, iron certificate forgiving ten deaths.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Qiongzhou chieftain Wang Qianneng and the Fuzhou rebel Han Xiuzheng, was again promoted to chancellor, and enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan with a fief of four hundred households. He received a year's revenue from the capital tribute, ten estates and mills in the capital, and an iron certificate forgiving ten capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 巢平，進潁川王，增實戶二百。

translations.literal: When Chao was pacified, he was advanced to Prince of Yingchuan and actual households increased by two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao was crushed, he was advanced to Prince of Yingchuan and his fief increased by two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 車駕東，敬瑄供億豐餘，又進檢校太師。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage went east, Jingxuan supplied abundantly and was again advanced acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned east, Chen Jingxuan provisioned the journey lavishly and was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 俄而令孜得罪，敬瑄被流端州。

translations.literal: Soon Lingzi offended; Jingxuan was exiled to Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tian Lingzi fell from favor, and Chen Jingxuan was exiled to Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會昭宗立，敬瑄拒詔，帝召為左龍武統軍，以宰相韋昭度代領節度。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong assumed the throne, Jingxuan defied the edict; the emperor summoned him as Left Dragon Martial commander, with Chancellor Wei Zhaodu replacing him to lead the commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Chen Jingxuan defied the recall. The emperor named him commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard and sent Chancellor Wei Zhaodu to replace him as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 使者至，敬瑄使百姓遮道剺耳訴己功，且言鐵券恕死。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, Jingxuan had common people block the road tearing their ears to plead his merit, moreover saying the iron certificate forgave death.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, Chen Jingxuan had the people block the road, mutilating their ears to plead his merits and citing the iron certificate that forgave capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 使者馳還。

translations.literal: The envoy galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy galloped back to report.

sentences.zh: 令孜勸敬瑄募黃頭軍為自守計。

translations.literal: Lingzi urged Jingxuan to recruit the Yellow-Head Army as a plan for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi urged Chen Jingxuan to recruit the Yellow-Head Army to defend himself.

sentences.zh: 時王建盜據閬、利，故令孜召建。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jian by theft held Lang and Li; therefore Lingzi summoned Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian had seized Lang and Li by force, so Tian Lingzi summoned him.

sentences.zh: 建至綿州，發兵拒之，激建攻諸州，以限朝廷。

translations.literal: When Jian reached Mianzhou, Jingxuan raised troops to resist him, incited Jian to attack the various prefectures, to limit the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian reached Mianzhou, Chen Jingxuan raised troops against him and goaded him to attack the surrounding prefectures, checking the court's power.

sentences.zh: 或言：「建鴟視狼顧，惟利是賴，公何用之？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Jian looks like an owl and a wolf glancing back—profit alone is what he depends on—why use him?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned: "Wang Jian has the eyes of an owl and the glance of a wolf—he follows profit alone. Why employ him?"

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 建詒顧彥朗書曰：「十軍阿父召我，欲依太師丐一大州。」

translations.literal: Jian deceived and wrote to Gu Yanlang: "The Ten Armies' Adopted Father summoned me; I wish to rely on the Grand Preceptor to beg one great prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian wrote deceitfully to Gu Yanlang: "The Adopted Father of the Ten Armies summoned me; I mean to rely on the Grand Preceptor to beg a large prefecture."

sentences.zh: 即寄孥梓州，身引兵入鹿頭關。

translations.literal: At once he sent wife and children to Zizhou and personally led troops into Deer-Head Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his family to Zizhou and personally led his army through Deer-Head Pass.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄不納，漢州刺史張頊逆戰，敗，建入漢州。

translations.literal: Jingxuan would not receive him; Hanzhou prefect Zhang Shu opposed in battle and was defeated; Jian entered Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan refused him entry. The Hanzhou prefect Zhang Shu met him in battle and was defeated; Wang Jian entered Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 成都嚴守，建走城下遙謝令孜曰：「父召我，及門而拒我，尚誰容？」

translations.literal: Chengdu was strictly guarded; Jian walked below the walls from afar and said to Lingzi: "Father summoned me, yet at the gate you reject me—who else would shelter me?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu stood under tight guard. Wang Jian walked below the walls and called out to Tian Lingzi: "You summoned me, Father, yet shut me at the gate—who else will take me in?"

sentences.zh: 與諸將斷髮再拜辭曰：「今作賊矣！」

translations.literal: With the generals he cut his hair and bowed again in farewell, saying: "Today I become a bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: He and his generals cut their hair and bowed again in farewell, declaring: "Today I become a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 因請兵於彥朗，攻成都，殘掠州縣。

translations.literal: He therefore requested troops from Yanlang, attacked Chengdu, and ravaged and plundered prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Gu Yanlang for troops, attacked Chengdu, and ravaged the surrounding prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 彥朗亦畏建，表請大臣代敬瑄。

translations.literal: Yanlang also feared Jian and memorialized requesting a great minister replace Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanlang too feared Wang Jian and memorialized asking that a senior minister replace Chen Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 建自請討敬瑄贖罪，詔立永平軍，授建節度使，以昭度為行營招討使，山南西道節度使楊守亮副之，彥朗為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Jian himself requested to punish Jingxuan to atone guilt; an edict established the Yongping army, appointed Jian military commissioner, Zhaodu as campaign punitive commissioner, Shannan West-Circuit military commissioner Yang Shouliang as deputy, Yanlang as campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian volunteered to attack Chen Jingxuan to atone for his crimes. The court established the Yongping army, made Wang Jian its commissioner, named Wei Zhaodu campaign commander, Yang Shouliang of Shannan West-Circuit as his deputy, and Gu Yanlang campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 有詔暴敬瑄殺孟昭圖罪，削官爵。

translations.literal: There was an edict exposing Jingxuan's crime in killing Meng Zhaotu and stripping his offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict publicized Chen Jingxuan's murder of Meng Zhaotu and stripped him of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 昭度使建屯學射山，敬瑄迎戰不克，又戰蠶厓，大敗。

translations.literal: Zhaodu had Jian encamp at Archery-Practice Mountain; Jingxuan met battle but could not overcome; again fought at Silkworm Cliff and suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu had Wang Jian camp at Archery-Practice Mountain. Chen Jingxuan met him in battle and failed; fighting again at Silkworm Cliff, he was routed.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年，昭度至軍中，持節諭人，約開門。

translations.literal: First year of Longji, Zhaodu reached the army, bore credentials to instruct the people, and agreed to open the gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longji, Wei Zhaodu arrived at the army, bore the imperial staff to address the people, and negotiated for the gates to be opened.

sentences.zh: 守陴者詬曰：「鐵券在，安得違先帝意！」

translations.literal: The wall defenders cursed: "The iron certificate remains—how dare we violate the former emperor's intent!"
translations.idiomatic: The defenders on the walls shouted back: "The iron certificate still stands—how dare we defy the late emperor's will!"

sentences.zh: 今孜籍城中戶一人乘城，夜循行，晝浚濠伐薪。

translations.literal: Lingzi registered each household in the city for one man on the walls; by night he patrolled the circuit, by day dredged the moat and cut firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi registered one man from every household in the city for wall duty; by night he patrolled the ramparts, by day he dug the moat and gathered firewood.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄屯彌牟、德陽，樹二壁拒建。

translations.literal: Jingxuan encamped at Mimu and Deyang and planted two ramparts to resist Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan encamped at Mimu and Deyang and built two walled camps to block Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 使富人自占貲多少，布巨梃，搒不實者，不三日輸錢如市。

translations.literal: He had the wealthy declare their own assets; huge cudgels were set out; those who underreported were beaten; within three days money poured in like a market.
translations.idiomatic: He made the wealthy declare their assets, set out heavy clubs, and beat those who underreported; within three days money poured in as if at market.

sentences.zh: 建、昭度傅城而壘，簡州刺史張造攻笮橋，大敗，死之。

translations.literal: Jian and Zhaodu built ramparts pressing the walls; Jianzhou prefect Zhang Zao attacked Bamboo Bridge, suffered great defeat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian and Wei Zhaodu built siege lines against the walls. The Jianzhou prefect Zhang Zao attacked Bamboo Bridge, was routed, and died.

sentences.zh: 大順元年，建稍擊降諸州。

translations.literal: First year of Dashun, Jian gradually attacked and subdued the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dashun, Wang Jian gradually attacked and brought the surrounding prefectures to surrender.

sentences.zh: 邛州刺史毛湘本令孜孔目官，謂其下曰：「吾不忍負軍容，以頭見建可也。」

translations.literal: Qiongzhou prefect Mao Xiang had been Lingzi's clerical officer; he said to his subordinates: "I cannot bear to betray the Military Commissioner—offering my head to meet Jian will do."
translations.idiomatic: The Qiongzhou prefect Mao Xiang had been Tian Lingzi's chief clerk. He told his men: "I cannot betray the Military Commissioner—let my head answer to Wang Jian."

sentences.zh: 乃沐浴以須，吏斬其首降。

translations.literal: Then he bathed and waited; an officer beheaded him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed and waited; an officer beheaded him and surrendered his head.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄戰浣花，不勝，明日復戰，將士皆為建俘。

translations.literal: Jingxuan fought at Washing-Flower Pavilion and did not prevail; the next day he fought again; officers and soldiers all became Jian's captives.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan fought at Washing-Flower Pavilion and lost. The next day he fought again, and his officers and soldiers were all taken by Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 城中謀降者，令孜支解之以怖眾。

translations.literal: Those in the city plotting surrender—Lingzi dismembered them to frighten the masses.
translations.idiomatic: When men inside the city plotted to surrender, Tian Lingzi had them dismembered to terrify the rest.

sentences.zh: 會大疫，死人相藉。

translations.literal: Then came great pestilence; the dead lay heaped upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: A great plague followed, and the dead lay heaped upon one another.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，詔還敬瑄官爵，召昭度還，諭建罷兵，建不奉詔。

translations.literal: Next year third month, an edict restored Jingxuan's offices and ranks, summoned Zhaodu back, instructed Jian to cease troops—Jian did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The following March an edict restored Chen Jingxuan's rank, recalled Wei Zhaodu, and ordered Wang Jian to stand down. Wang Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 帝更以建為西川行營招討制置使。

translations.literal: The emperor again appointed Jian as Xichuan campaign punitive and provisioning commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then named Wang Jian campaign commander and provisioning commissioner for Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 建知敬瑄可禽，欲遂有蜀地，即脅說昭度曰：「公以數萬眾討賊，糧數不屬，關東諸節度相吞噬，朝廷危若贅斿，與其勞師遠方，不如先中國，公宜還為天子謀之。」

translations.literal: Jian knew Jingxuan could be captured, wished then to possess Shu lands; at once he coerced persuasion on Zhaodu: "You with tens of thousands punish bandits; grain and funds do not reach you; Guandong's various commissions devour one another; the court is perilous as an appended boat—rather than laboring the army far away, better first secure the central realm; you ought to return and scheme for the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian knew Chen Jingxuan could be taken and meant to seize Shu for himself. He pressed Wei Zhaodu: "You lead tens of thousands against a rebel, yet supplies never reach you. The eastern commissioners devour one another, and the court hangs by a thread. Rather than wear out your army in a distant province, secure the heartland first—return and plot for the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 昭度未決。

translations.literal: Zhaodu had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu hesitated.

sentences.zh: 會吏盜減諸軍稟食，建怒其眾曰：「招討吏之謀也。」

translations.literal: It happened a clerk stole and reduced the various armies' ration food; Jian angered his masses saying: "The punitive commissioner's clerks plotted it."
translations.idiomatic: When a clerk was caught stealing army rations, Wang Jian roused his troops: "This was the campaign commander's plot."

sentences.zh: 縱士執之，醢食於軍。

translations.literal: He released soldiers to seize him and minced his flesh to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: He let his men seize the man, mince him, and feed the army.

sentences.zh: 昭度大駭，是日授建符節，跳馳出劍門。

translations.literal: Zhaodu was greatly terrified; that day he bestowed Jian credentials and banner, leaped on horse and galloped out Sword Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu was horrified. That same day he handed Wang Jian the commissioner's seal and banner and fled through Sword Gate.

sentences.zh: 建絕棧梯，東道不通。

translations.literal: Jian severed plank roads and ladders; the eastern route was impassable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian cut the plank roads and ladders, blocking the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 因急擊敬瑄，分親騎為十團，所當輒披靡，烽塹相望幾百里，縱諜入城，以搖眾心。

translations.literal: Therefore he urgently struck Jingxuan, divided personal cavalry into ten groups; wherever they met, foes scattered; beacon towers and trenches stretched nearly a hundred li; he released spies into the city to shake popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed the attack on Chen Jingxuan, dividing his personal cavalry into ten squadrons that swept all before them. Beacon fires and trenches stretched for nearly a hundred li. He sent spies into the city to shake morale.

sentences.zh: 建好謂軍中曰：「成都號『花錦城』，玉帛子女，諸兒可自取。」

translations.literal: Jian addressed the army well: "Chengdu is called the Brocade-Flower City—silks, jewels, women and children—you lads may take for yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian rallied the army: "Chengdu is called the Brocade City—silks, jewels, women and children are yours for the taking."

sentences.zh: 謂票將韓武等：「城破，吾與公遞為節度使一日。」

translations.literal: He said to warrant officers Han Wu and others: "When the city falls, you and I shall take turns being military commissioner for a day each."
translations.idiomatic: He told his deputy generals Han Wu and others: "When the city falls, you and I shall each be military commissioner for a day in turn."

sentences.zh: 下聞之，戰愈力。

translations.literal: The troops hearing this fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers heard this and fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 圍凡三歲，城中糧盡，以筒容米，率寸鬻錢二百。

translations.literal: The siege in all three years; inside the city grain was exhausted; they used tubes to hold rice—roughly per inch sold for two hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted three years. When grain inside the city ran out, rice was measured in tubes—about an inch selling for two hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄出家貲給民，募士出剽麥，收其半。

translations.literal: Jingxuan took his family's wealth to give to the people, recruited men to go out and seize wheat, and took half for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan spent his family fortune to feed the people, recruited men to raid for wheat, and kept half the harvest.

sentences.zh: 民亦夜至建壘市鹽，不可禁，吏請殺之。

translations.literal: The people also came by night to Jian's camp to trade for salt; it could not be stopped, and officials asked to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians also slipped by night to Jian's camp to buy salt; nothing could stop them, and officials urged execution.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄曰：「民饑無以恤，使求生可也。」

translations.literal: Jingxuan said, "The people are starving and we have no means to relieve them; let them seek to live—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan said, "The people are starving and we cannot save them all; let them do what they must to survive."

sentences.zh: 人至相暴以相啖，敬瑄不能止，乃行斬、劈二法，亦不為戢。

translations.literal: Men came to such violence that they ate one another; Jingxuan could not stop it and imposed the two punishments of beheading and quartering, yet still there was no quiet.
translations.idiomatic: People turned on one another and cannibalized the dead; Jingxuan could not stop it. He imposed beheading and dismemberment as punishments, yet the horror did not cease.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄自將出犀浦，列二營邀建。

translations.literal: Jingxuan personally led his troops out to Xipu, arrayed two camps, and intercepted Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan led the army out to Xipu himself, set two camps, and blocked Jian's path.

sentences.zh: 建軍偽遁，遇伏，敬瑄敗，建破斜橋、昝街二屯。

translations.literal: Jian's army feigned flight, met an ambush, and Jingxuan was defeated; Jian broke the two garrisons at Xieqiao and Zanjie.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's army pretended to flee, sprang an ambush, and routed Jingxuan; he then overran the garrisons at Xieqiao and Zanjie.

sentences.zh: 明日戰，又破一壁，降其將。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; he broke another wall and received the surrender of its commander.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he fought again, breached another redoubt, and accepted its commander's surrender.

sentences.zh: 建屯七里亭，敬瑄攻之。

translations.literal: Jian encamped at Qili Pavilion; Jingxuan attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian encamped at Qili Pavilion, and Jingxuan attacked.

sentences.zh: 建將張武馳入城，戰子城下，守陴皆噪，不能克。

translations.literal: Jian's general Zhang Wu galloped into the city and fought below the inner wall; the defenders on the ramparts all shouted, and he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's general Zhang Wu charged into the city and fought below the inner gate; the defenders on the walls roared, and he could not break through.

sentences.zh: 張破浣花營，敬瑄諸將或死或降且盡。

translations.literal: Zhang broke the Huanhua camp; Jingxuan's generals were killed or surrendered until nearly all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang overran the Huanhua camp; Jingxuan's generals were killed or surrendered until almost none remained.

sentences.zh: 凡五十戰，敬瑄皆北，乃上表以病丐還京師。

translations.literal: In fifty battles altogether Jingxuan was always defeated; he then memorialized, pleading illness, to beg leave to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After fifty battles Jingxuan had lost every one; he memorialized the throne, citing illness, and begged to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 令孜素服至建軍。

translations.literal: Lingzi went in plain dress to Jian's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi came to Jian's camp dressed in white mourning garb.

sentences.zh: 建入自西門，以張為斬斫使，建徇於軍曰：「與而等累年鬥死，今日如誌。

translations.literal: Jian entered by the west gate, made Zhang executioner, and proclaimed to the army: "I have fought you to the death for years; today my wish is fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Jian entered through the west gate, appointed Zhang chief executioner, and addressed the army: "We have fought one another to the death for years; today that wish is fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 若橫恣有犯者，吾能全之；

translations.literal: If any man acts wildly and commits offenses, I can spare him;
translations.idiomatic: If any of you run wild and break the law, I can still protect you;

sentences.zh: 即為所斬，吾不得救也！」

translations.literal: but if you are beheaded for it, I cannot save you!
translations.idiomatic: but once Zhang executes you, I cannot save you!"

sentences.zh: 軍中肅然。

translations.literal: The army fell silent and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The army fell silent.

sentences.zh: 囚敬瑄、令孜，建自稱留後，表於朝。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Jingxuan and Lingzi; Jian styled himself acting commissioner and memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Jingxuan and Lingzi, declared himself acting commissioner, and memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 詔以建為西川節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jian deputy military commissioner of Xichuan and gave him charge of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Jian deputy military commissioner of Xichuan with full authority over the circuit.

sentences.zh: 建以敬瑄居新津，食其租賦，累表請誅，不報。

translations.literal: Jian kept Jingxuan at Xinjin and lived off his rents and taxes; he repeatedly memorialized asking that Jingxuan be executed, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jian kept Jingxuan at Xinjin and lived off his tax revenues; he memorialized again and again for his execution, but the court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 景福二年，陰令左右告敬瑄、令孜養死士，約楊晟等反，於是斬敬瑄於家。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingfu he secretly had his attendants accuse Jingxuan and Lingzi of keeping death-loyal soldiers and plotting rebellion with Yang Sheng and others; Jingxuan was then beheaded at home.
translations.idiomatic: In 893 he secretly had his men accuse Jingxuan and Lingzi of training diehard troops and plotting rebellion with Yang Sheng; Jingxuan was executed at his residence.

sentences.zh: 初，敬瑄知不免，嘗置藥於帶，至就刑，視帶，藥已亡矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, knowing he could not escape, Jingxuan had kept poison in his belt; when he came to execution he looked at his belt—the poison was already gone.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan had known he could not escape and had kept poison in his belt; at the moment of execution he found the pouch empty—the poison was gone.

sentences.zh: 自是建盡有兩川、黔中地。

translations.literal: From then on Jian held all the lands of the Two Chuan and Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Jian held all of the Two Chuan and Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 李巨川李巨川，字下己，逢吉從曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Juchuan. Li Juchuan, courtesy name Xiaji, was the great-great-grandson of Fengji on the collateral line.
translations.idiomatic: Li Juchuan. Li Juchuan, courtesy name Xiaji, was a collateral descendant of Li Fengji.

sentences.zh: 乾符中舉進士。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 方天下崩騷，乃去京師，河中王重榮辟為掌書記。

translations.literal: Just as the realm was collapsing in turmoil, he left the capital; Wang Chongrong of Hezhong recruited him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire slid into chaos he left the capital; Wang Chongrong of Hezhong took him on as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 重榮討黃巢，書檄奏請日紛沓，須報趣發，皆屬巨川。

translations.literal: When Chongrong campaigned against Huang Chao, proclamations and memorials piled up day by day and urgent replies were needed; all fell to Juchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongrong marched against Huang Chao, proclamations and memorials poured in daily and urgent dispatches had to go out at once—all were Juchuan's work.

sentences.zh: 神安思敏，言輒中理，鄰藩皆驚。

translations.literal: His spirit was calm and his thought keen; his words always hit the mark, and neighboring circuits were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Composed and quick-witted, his words always struck true, and neighboring circuits marveled.

sentences.zh: 會賊走出關，收京師，人言巨川有助力。

translations.literal: When the bandits fled out of the passes and the capital was recovered, people said Juchuan had lent strong aid.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fled beyond the passes and the capital was retaken, people credited Juchuan with a major share of the effort.

sentences.zh: 重榮死於亂，貶為興元參軍，節度使楊守亮喜曰：「天以生遺我邪！」

translations.literal: Chongrong died in the turmoil; Juchuan was demoted to military adjutant at Xingyuan. Military Commissioner Yang Shouliang rejoiced, saying, "Has Heaven left this man alive for me!
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong died in the upheaval; Juchuan was demoted to adjutant at Xingyuan. Commissioner Yang Shouliang exclaimed, "Has Heaven sent this man to me alive!"

sentences.zh: 復管記室。

translations.literal: He again took charge of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He again headed the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 守亮為韓建所禽，巨川械以從，題木葉遺建祈哀。

translations.literal: Shouliang was captured by Han Jian; Juchuan was bound and taken along, and wrote a plea for mercy on a tree leaf and sent it to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouliang was captured by Han Jian, Juchuan was shackled and led away; he wrote a plea on a leaf and sent it to Jian begging for mercy.

sentences.zh: 建動容，因釋縛，置幕府。

translations.literal: Jian was moved, released his bonds, and placed him in the staff office.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was moved, had his bonds cut, and took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 昭宗幸華，建患一州供億不能濟，使巨川傳檄天下，督轉餉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong came to Hua, Jian worried that one prefecture could not meet the supply burden and had Juchuan circulate a proclamation throughout the realm to press for grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong visited Hua, Jian feared one province could not sustain the court; he had Juchuan issue proclamations across the empire to hurry supplies.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在石門，數遣嗣延王、通王將親軍，大選安聖、奉宸、保寧、安化四軍，又置殿後軍，合士二萬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at Shimen, he repeatedly sent the Prince of Siyan and the Prince of Tong to command the personal armies; he greatly selected the four armies An Sheng, Fengchen, Baoning, and Anhua, and also established a Rear Guard Army—altogether twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at Shimen, the emperor had repeatedly sent the princes of Siyan and Tong to lead the imperial guard, reorganized the An Sheng, Fengchen, Baoning, and Anhua corps, and added a Rear Guard—twenty thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 建惡衛兵強，不利己，與巨川謀，即上飛變，告八王欲脅帝幸河中，因請囚十六宅，選嚴師傅督教，盡散麾下兵。

translations.literal: Jian hated the strength of the palace guard, which did not serve his interests; with Juchuan he plotted and at once submitted an urgent report that the eight princes intended to coerce the emperor to go to Hezhong, then asked to imprison the Sixteen Mansions, choose strict tutors to supervise instruction, and disperse all troops under their command.
translations.idiomatic: Jian resented the palace guard's strength and, with Juchuan, filed an urgent report claiming the eight princes meant to force the emperor to Hezhong; he asked to confine the imperial clansmen in the Sixteen Mansions, appoint strict tutors, and disband all their troops.

sentences.zh: 書再上，帝不得已，詔可。

translations.literal: The memorial came again; the emperor had no choice and approved by edict.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial came again; the emperor had no choice and assented.

sentences.zh: 又廢殿後軍，且言「無示天下不廣」。

translations.literal: The Rear Guard Army was also abolished, with the words "let us not show the realm that we are narrow."
translations.idiomatic: The Rear Guard was abolished as well, and he said, "Do not show the realm a lack of breadth."

sentences.zh: 詔留三十人為控鶴排馬官，隸飛龍坊。

translations.literal: An edict left thirty men as Crane-Control horse-ranking officers, attached to the Flying Dragon Ward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict left only thirty Crane-Control horse officers under the Flying Dragon Ward.

sentences.zh: 自是天子爪牙盡矣。

translations.literal: From then on the Son of Heaven's claws and fangs were wholly gone.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor had no armed force of his own.

sentences.zh: 建初懼帝不聽，以兵環宮，請誅定州行營將李筠。

translations.literal: At first Jian feared the emperor would not listen; he surrounded the palace with troops and asked that Li Yun, camp commander of Dingzhou, be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian first feared refusal; he ringed the palace with troops and demanded the execution of Dingzhou camp commander Li Yun.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，斬筠，兵乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor was afraid, beheaded Yun, and only then were the troops withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the emperor had Yun executed, and the troops withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又言：「七國災漢，八王亂晉，永王帥江左謀不軌，吐蕃、朱玫亂，首立宗支搖人望。

translations.literal: He also said, "The seven states brought calamity on Han, the eight princes threw Jin into chaos, Prince Yong led the lower Yangtze in treason, and in the disorders of the Tibetans and Zhu Mei the first move was to set up an imperial clansman to sway men's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: He argued further: "The seven states ruined Han, the eight princes ruined Jin, Prince Yong raised the lower Yangtze in rebellion, and in the Tibetan and Zhu Mei disorders the first step was always to elevate a prince to sway men's hopes.

sentences.zh: 今王室多故，渠可使諸王將命四方，惑征鎮？」

translations.literal: Now the royal house has many troubles—how can we let the princes take commands in every direction and confuse the military commissioners?
translations.idiomatic: The throne is beset with troubles—how can we let princes take commands across the realm and unsettle the commissioners?"

sentences.zh: 於是詔諸王奉使者，悉赴行在。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered all princes serving as envoys to proceed to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered every prince on mission to return to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 巨川日夜導建不臣，乃請立德王為皇太子，文掩其惡。

translations.literal: Day and night Juchuan led Jian in disloyal courses; he asked that Prince De be made heir apparent, his writings covering Jian's wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night Juchuan urged Jian toward treason; he petitioned to make Prince De heir apparent, his prose papering over Jian's crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝還京，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Juchuan was made Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Juchuan was appointed Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 光化初，朱全忠陷河中，將攻潼關，建懼，使巨川往詣軍納款，因言當世利害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua, Zhu Quanzhong took Hezhong and was about to attack Tong Pass; Jian was afraid and sent Juchuan to the army to submit and speak of the advantages and harms of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guanghua era Zhu Quanzhong seized Hezhong and threatened Tong Pass; terrified, Jian sent Juchuan to submit and discuss the balance of power.

sentences.zh: 全忠屬官敬翔以文翰事左右，疑巨川用則全忠待己或衰，乃詭說曰：「巨川誠奇才，顧不利主人，若何？」

translations.literal: Quanzhong's subordinate Jing Xiang handled documents at his side; he suspected that if Juchuan were employed Quanzhong's regard for himself might fade, and craftily said, "Juchuan is truly a rare talent, yet he does not benefit his master—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong's adviser Jing Xiang handled his correspondence; fearing Juchuan would displace him, he whispered, "Juchuan is a genius, but geniuses do not serve their masters well—what then?"

sentences.zh: 是日，全忠殺之。

translations.literal: That same day Quanzhong killed him.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Quanzhong had him killed.
